### 165. Add-on toggles fire without any visible price feedback in the wizard

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking wizard > step 6 > Add-on toggles
- **What breaks:** toggleAddon() updates internal state but the running estimate is only shown on step 7. Users toggling multiple add-ons cannot see the total impact until they advance, undermining the 'see what you are paying for' promise.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a sticky 'Estimated total: $X' bar at the bottom of step 6 that updates live as add-ons toggle. Show the +$N delta as a brief chip animation next to the toggled add-on. Reuses pricebox calculations from step 7.

### 166. Color rows show 'Included' even when user picked a fashion color with no upcharge

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking wizard step 7 > pricebox
- **What breaks:** buildReview() shows 'Included' when colorUp() returns 0 — which is true for natural colors but also for 'Custom' under bold (which has no entry in the upcharge logic beyond a flat 40). The combo 'Two-Tone' / 'Highlights' / 'Peekaboo' rely on combos.find returning a row; if data drifts, the price collapses to 0 silently with 'Included' label.
- **Proposed fix:** Rename the row label by branch: row.colorUpcharge > 0 → '+$N'; row.colorUpcharge === 0 AND color is a natural shade → 'Included'; colorUpcharge === 0 AND color is bold/combo → 'Charge confirmed at chair'. Also make combos.find fallback log a warning so data drift is caught.

### 167. Aftercare banner stays forever after first demo toggle

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Home > Aftercare entry banner (after toggling 'Enter the chair' once)
- **What breaks:** hadVisit flips true the first time toggleChair() runs and never resets. In real life a client gets aftercare for ~1-2 weeks after a visit. Demo state means once the reviewer hits 'Enter the chair' once, the dark 'Thank you for visiting / Open your aftercare' banner permanently anchors Home for the rest of the session, even after they 'rebook' or pretend months have passed. Surface a sunset rule (e.g. 14 days post-install).
- **Proposed fix:** Implement a sunset rule: aftercare entry visible for 14 days after a completed visit, then auto-hides. Use last-completed-visit timestamp (in real product) or last toggleChair-off timestamp (in prototype). Show 'Aftercare guide closes April 28' caption in the banner.

### 168. Live break banner timestamp '2:38' is hardcoded, contradicts appointment

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Home > 'Enter the chair' demo toggle (chairOn=true) > FAB bell + Live banner
- **What breaks:** Upcoming appointment is Today 1:00 PM. Live banner once chair-on says 'Zainab is on a lunch break and will be back around 2:38'. There's no derivation linking those — and 'lunch break' 1h38m into a 5-7 hour Knotless install is unusual. Either compute the break window from the appointment, or pick copy that doesn't tie itself to a specific time.
- **Proposed fix:** Compute break window from appt.time: break starts 90 min into service, lasts 30 min. For 1:00 PM Knotless install, break is 2:30-3:00. Banner now says 'Zainab is on a quick break and will be back around 3:00'. Also tie progress bar to elapsed/total break time, not a 1.2%/s ticker.

### 169. Loading orb uses three accent colors at once

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Style Consultant > Loading screen > .consult-orb (3 dots)
- **What breaks:** The three bouncing dots are clay, ochre, teal — every accent color in the system fighting for attention in one 14px element. Diessou's palette uses these colors for distinct meanings (clay = action, ochre = celebration, teal = care). Blending them in one decorative loader dilutes that vocabulary. A single-color or tonal trio (clay → clay-deep → bone) would feel more like her brand.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the three orb dots to a tonal trio: clay-500, clay-300, bone. Removes the teal and ochre conflict. One semantic family (action), three shades.

### 170. Photo upload says 'up to 2' but no count enforcement or counter

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Book > Wizard step 6 > 'Inspiration photos (up to 2)' label
- **What breaks:** Label asks for up to 2 inspiration photos but the upload tile is a single tap-to-upload stub with no slot counter, no '1 of 2' indicator, and no upper bound. Clients have no way to see how many they've added. Either match the photo-slot grid pattern used in /consultant (3 distinct slots with labels) or drop the '(up to 2)' constraint.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the single upload div with two .pslot tiles matching the consultant pattern. Add a '0/2 added' counter above. Cap at 2. Reuses existing components.

### 171. Hardcoded years and dates will go stale on Diessou's review timeline

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Profile > Profile head ('Member since 2023 · 14 visits') and circle-card ('renews June 12')
- **What breaks:** 'Member since 2023' is a literal string; in two years' time it'll still say 2023 alongside drifted everything else. Circle-card 'renews June 12' has no year. If Diessou opens this in 2027 it still reads 2023/June 12. Demo dates should derive from TODAY (2026-04-14) so the prototype stays believable across review cycles.
- **Proposed fix:** Derive 'Member since' from TODAY - tenure years (e.g. '3 years' → '2023' computed at render). Derive 'Renews' from membershipStartDate + 1 month. Centralize TODAY anchor (2026-04-14) in one constant; every date renders from offsets.

### 172. Toast overlaps the FAB during in-chair state

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Home > Toast (bottom:120px) + FAB bell (bottom:98px) — both visible while in the chair
- **What breaks:** When chairOn=true the FAB shows at bottom:98px (60px diameter, top at ~158px). Toast sits at bottom:120px (height ~44px, top at ~164px). They occupy the same vertical band on the right side. A 'Request sent · a team member will be with you shortly' toast partially covers the bell the user just tapped, which is the exact moment they want visual confirmation the bell is still there.
- **Proposed fix:** When chairOn=true, push the toast position up: toast bottom changes from 120px to 168px. Toast no longer sits in the same vertical band as the FAB. Alternatively, anchor toasts to top-center when a FAB is visible.

### 173. Error copy points user to 'the Book tab' — but Consultant is already in Book

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-results > error state (cerr block)
- **What breaks:** Error copy reads 'You can also browse styles directly in the Book tab' as the recovery path. But the consultant screen lives inside the book route (entered from bk-entry > Start consultation). The instruction is geographically incoherent — there's no clickable Book tab callout in the error card.
- **Proposed fix:** Update error copy to reference 'the full style menu' (which is the bk-cat screen). Add a 'Browse the menu' secondary CTA that calls go('book').
  - *New copy:* "Couldn't reach the consultant. Try again, or browse the full style menu."

### 174. Step 1 auto-advances on tap; step 2 requires Continue — inconsistent flow control

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Book > Wizard step 1 (category) vs Step 2 (style)
- **What breaks:** pickCat() calls showStep(2) immediately, so tapping a category jumps the user forward. pickStyle() does not — the user has to tap a style and then also tap 'Continue'. The same tap-to-pick gesture means different things on adjacent steps with no visible explanation.
- **Proposed fix:** Make step 2 also auto-advance on style tap (pickStyle calls showStep(3) at the end). Remove the Continue button from step 2 entirely. Consistent tap-to-pick behavior across steps 1, 2, 3, 4. Steps 5-6 keep Continue because they have multi-state interactions.

### 175. Bold color swatches show no price; uniform +$40 only revealed at review

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Book > Wizard step 5 > Bold and fashion swatches (Burgundy, Red, Blonde, Copper, Purple, Blue, Pink, Custom)
- **What breaks:** All eight bold-color swatches add $40 (colorPrices.bold=40 / colorUp() returns 40 for any bold pick). The swatch itself shows only the color and name — no '+$40' badge. The client doesn't learn there's an upcharge until Step 7 review and may be surprised.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a '+$40' badge to the top-right of each bold/fashion swatch. Add a '+$80' badge to combo cards. Natural swatches have no badge. Pricing visible at decision time.

### 176. Loading-message interval leaks if user navigates away mid-consult

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-loading screen > navigating away during fetch
- **What breaks:** runConsult() spins up setInterval(cyc) that flips loadingMsg every 1.4s. It's only cleared inside the try/catch when the fetch resolves. If the user navigates away (taps a nav tab, hits the chair toggle, etc.) before the response, cyc keeps writing textContent to a hidden element forever.
- **Proposed fix:** Store the interval ID in a module-scope variable. Clear it in cancelConsult(), in cs-loading's beforeUnmount, and in any go() call from cs-loading. Also abort the AbortController for the in-flight fetch.

### 177. Dead no-op forEach in toggleWish suggests cross-carousel sync was abandoned

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Home > toggleWish() handler (Featured + Wishlist carousels)
- **What breaks:** toggleWish ends with `document.querySelectorAll('.style-card .heart').forEach(h=>{});` — an empty arrow body. It's clearly a leftover stub of the intended Featured-carousel heart sync, never completed. Confirms #48 (Featured doesn't re-render) was a known TODO that never landed.
- **Proposed fix:** Fill in the forEach body with the refreshHearts() logic from flag #35. Or replace the forEach entirely with a single refreshHearts() call after state mutation.

### 178. Tapping a filled photo slot re-opens the file picker instead of previewing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-photos > filled slot tap
- **What breaks:** Each pslot is a label wrapping the file input. Once filled, tapping anywhere on the slot (including the preview image) triggers the file picker again. There is no 'View larger', 'Replace', or 'Remove' menu — the only behavior is silently overwriting with a fresh upload.
- **Proposed fix:** Filled slots show a tap-menu: Preview large / Replace / Remove. Implement as a small bottom-sheet (reuse sheet pattern) triggered on filled-slot tap. The bare label-click-opens-picker behavior only fires on empty slots.

### 179. Color row hardcodes 'Natural Black' fallback when colorName missing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Book > Wizard step 7 (review) > pricebox > 'Color · Natural Black' / 'Color · <name>' row
- **What breaks:** buildReview prints `Color · ${wiz.colorName||'Natural Black'}`. Step-5 validation does prevent advancing without a color, so the fallback should never display — but if validation is ever loosened or skipped via dev tools, the review will lie that the user chose Natural Black when they chose nothing.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the fallback string. If wiz.colorName is missing, throw a validation error blocking step 7 entry. Step 5 validation already requires a selection; this makes the contract explicit.

### 180. Empty wish preview still renders the section header

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Home > 'Your wishlist' carousel section-label (when wishlist is empty)
- **What breaks:** When wishlist=[], renderWishPreview() injects placeholder text into #wishPreview but the parent .section-label 'Your wishlist View all' still shows above it. Result: an empty hscroll under a 'View all' link that, when tapped, takes you to an empty Wishlist screen. The section should hide when there is nothing saved.
- **Proposed fix:** When wishlist.length === 0, hide the entire 'Your wishlist' section on Home (header + 'View all' + carousel). Only show when ≥1 item saved. Section reappears on first save.

### 181. Spotlight card's name and 'star this month' text are not selectable as drill-in

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Home > Spotlight ('Employee of the Month' Aminata D.) — entire card
- **What breaks:** The whole .spotlight is a single onclick='go("book")'. There's no per-element handler that takes 'Aminata D.' to her stylist profile or portfolio — separate from #60, the click target is genuinely indivisible, so even copy ('Book with our star stylist') falsely implies more.
- **Proposed fix:** Split the spotlight into two distinct tap targets: avatar+name → go('sub-stylist','aminata-d'); 'Book with our star stylist' button → startBookingWithStylist('aminata-d'). Use stopPropagation to separate targets.

### 182. Member badge in Profile head is a plain span — not tappable into membership detail

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Profile > Profile head > 'Jolieden Circle member' badge
- **What breaks:** The badge .member-tag with the star icon is a visual indicator with no onclick. Tapping it should jump to the Circle card / 'Your membership' section below or to a membership-details screen, but it does nothing. The natural drill-in from a 'Member' label is broken.
- **Proposed fix:** Wire the .member-tag onclick to scroll to the 'Your membership' section on Profile (smooth scroll). On membership detail screens (flag #17), tapping the badge from elsewhere opens sub-membership directly.

### 183. No sign-out, no switch-account, no developer 'Reset prototype' affordance

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Phone notch area (top of every screen) and Profile screen
- **What breaks:** Beyond #18 (no sign-out in Profile), there is no surface anywhere — notch, header, Account block, or modal — to reset the prototype, switch personas, or sign out. For demo purposes this also means no way to re-seed wishlist/answers without a hard browser refresh.
- **Proposed fix:** Add Sign out in Account (flag #18). Behind ?demo=1, add 'Reset prototype' and 'Switch persona' rows at the bottom of Profile that re-seed state. These are stripped from production.

### 184. Two stylists share the 'A' initial avatar with no differentiator

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Profile > Meet our stylists > avatar initials
- **What breaks:** Aminata D. and Awa J. both render with a circular 'A' tile in the same gradient, side-by-side in the directory. A user scanning by avatar cannot distinguish them and the names underneath do the entire job alone.
- **Proposed fix:** Render initials from first + last name when first names start with the same letter ('AD' for Aminata D., 'AJ' for Awa J.). Also use a different gradient seed per stylist (hash from slug) so the colors differ subtly.

### 185. Stylist ratings show '★ 4.9' with no scale

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Profile > Meet our stylists > rating value
- **What breaks:** Each stylist row reads '★ 4.9 rating' with no 'out of 5'. A first-time user has no anchor for whether 4.6 is good or bad and the precision implies more data than the prototype actually models.
- **Proposed fix:** Append '/ 5' to every rating display and show review count next to it. On the stylist-detail screen, show a reviews list.
  - *New copy:* "4.9 / 5 · 412 reviews"

### 186. Aftercare hero hardcodes the persona name 'Amara'

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Aftercare > Hero > '<em>Amara</em>' display headline
- **What breaks:** The hero reads 'Thank you, Amara' as static HTML. If the user is on the profile screen labelled 'Amara N.' it works, but it is not bound to the same source — any future persona swap in Profile would not propagate, and the headline is structurally independent of the rest of the personalisation system.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the static HTML with a render-time binding from the central user state (e.g. user.firstName). Same source as Profile head and Home greeting.

### 187. Legal disclaimer overlay crops into name/price below

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Home > Featured styles + Wishlist preview > .dis legal overlay
- **What breaks:** Every style photo carries a .dis overlay with 'Results may vary. For inspiration only.' that occupies the bottom 18px of the 180px image. The style name (.nm) and price (.pr) sit immediately below the photo with only 9px breathing room, making the card feel cramped and the overlay feel like it bleeds into the metadata.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the in-photo .dis overlay (flag #79 fix). Move disclaimer to a single footer line under the carousel. Recovers 18px of breathing room above the name/price.

### 188. Recommendation tags use teal color outside the client palette

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-results > rec-card .rtags
- **What breaks:** The .rtag chips on Claude's recommendation cards render with background rgba(78,126,118,.13) and color #3c655d — a teal that's used elsewhere only as an aftercare accent. On the client surface (cream/clay/ochre), the teal tags pop as a fourth accent color with no other anchor on the screen.
- **Proposed fix:** Recolor .rtag chips to use --clay-100 background with --clay-700 text (warm tones matching the rest of the client surface). Reserve teal for aftercare context only.

### 189. Size & Length 'Included' pricing rows show no $0 differentiation

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking wizard > step 3 (Size) > 'Large / Jumbo' option / step 4 (Length) > 'Shoulder' option
- **What breaks:** Sizes/lengths with up=0 (Medium, Large/Jumbo, Shoulder) show the label 'Included' identical to base-included; client cannot tell which option is the salon-default vs which actually costs extra without tapping each.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace 'Included' with 'Standard' for the salon-default options (Medium size, Shoulder length). Options that cost extra show '+$N'. Options that are smaller-than-default could show 'Standard' too. Eliminates ambiguity between 'no upcharge' and 'salon default'.
  - *New copy:* "Standard / +$N"

### 190. Single-select questions allow tapping the same answer to clear it

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-q (questionnaire) > question option rows (.copt)
- **What breaks:** pickAnswer for single-select questions has no else branch — tapping the currently-selected option re-assigns the same value with no visual change but does not lock the answer. Users get no feedback that the option is already chosen, just a silent re-render.
- **Proposed fix:** Make single-select truly single: tapping the currently-selected option does nothing (no re-render, no side effect). Selected option stays selected until a different one is tapped. Add a haptic blip if available.

### 191. Each question re-renders its own Continue button, causing layout flicker

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-q > 'Next' / 'Continue' button (inside cQuestionHost)
- **What breaks:** renderQuestion() rebuilds the entire question host (including the button) every tap on a multi-select. The button visibly re-renders on every selection change, which on slower devices flashes the CTA.
- **Proposed fix:** Render the Continue button once outside renderQuestion() (in the wizard chrome, like the Booking wizard's wizNext). Updates its enabled/disabled state on each selection without rerendering.

### 192. Duration estimate ignores add-ons individually — flat +1 hour cap

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking wizard step 7 (review) > Estimated duration card
- **What breaks:** buildReview adds +1 hour to the high end only if wiz.addons.length > 0, regardless of how many add-ons (1 vs 3). A client adding curly ends + beads + creative parts gets the same time estimate as adding one.
- **Proposed fix:** Refactor to per-addon duration deltas: each addon row defines its own duration impact (curly ends +30 min, beads +20 min, creative parts +45 min). Sum them. Total duration estimate now accurate to selected add-ons.

### 193. Takedown reminder appears even before chairOn has ever fired

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Care reminder card > 'Time for a takedown'
- **What breaks:** The takedown care reminder is hardcoded into the home page markup with no conditional gating — it renders on a fresh load whether or not the user has any history of needing one.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag #75: gate the reminder card on last-install-date being ≥6 weeks ago AND no upcoming install in the next 7 days. On a fresh prototype load (no history), suppress the reminder.

### 194. Points tier scale labels overflow horizontally when the next tier name is long

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Journey > points card (pts-card)
- **What breaks:** pts-scale spans use position:absolute with left:0% and left:100%, transform:translateX(-50%). 'Diamond 3,001' at left:100% will visibly clip off the right edge of the card on a 350px-wide phone.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag #47: anchor labels to card edges with left:0/right:0 + text-align rather than 100% + translate. Eliminates clipping on narrow phones.

### 195. Video sheet's player background only sets one gradient — does not clear the previous one when sheet reopens for a different video

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Aftercare > video sheet > .ac-player (paid video gradient)
- **What breaks:** openAcVideo overrides the player background, so re-opening for video 1 after viewing video 5 works. But between renders, the steps and title swap instantly — no transition — so when reopening for a different video, the previous video's gradient briefly flashes before being replaced.
- **Proposed fix:** On openAcVideo, reset the player background to a neutral state first, then apply the new gradient with a 200ms fade transition. Eliminates the cross-fade flash.

### 196. Persona name 'Amara' is hardcoded in five separate places across the app

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Profile > Profile head (Amara N.) and rest of app
- **What breaks:** Amara N. appears in Profile head, Home greeting display, Aftercare hero, check-in sheet QR caption, and aftercare hero email body. There is no central persona binding; any rename requires hand-editing every occurrence. Brittle for the prototype's demo persona swap.
- **Proposed fix:** Centralize in a single USER constant (firstName, lastName, etc.). Every surface reads from USER. Persona swap (gated by ?demo=1 or a Profile switcher) updates all five surfaces at once.

### 197. Multi-select allows selecting all 6 options with no maximum enforcement

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Style Consultant > Question 5 (multi-select 'What look are you drawn to?') > options
- **What breaks:** pickAnswer's multi branch toggles selections in/out without caps. A client could select all 6 mood options, providing no useful signal to the AI — the model then has to disambiguate between 'natural + bold + protective' which contradict each other.
- **Proposed fix:** Cap multi-select at 3 selections (per flag #122). Disable additional taps with greyed styling and inline 'You've picked 3' caption. Matches both UX clarity and the model's signal quality.

### 198. Dead code in toggleWish forEach over .style-card .heart with empty body

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Style card heart > toggleWish > document.querySelectorAll forEach empty
- **What breaks:** toggleWish ends with: document.querySelectorAll('.style-card .heart').forEach(h=>{}); — a no-op iteration. The author started writing cross-carousel sync but left the body empty. Hearts on the Home featured carousel will not visually reflect changes made on the Wishlist screen.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the dead forEach with the refreshHearts() implementation from flag #35. Tag every heart with data-style attribute. Sync across Featured, Wishlist preview, Wishlist grid, and rec-cards.

### 199. Combo options re-use pickColor for radio behavior but also have selection visual artifact

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking wizard > Step 5 > Combinations > combo .opt rows like 'Ombré'
- **What breaks:** pickColor clears all .swatch and #comboOpts .opt sel classes, then adds sel to the clicked element. But the natural/bold swatches use .swatch.sel CSS, while combos use .opt.sel CSS — both inherit different ring styling, so when switching from a combo back to a swatch, the previously-selected combo briefly shows a faded ring during the swap.
- **Proposed fix:** Unify selection styling: use a single .selected class on both .swatch and .opt with a single ring spec (--clay-500 2px). Clear all .selected before applying new one. No more dual-class swap artifact.

### 200. Live banner copy directs to the bell, but the bell is bottom:98px (above nav) while banner is in scroll area

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Live banner > 'Tap the bell anytime' copy + FAB bell position
- **What breaks:** When the user scrolls down on Home in chair mode, the banner scrolls away while the FAB stays fixed — the copy says 'tap the bell' but the bell is no longer adjacent to or referenced by anything contextual.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the live banner sticky (position: sticky; top: 0) so the bell instruction stays adjacent to the FAB always. Or move the bell instruction onto the FAB itself as a one-time tooltip.

### 201. Consultant intro's Back button is labeled 'Back' but it's actually 'go to Book screen'

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Style Consultant > intro screen > 'Back' button
- **What breaks:** The .btn ghost 'Back' button on cs-intro calls go('book') which is the Book entry, not 'back to where the user came from'. A user who arrived via a deep link or from somewhere else gets dumped to Book rather than the actual previous screen.

### 202. 'Reschedule locks 48 hours before' caption contradicts Manage button toast

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking wizard step 7 (review) > deposit caption
- **What breaks:** Step 7's caption says reschedule locks 48 hrs before. Manage button on home shows the same toast. But there is no actual reschedule UI anywhere — the 48-hour rule is shown twice and applied zero times.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag #6 creating a real Manage sheet, the 48-hour rule is enforced visually: Reschedule button is disabled within 48 hrs of the appointment, with the caption shown inline. Single source of policy truth.

### 203. Video sheet title renders twice when read mode rendered into video sheet

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** openAcVideo populates #acSteps with the .ac-read partial, but the .ac-read partial uses .act for its own title. Since openAcVideo also sets #acTitle (.sheet-h) separately, the title appears both as 'Washing your braids' header AND would appear inside the .ac-read partial — except the openAcVideo HTML strips it, but it leaves the inconsistent style legacy.

### 204. Filled photo slot still shows the upload camera icon behind the photo

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** On filled slots, the camera SVG is still in the DOM behind the img element. The .pl3 label is also still there. Both are hidden by the absolutely-positioned img (z-index implicit) but on iOS, the underlying touch target priority can mean taps register on the input rather than the visible photo.
- **Proposed fix:** On fill, remove the camera SVG + 'Add photo' label from the DOM (not just visually hidden). Replace with the img + the new X remove control (from flag #51). Touch targets are explicit and non-overlapping.

### 205. Duration estimate flashes 5-7h on first paint then recalculates

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Book > Wizard step 7 > pricebox > duration row ('5 to 7 hours' static)
- **What breaks:** The HTML hardcodes 'Estimated duration: 5 to 7 hours' but buildReview() recomputes to '4 to 6 hours' for the default (Medium/Shoulder/no addons). On step 7 entry the user briefly sees 5-7 then it changes — and only changes when buildReview runs, which is fine, but the initial mismatch reads as a glitch.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the hardcoded '5 to 7 hours' from the HTML. Render the duration row only after buildReview computes — initial state shows '—' or a small skeleton, then replaces with the computed value. No flash.

### 206. Spotlight has no relationship to the Employee-of-the-Month listing logic

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Spotlight ('Aminata D.') and Profile > Meet our stylists (also Aminata D. listed as Master Influencer)
- **What breaks:** Aminata is highlighted as 'Employee of the Month' on Home but on Profile she's just one of four stylists with no badge. The two surfaces never reconcile — a user clicking from Profile sees no indication this stylist is the featured one.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 'Stylist in the spotlight' badge (gold pill) on Aminata's row in the Meet our stylists directory. Drives off the same employeeOfMonth state. Single source of truth, consistent indicator.

### 207. Lunch break copy says 'around 2:38' but progress bar fills in under a minute

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Live banner > 'will be back around 2:38' + progress bar (1.2% per second)
- **What breaks:** Setting `w=Math.min(100,w+1.2)` per second means the bar goes from 35% to 100% in 54 seconds — yet the copy implies the break ends at a clock time. There's no mapping between progress and the stated 2:38 return.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag #116/#138: bind progress bar to (elapsed / breakDuration) so the bar matches the stated end time. For prototype demo, add a ?fastBreak=1 query param to speed it up if needed.

### 208. Book another immediately re-enters solo wizard, discarding group context if user was in a group flow

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Book > bk-done > 'Book another' button
- **What breaks:** After confirming a group booking, the bk-done screen shows 'Book another' which calls wizStart(false) — silently downgrading to a solo wizard with no warning, even if the prior confirmation was a group.
- **Proposed fix:** On bk-done, 'Book another' inherits the group flag from the previous booking. If wiz.group=true, the new wizard also starts in group mode (wizStart(true)). Optionally show 'Book another for the group' as the button label.

### 209. VIP toggle row's chevron-shaped slot is filled by a toggle, breaking visual rhythm

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Profile > Account > VIP early access toggle (pf-link contains a .tog)
- **What breaks:** Every other Account row ends with a chevron-right; the VIP row substitutes a toggle in the same slot. The grouping reads inconsistent and an eye scanning down the list misses the affordance change (already #130 noted mixing, but here specifically the VIP row breaks the otherwise-uniform chevron column).
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the toggle in the same chevron-slot styling as other rows: position it where the chevron sits, same padding. Or alternatively, group toggles into a 'Preferences' subsection below chevron rows. Recommended: keep VIP as a toggle but visually align it to the chevron column position.

### 210. Skip-photos path still tells the AI 'The client did not upload photos' but the AI's response style implies photo analysis

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Style Consultant > cs-photos > skip flow and runConsult (no photos uploaded)
- **What breaks:** The prompt template includes 'Look at them for density, length, edge health, and breakage' only when photos exist, but the system prompt frames the consultant around hair-health reading. Without photos the assistant has no signal for fragile edges except the questionnaire, yet the care note can still claim photo-based insight.
- **Proposed fix:** Branch the system prompt: when photos present, include 'Look at the uploaded photos for density…' instructions; when absent, omit photo-related instructions and rely on questionnaire. Response style follows accordingly.

### 211. Care reminder and Aftercare entry duplicate each other thematically

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > 'Care reminder' section-label appearing always vs. Aftercare section appearing only after the chair toggle
- **What breaks:** Both surface 'how to take care of your hair right now' but use different visual systems (warm cream card vs. dark espresso banner) and different copy. After a service both show simultaneously, which is redundant — the user can't tell if Aftercare replaces Care reminder or supplements it.
- **Proposed fix:** Single 'Hair care' section on Home that switches based on context: post-visit (≤14 days since install) → Aftercare entry; mid-cycle (3-5 weeks in) → Maintenance reminder; end-of-cycle (≥6 weeks in) → Takedown reminder. One module, three states.

### 212. No visual signal in stylist directory that one of them is the spotlighted EOM

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Profile > Meet our stylists > Aminata D. row (also Employee of the Month on Home)
- **What breaks:** Home spotlights Aminata as Employee of the Month, but the Profile stylist directory shows her as a plain row identical to the other three. Tapping the spotlight should arguably land on her profile, but at minimum the directory should flag her with the same crown/star indicator.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag #194: add a gold 'Stylist in the spotlight' pill on Aminata's row in the directory. Tappable like the rest of the row.

### 213. User name 'Amara' is repeated everywhere but Profile shows last initial as 'N.' with no surface explaining who/why

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > Avatar circle ('A') + Aftercare hero ('Thank you, Amara') + Profile > 'Amara N.'
- **What breaks:** Last name 'N.' is used in Profile, in the check-in card ('Amara N. · Knotless Box · 1:00 PM'), but the home greeting and aftercare just say 'Amara'. There's no consistency rule — a casual reader can't tell what the user's actual last name is or whether 'N.' is intentional anonymization.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize on full last name in formal surfaces (Profile head, check-in card) and first name in casual surfaces (Home greeting, aftercare hero). Add a 'Display name' setting in the editable Profile (flag #76 / #90) so users control this.

### 214. Card on file 'Visa ending 4242 · Apple Pay' implies both, but only one is the default

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Profile > Account block (Oopsie, Payment, Notifications, VIP)
- **What breaks:** The description 'Visa ending 4242 · Apple Pay' bundles two payment methods on a row whose only affordance is a chevron-only toast. The user can't tell which is the default for the 50% deposit charged at booking confirm.
- **Proposed fix:** Clarify the default in the row label. The new sub-payment screen (flag #15) lets users change which is the default; the Account row reflects the current setting.
  - *New copy:* "Visa · 4242 (default) · Apple Pay available"

### 215. 'View all' on Wishlist row shows after the empty-state line, looking redundant

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Home > 'Your wishlist' section-label > 'View all' link (when wishlist preview is empty)
- **What breaks:** When wishlist is empty, renderWishPreview shows 'Tap the heart on any style to save it.' inline, but the section-label still has 'View all' to the right — sending the user to a screen that just says 'Nothing saved yet'. Two empty-state messages on the same flow.
- **Proposed fix:** Hide the entire Wishlist section on Home when empty (flag #110). No section header, no View all, no carousel. Section reappears on first save.

---

## Station Kiosk  `kiosk`

*Per-chair tablet. Shows current client, service progress, station bell, idle/active states.*

**183 findings · 182 fixes**

### 1. Service name h2 is hardcoded text, identical regardless of which client signs in

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Static 'Knotless Box Braids' h2
- **What breaks:** Every client at this station, no matter their booked service, sees 'Knotless Box Braids' — the tracker has no data source, just a literal string.
- **Proposed fix:** Source the H2 from a booking object: kiosk reads `bookings[stationId]` (which would come from the operator app via API in production). For the prototype, use a fixture keyed by URL param: `?service=knotless-box-braids`.
  - *Route target:* Operator Floor Command owns booking data; Kiosk subscribes via shared store.

### 2. Stylist name and title are hardcoded — never reflect actual assigned stylist

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stylist row (Zainab O. hardcoded)
- **What breaks:** Station 14 always shows Zainab O. as the stylist regardless of the day's schedule — if a different stylist is working this chair, the kiosk lies.
- **Proposed fix:** Source stylist from the same booking object as flag 137. `bookings[stationId].stylist` provides name, title, avatar, slug. Resolve via the personas registry.
  - *Route target:* Operator Floor Command owns stylist assignment.

### 3. No navigation to any other surface in the artifact

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Global (every screen)
- **What breaks:** The kiosk has no links to the Client Companion App, Stylist App, Owner Admin, Manager Admin, Catalog Shoot, or Public Booking. A reviewer exploring the prototype reaches this surface and has no way out except closing the tab — there is no surface picker, no Jolieden wordmark link, no footer.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a fixed top-right "Surface" pill (mirroring the station-tag treatment, opposite corner) that opens a slide-down sheet listing all six neighbor surfaces (Client Companion, Stylist App, Owner Admin, Manager Admin, Catalog Shoot, Public Booking). Behind a 3-tap gesture on the JOLIEDEN wordmark so real clients never see it but reviewers always can.
  - *Route target:* Surface picker sheet (new, shared component reused on every artifact surface)

### 4. Prominent bell looks like a call-staff button but is decorative

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Bell icon (top-right of assistance panel)
- **What breaks:** The large bell icon next to 'Need something? Tap and a team member comes to you' invites tapping — it has a hover treatment and an onclick. But the handler (ringBell) only plays a chime and swings the bell visually; it does NOT send any request or open the confirm modal. A nervous client who taps the bell thinking they have summoned staff will be ignored. Only the six tiles below actually summon anyone.
- **Proposed fix:** Repurpose the bell into a real "Call my stylist" button that fires sendRequest with a 7th request type ("Stylist, when you have a sec"). Update ringBell() to also open the confirm modal with copy "We let Zainab know — she'll be with you when she finishes this section."
  - *New copy:* "Confirm title: \"On its way\" → modal body: \"Zainab knows you'd like her. She'll wrap this section and check in.\""

### 5. Time remaining never decrements while bar fills

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Progress text ('About 2 hr 10 left')
- **What breaks:** The progress bar advances (0.4% per second) but the 'About 2 hr 10 left' text is hardcoded in markup and never updates. A client watching for more than a minute sees the bar move while the time stays frozen at 2:10, which destroys trust in the whole tracker. The two displays should advance together.
- **Proposed fix:** In startProgress, compute remaining minutes from progPct against a serviceTotalMinutes constant (default 240 for braids) and update #progText each tick: `About Xh Ymin left` until <60, then `About Y min left`, then `Finishing touches`, then current 'All done' copy.
  - *New copy:* "Format: \"About 2h 10 left\" → \"About 1h 47 left\" → \"About 38 min left\" → \"Finishing touches\" → \"All done, you look beautiful\""

### 6. Stylist title reads as nonsensical AI copy

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Stylist card ('Senior Braiding Influencer')
- **What breaks:** Zainab O. is labeled 'Senior Braiding Influencer.' That title doesn't exist at a hair salon, doesn't match Diéssou's voice, and confuses the client about who is doing their hair. Should be 'Senior Braider' or 'Senior Stylist.' Also: 'Zainab O.' isn't in the canonical cast (Oumou, Fatou, Dieynaba) — undercuts brand consistency across surfaces.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace hardcoded stylist with canonical cast member Oumou D. (the Senior Braider per CLAUDE.md cast). Update stylist row to render Oumou D., title "Senior Braider", avatar initial "O". Source from a stylists object keyed by station number for future flexibility.
  - *New copy:* "Name: \"Oumou D.\" / Title: \"Senior Braider\""

### 7. Single tap fires request with no cancel or undo

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Assistance grid > Request cards (Water, Bathroom Break, etc.)
- **What breaks:** Tapping any of the six cards immediately rings the bell, plays the chime, and posts the request to staff. A capped client with a stylist working over them is prone to accidental brushes against the tablet (jewelry, sleeve, leaning back). There is no Cancel button in the confirmation modal — only 'Got it.' Stylists will get pinged for ghost requests with no way for the client to retract.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 5-second "Undo" affordance: after sendRequest, the confirm modal shows a Cancel button (outline) alongside Got it. Cancel posts a cancellation event. After 5s the Cancel button fades out and only Got it remains.
  - *New copy:* "Outline button: \"Cancel — I tapped by mistake\" / Primary button: \"Got it\""

### 8. Typing two full names defeats the chair-side context

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Sign-in screen (name fields + Enter button)
- **What breaks:** The sub-copy already says 'Your stylist already has your booking, this is just so we can take care of you.' If that's true, why does the client need to type their first AND last name into a serif text field on a tablet while they're already capped and sat in the chair? The on-screen keyboard will cover the Enter button, autofocus fires the keyboard before they're ready, and clients with braiding tools or fresh tips can't type cleanly. A simple 'Tap to begin' or staff-assisted launch would respect the form factor.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the two-input sign-in with a single full-width "Tap to begin" button (clay, 80vw). One tap signs in using the stylist's pre-loaded booking client name. Add a small text link below "Not [Name]? Let staff know" that opens a confirm with options to verify identity with staff.
  - *New copy:* "H1: \"Welcome to your chair, [name].\" / Button: \"Tap to begin\" / Link: \"Not [name]? Let us know.\""

### 9. Demo toggles visible to real clients in production layout

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Demo controls (bottom-right buttons)
- **What breaks:** 'Demo: stylist on break' and 'Reset' sit at the bottom-right corner at 50% opacity — visible to any client. On a deployed kiosk this would let any client toggle a 'stylist on break' overlay or reset the session mid-visit. Should be hidden behind a long-press, key sequence, or admin gesture, not dimmed-but-tappable.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as flag 10: hide .demo by default, reveal via long-press on the JOLIEDEN wordmark or ?demo=1. Add a persistent "PROTOTYPE" ribbon when revealed so testers know they're in demo mode.

### 10. Progress interval never clears when client signs out mid-service

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > Interval timer
- **What breaks:** startProgress sets progInt but endSession does not clear it. If a user signs out and then a new user signs in, startProgress is called again creating a second interval — progPct ticks twice as fast, and after multiple cycles the kiosk's progress bar accelerates incorrectly.
- **Proposed fix:** In endSession, call `clearInterval(progInt); progInt=null;` and `clearInterval(breakInt); breakInt=null;` before resetting fields. Add the same to the celebration-overlay exit.

### 11. Progress percentage state persists across sign-out / sign-in

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > 'About 2 hr 10 left'
- **What breaks:** progPct is a module-level let that is never reset to 46 on endSession. A second client signing in inherits the previous client's progress — they sit down to a chair that says 'About 2 hr 10 left' when their own service hasn't started.
- **Proposed fix:** In endSession, reset `progPct = 0` (or to a per-client start value pulled from the booking). On enterKiosk, restart progress from the appropriate baseline.

### 12. cap() function destroys culturally-styled names

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Name fields (First name, Last name)
- **What breaks:** The greeting uses cap(firstName) which forces first-letter-uppercase + lowercase-everything-else. Real client names like 'MacKenzie', 'DeShawn', 'O'Brien', 'LaTanya', 'McKenna' get flattened to 'Mackenzie', 'Deshawn', 'O'brien' — a particularly tone-deaf failure for a Black-clientele salon where identity-marked names matter.
- **Proposed fix:** Delete the cap() helper. Display the client's name verbatim as typed (after the trim from flag 27). For typing safety, optionally show a caption "Type your name the way you write it — we won't change it." beneath the first-name input.
  - *New copy:* "Caption beneath inputs: \"Type your name the way you write it.\""

### 13. Same green checkmark for hospitality and discomfort requests

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Checkmark icon
- **What breaks:** Tapping 'Too Tight or Discomfort' shows the identical cheery green checkmark used for 'Water on its way' and 'A treat is coming'. A pain/safety concern receives the same celebratory affordance as a snack request — tonally wrong.
- **Proposed fix:** Branch the confirm icon by request category. Discomfort uses a hand/touch glyph in --teal (concerned, not celebratory). Phone Charger uses a battery glyph. Default for hospitality requests stays as the checkmark. Wire via a icon-key on each request object.

### 14. No idle timeout or screensaver between clients

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Global > Idle/screensaver behavior
- **What breaks:** A kiosk left signed-in after a client leaves still shows their first name in the greeting. The next person to sit down (or a passing client) sees 'Welcome, Amara' until someone manually signs out. No auto-revert to sign-in, no screen dim.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an idle timer (15 min no interaction) that fades the kiosk to a 'Resting' screen showing the JOLIEDEN wordmark + Station number + "Tap anywhere to begin." After 30 min, full endSession. Reset on any tap or progress event.

### 15. Request cards are not keyboard or screen-reader reachable

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance request cards
- **What breaks:** All six .areq cards use onclick on a plain div with no role='button', tabindex, or aria-label. A client using VoiceOver/TalkBack or a paired keyboard cannot request water, translation, or report discomfort.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert .areq divs to <button> elements (or add role='button', tabindex='0', keydown Enter/Space handlers). Add aria-label "Request water" etc. derived from the card title.

### 16. Single-name clients cannot sign in

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Required First + Last name
- **What breaks:** The Enter button stays disabled unless both fields contain at least one character. Clients who go by a single name (common in some West African and diaspora naming) — or who simply prefer to enter just a first name on a kiosk — are locked out with no override.
- **Proposed fix:** With the "Tap to begin" simplification from flag 14, this disappears. If keeping the input form: make last name optional. Enter button enables when first name has ≥2 valid characters. Label last name as "Last name (optional)".

### 17. UI is English-only, including the translate request itself

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Translate Please card > Language list (English/French/Spanish)
- **What breaks:** The 'Translate Please' card and confirmation are written in English. A non-English-speaking client has to read English copy ('Help in your language, English, French, or Spanish') to discover that translation help is available. Card copy or icon should be self-evident across languages.
- **Proposed fix:** On the Translate Please card, render the title in all six supported languages as a small carousel/marquee cycling every 2.5s ("Help in your language / Aide dans votre langue / Sa lakk wi nga dégg" etc). The icon should be a universal speech-bubble + globe glyph that needs no language.

### 18. Charger request confirms before user picks iPhone or Android

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Phone Charger card
- **What breaks:** Tile copy says 'just tell us which kind' and confirm says 'Let us know iPhone or Android' — but the confirm fires immediately with no follow-up step to collect the choice. Staff arrives without knowing which charger to bring.
- **Proposed fix:** Tapping the Charger card opens a small follow-up sheet with two large buttons: "iPhone" / "USB-C (Android)". Only after pick does the confirm fire with the chosen type appended.
  - *New copy:* "Sheet title: \"Which charger?\" / Buttons: \"iPhone\" · \"USB-C\" / Confirm body: \"USB-C charger coming to Station 14.\""

### 19. No secondary 'Cancel' or 'Wrong button' option in confirm modal

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > 'Got it' is the only action
- **What breaks:** After a request is submitted, the modal shows only 'Got it' which acknowledges, not cancels. A client who fat-fingered the wrong tile has no way to recall the request — staff is already being summoned.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 13 — add a Cancel button alongside Got it for the 5-second undo window.

### 20. Discomfort confirm says stylist will check in — but stylist is on break

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > 'Too Tight or Discomfort' card during break
- **What breaks:** Confirm message hardcodes 'Your stylist will check in and adjust right away'. If the client taps this while the break overlay is showing, the message contradicts the visible break state. No handling for break-state messaging.
- **Proposed fix:** Branch the discomfort confirm copy on onBreak. During break: "Pause — we'll get someone over to help right now." Always route discomfort to whoever is nearest, not just the assigned stylist.
  - *New copy:* "During break: \"Pause — we'll get someone over to help right now.\""

### 21. Greeting uses only first name despite collecting last name

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > 'Welcome, Amara' (first name only)
- **What breaks:** Sign-in requires first AND last name (won't enable Enter without both) but the greeting only ever uses the first name. The last name capture is functionally wasted - it serves no displayed purpose, no lookup, no record. Asks the client for data the system throws away.
- **Proposed fix:** Either use the last name in the greeting ("Welcome, Amara Diop") on first sign-in then collapse to first name afterward, OR drop the last name field entirely per flag 14's "Tap to begin" pattern. Recommended: drop the last name field.

### 22. Phone Charger icon is identical silhouette to Bathroom Break

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Phone Charger card icon
- **What breaks:** Both Bathroom Break and Phone Charger use a rounded rectangle as their primary shape ('rect x=5/7 ... rx=2'). At a glance the two cards' icons are nearly indistinguishable, defeating the icon-first scannability the grid layout depends on.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace with a Lucide 'BatteryCharging' icon (battery shape + lightning bolt). Distinguishes via the bolt cut-out so the silhouette differs from the restroom rectangle at a glance.

### 23. Stylist's actual arm-by-arm pace ignored - estimate is static fiction

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > 'About 2 hr 10 left' text
- **What breaks:** The 'About 2 hr 10 left' string never updates. The progress bar fills on a fake interval (0.4% per second), but the human-readable time estimate is a hardcoded string. A 4-hour braid appointment showing the same '2 hr 10' for the entire visit erodes trust in every other estimate the salon gives.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as flag 11: derive remaining-time from progPct against a serviceTotalMinutes value. Even better — fetch the stylist's logged pace from the Stylist App and update the kiosk in real-time.
  - *Route target:* Stylist App owns service duration; Kiosk subscribes.

### 24. Current stage 'now' indicator looks identical to 'done' after first stage

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Stages row > 'now' state dot ring
- **What breaks:** Both .done and .now states set the dot to clay background. The only difference is .now adds a 5px shadow ring - very subtle at tablet viewing distance. A client glancing at the stages can't easily tell which stage they're currently in vs which are complete.
- **Proposed fix:** Differentiate 'now' with motion + a brighter ring. .stage.now .dot keeps the clay fill but adds a 2px --ochre ring + a 1.5s pulse animation. .stage.done .dot stays static clay. Now the active stage visibly breathes.

### 25. Stage labels are braid-specific but kiosk reused for all services

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stage labels (Sectioning, Braiding, Finishing, All done)
- **What breaks:** The stages 'Sectioning / Braiding / Finishing / All done' are hardcoded for braids - if this kiosk lives at every chair, a silk press client sees 'Braiding' as their second stage. The progress structure isn't service-aware, betraying the chair-side context the kiosk promises.
- **Proposed fix:** Source stages from a serviceTypes config keyed by service slug. Braids: Sectioning/Braiding/Finishing/Complete. Silk press: Wash/Blow-dry/Press/Complete. Color: Prep/Process/Rinse & style/Complete. Default to a generic Start/Mid/Finishing/Complete if unknown.

### 26. Confirm modal stays open indefinitely until tapped

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Auto-dismiss timing
- **What breaks:** After a client taps Water, the 'On its way' modal blocks the entire assistance grid until they hit Got it — they cannot send a second request (e.g. also need a charger) without dismissing first.
- **Proposed fix:** Auto-dismiss the confirm modal after 4 seconds (the cancel window from flag 13 ends, then the modal fades out). Background returns to the assistance grid so the client can stack requests.

### 27. Demo controls remain pointer-targetable even at opacity .5

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Reset button + Demo break toggle
- **What breaks:** The .demo container drops to opacity .5 but remains fully clickable — a real client at the chair can accidentally tap Reset (which signs them out) or trigger the break demo without noticing the buttons are 'subtle'.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 10 — hide them entirely behind a long-press gesture. When hidden, set pointer-events:none. When revealed, set pointer-events:auto.

### 28. Station number is hardcoded in HTML — same kiosk file deployed to every chair

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Station tag 'Station 14'
- **What breaks:** The station-tag .st span hardcodes 'Station 14' — there's no parameter, query string, or config that lets a single HTML file serve different chairs.
- **Proposed fix:** Read station from `?station=14` query param on load. Set #stationNumber.textContent from the param. Default to "Station —" if missing so it's visibly unconfigured.

### 29. Translate confirm body says 'who can help in your language' without recording which language

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Translate Please confirm body
- **What breaks:** Tapping Translate Please immediately fires the confirm without ever asking which language the client speaks — staff arrive without knowing which translator/tool to bring.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 57/63 — tapping Translate Please opens a follow-up sheet listing the six languages. Only after a pick does the confirm fire with the chosen language included.
  - *New copy:* "Confirm body: \"A Wolof-speaking team member is on the way.\""

### 30. Reset/endSession does not close an open confirm modal

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Reset button > endSession() while modal is open
- **What breaks:** If a confirm modal is showing and the demo Reset is tapped, the user is signed out but the scrim and confirm panel remain visible over the sign-in screen until tapped.
- **Proposed fix:** In endSession, first call closeConfirm() to dismiss any open modal, then proceed with state cleanup. Same applies to the celebration overlay (flag 22).

### 31. Demo controls cover the bottom-right corner of the .areq-grid 'Refreshment' card

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Button position fixed bottom 20px right 26px
- **What breaks:** On smaller kiosk screens the .demo container at fixed bottom 20/26px overlaps the bottom-right Refreshment request card hit area — taps land on demo buttons instead of Refreshment.
- **Proposed fix:** With demo controls hidden (flag 10), the overlap disappears. When revealed in prototype mode, dock them to the bottom edge as a full-width strip (not floating) so they never overlap content.

### 32. Two large Fraunces name inputs stacked vertically push the Enter CTA below the fold on portrait tablets

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Two name inputs stacked vertically
- **What breaks:** Each name field is 22px padding + 26px Fraunces + 22px margin-bottom = roughly 90+ px per input. On a portrait iPad with the soft keyboard up, the H1 (54px), sub-copy, both inputs, and the Enter button cannot all fit above the keyboard at once — the disabled Enter button (the thing you're trying to reach) scrolls off-screen the moment focus lands. Could be a single row of two side-by-side fields, or a single 'Full name' input.
- **Proposed fix:** With 'Tap to begin' (flag 14) the inputs disappear. If they must stay: place them side-by-side on tablets ≥768px (`.name-fields{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:14px}`). The Enter button stays above the fold even with keyboard up.

### 33. Sign out wipes state but does not confirm — easy to fat-finger

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > 'Not you? Sign out' button
- **What breaks:** The 'Not you? Sign out' button at the top of the kiosk drops the current client back to a blank sign-in screen with no confirmation prompt. A client who taps it by accident mid-service loses their name from the greeting and has to re-enter — no recovery, no undo. Should at least confirm before resetting.
- **Proposed fix:** Reuse the existing confirm modal pattern: tapping the end button opens it with title "End your visit?" and TWO buttons ("Stay in my chair" outline, "End visit" clay). Only the second calls endSession.
  - *New copy:* "Title: \"End your visit?\" / Body: \"This clears the screen so the next client can sign in. You can always sign back in.\""

### 34. Style/stylist card is not tappable for details

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker panel (Knotless Box Braids, Zainab O.)
- **What breaks:** The tracker card shows 'Knotless Box Braids · Medium · Waist length · Gold cuffs' and stylist Zainab O. A curious client expects to tap for inclusions, reference photo, or stylist bio. Nothing is interactive — no hover affordance, no handler. The card is purely informational with no path to learn more or to the Client Companion App where this would naturally live.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the .tracker h2 + .meta + .stylist block tappable. On tap, slide up a bottom-sheet (same backdrop pattern as confirm modal) showing the reference photo, full modifier list, stylist's bio + portfolio thumbnail, and a footer link "See more in your Companion App" that opens the Client Companion App surface.
  - *Route target:* Client Companion App > Today's appointment detail

### 35. Translation language list doesn't match the clientele

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Assistance > 'Translate Please' card
- **What breaks:** Offers English, French, Spanish — but Jolieden serves a West African / Black hair clientele (founders and stylists have Senegalese names). Wolof, Bambara, Haitian Creole, or Yoruba would matter far more than Spanish here. The card title 'Translate Please' also reads as broken English; 'Help in your language' (the subtitle) is already the better title.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the language list in the Translate card subtitle. Pull from a salonLanguages config so it's editable per location.
  - *New copy:* "Card title: \"Help in your language\" / Subtitle: \"Wolof, French, Bambara, Yoruba, Haitian Creole, English\""

### 36. 'One per visit' transactional caveat breaks hospitality tone

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Assistance > 'Refreshment' card subtitle
- **What breaks:** Subtitle reads 'A mini sandwich and juice, on us, one per visit.' The 'one per visit' policy disclaimer reads as a vending-machine restriction in the middle of a hospitality moment. Belongs in the operator policy doc, not on the client tablet. Same surface tries to set a 'you are in good hands' mood — this contradicts it.
- **Proposed fix:** Drop the policy clause from the client-facing subtitle. Keep the policy in operator-side notes only.
  - *New copy:* "Subtitle: \"A mini sandwich and juice, on us, one per visit\" → \"A mini sandwich and juice, on the house.\""

### 37. Sign-out button copy serves two unrelated jobs

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Greeting bar 'Not you? Sign out' button
- **What breaks:** The same button is labeled 'Not you? Sign out' — but it's also the only way for the legitimate client to exit at the end of their visit. A client who is the right person should never tap a button that begins with 'Not you?' It should either split into two affordances (verify identity vs. end session) or use neutral copy like 'End my visit.'
- **Proposed fix:** Split into one action with clearer copy. The greeting bar gets a single "End my visit" pill (outline). The "Not you?" case is handled by a smaller text link at the bottom of the tracker card ("Not [name]? Let staff know.") that opens an identity confirm sheet.
  - *New copy:* "Greeting button: \"End my visit\" / Tracker footer link: \"Not [name]? Let us know.\""

### 38. Stage thresholds compress the last two stages into 25% of the timeline

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Stage markers (Sectioning / Braiding / Finishing / All done)
- **What breaks:** Stage completion marks are [15, 75, 95, 100]. Braiding occupies 60% of the bar (15 to 75), Finishing only 20%, 'All done' a 5% sliver. A client watching the dots move will see 'Braiding' for what feels like the whole appointment, then a fast jump through Finishing. This makes the tracker feel inaccurate. Even thresholds (e.g., 20/65/90/100) would feel more honest.
- **Proposed fix:** Change marks from [15,75,95,100] to [25,60,90,100]. Distributes Sectioning 0-25%, Braiding 25-60%, Finishing 60-90%, All done at 90-100%. Update updateStages() to match.

### 39. Break-state ring fills on its own clock, not the return time

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Break state ring (conic gradient timer)
- **What breaks:** The ring fills from 20 to 330 degrees at 0.4 deg/sec — a 13-minute animation that visually implies countdown to the return time shown ('back around 2:38'). But the ring's animation is completely decoupled from the actual return time. A client doing the math will see the ring near full while the clock still says minutes away. Either tie the ring to the displayed return time or remove the implied countdown.
- **Proposed fix:** In toggleBreak, store returnTimestamp = Date.now() + 30*60*1000. The break interval now computes deg = 20 + (310 * elapsed / totalBreakMs) and clamps at 330. Ring and clock now share one source of truth.

### 40. Bell looks like the primary CTA but is decorative

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Assistance side > Bell icon (top-right of assistance column)
- **What breaks:** The 58px bell sits next to 'Need something? Tap and a team member comes to you' and animates on tap. A client reading that copy will tap the bell first — but the bell does nothing useful: it just plays the chime/swing animation. The six request cards underneath are the real CTAs. Either remove the bell or repurpose it as 'Call my stylist' (a generic, no-reason ping).
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 2 — wire the bell to a real "Call my stylist" request (7th request type). Update aria-label, add cursor:pointer ring on focus.

### 41. No celebration or exit moment when style is complete

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > Completion state ('All done, you look beautiful')
- **What breaks:** When progress hits 100% the progress text changes to 'All done, you look beautiful' but the rest of the kiosk doesn't change: same tracker layout, same assistance grid, same fixed station tag. This is the brand's biggest moment (the reveal) and there's no champagne accent, no 'Share your look,' no auto-transition to checkout or sign-out. The salon's whole emotional arc lands on a text swap.
- **Proposed fix:** When progPct hits 100, fade the tracker grid out and present a celebration overlay (champagne gold accent — --ochre + --sand): photo capture viewfinder "Share your look" CTA, "Tip Oumou" CTA, "See you next time" sign-out. After 90s of no interaction, auto-return to sign-in.
  - *New copy:* "Headline: \"You look beautiful.\" / CTAs: \"Save this look\" → routes to Client Companion App journey, \"Leave a tip\" → routes to Companion App tipping, \"End my visit\" → endSession"
  - *Route target:* Client Companion App > Journey (Save look) + Companion App > Tipping

### 42. Subtitle copy under-sized for tablet-at-arm's-length viewing

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Assistance grid > Card subtitle text (12.5px)
- **What breaks:** Request card subtitles are 12.5px and the stage labels under the progress dots are 11.5px, both in the muted --espresso-soft color. A client in a salon chair views the tablet at arm's length, often with a cape and overhead lighting glare. For a tablet kiosk these supporting strings should be 14-15px minimum and the muted color reserved for true metadata.
- **Proposed fix:** Bump .areq .ah-sub from 12.5px to 15px and .stage .sl2 from 11.5px to 14px. Darken --espresso-soft to --espresso for the stage labels of done/now stages (already done) and increase contrast on muted text to 5:1 minimum.

### 43. Rapid taps on different request cards stack confirm modals incorrectly

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance request cards (any of the six)
- **What breaks:** sendRequest replaces the confirmTitle/confirmMsg in place and re-adds the .show class. Tapping Water then immediately Bathroom Break swaps the visible copy mid-fade, so the user sees a confirmation for a request they may not have meant — and any pending 'cancel' window is invisible.
- **Proposed fix:** In sendRequest, track an open-modal lock. If already open, queue the new request and wait until close. Alternative: extend the modal to a list view — "On its way: Water · Bathroom Break" showing both, with one shared Got it.
  - *New copy:* "Multi-request modal title: \"On its way\" / body: \"Water · Bathroom Break — both coming.\""

### 44. Auto-focus on first input opens on-screen keyboard immediately, covering instructions

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > Page load focus
- **What breaks:** window.load focuses #firstInput automatically. On a tablet kiosk this triggers the OS soft keyboard before the user has read the 'Welcome to your chair' eyebrow or sub-copy. The instructional context disappears the instant the screen loads.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the window.load focus() call. Instead, focus the input only when the user taps a new "Tap to begin" affordance (per flag 14). On a real tablet kiosk this defers the keyboard until the client has read the welcome.

### 45. Return time is computed once on toggle and never refreshes if break is extended

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > Return time
- **What breaks:** toggleBreak sets returnTime to now + 30 min once. If the stylist's break runs long there is no mechanism to update the displayed time — the client sees a stale 'back around 2:38' even after that time has passed.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an "Extend break" affordance only visible in the operator's manager/stylist app, not the kiosk. On the kiosk side, watch a returnTimestamp value and re-render the displayed time each tick of the break interval. If returnTimestamp passes, append "running a few minutes over" to the copy.
  - *New copy:* "Past return time: \"Zainab is on a lunch break. Back around 2:38, running a few minutes over.\""

### 46. No throttle or de-duplication on repeated taps of same request

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > All 6 request cards
- **What breaks:** Tapping 'Water' five times in a row fires five identical confirm modals (the visible one just keeps re-showing the same copy). In production this would queue five real staff alerts. No 'request already sent' state.
- **Proposed fix:** Track an inFlightRequests Set keyed by request type. If a type is in the set, sendRequest no-ops and instead pulses the existing card with a clay outline + caption "Already sent — coming up." Clear the set entry after 5 minutes or on staff fulfillment.
  - *New copy:* "Repeat tap caption: \"Already on its way.\""

### 47. Audio context created on first tap with no mute/preference

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Bell chime audio
- **What breaks:** chime() creates a Web Audio context on first request. There is no mute toggle, no volume preference, and no acknowledgement that some clients may be in a quiet salon where a 'ding-dong' from the chair is disruptive. No way to silence.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a mute toggle in the sign-in flow: a small speaker icon (top-right of sign-in, paired with the surface picker) toggles a localStorage flag. The chime() function checks the flag before playing. Default to muted on the kiosk surface — chair-side audio is rarely wanted.
  - *New copy:* "Toggle aria-label: \"Quiet mode — no sound when you tap\""

### 48. Break-state copy references 'buttons on the right' but layout collapses to single column under 900px

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > 'The buttons on the right still work'
- **What breaks:** Below the 900px breakpoint the kiosk grid stacks vertically, putting assistance below the tracker. The break-state instruction 'The buttons on the right still work' becomes incorrect — buttons are now below.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the break-state instruction to be position-neutral.
  - *New copy:* "\"The buttons on the right still work\" → \"The request buttons still work — ask for anything you need.\""

### 49. Demo break toggle still works on the sign-in screen, no-op visually but mutates state

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > 'Demo: stylist on break' toggle
- **What breaks:** Clicking 'Demo: stylist on break' before signing in flips the onBreak boolean and renames the demo button to 'Demo: stylist back' even though the break-state UI never appears. After sign-in, the kiosk loads in a hidden-break state and the user has to toggle twice to reach the demo break.
- **Proposed fix:** Hide the demo controls entirely on the sign-in screen (already proposed in flag 10). Additionally, the toggle function should no-op if signin is the active screen.

### 50. No autocapitalize/spellcheck/inputmode hints for tablet keyboard

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > First/Last name inputs
- **What breaks:** Name inputs have autocomplete='off' but no autocapitalize='words', spellcheck='false', or inputmode hints. On an iPad kiosk, typing 'Aïssatou' or 'Mame Diarra' triggers red-underline spellcheck and autocorrect fights the client.
- **Proposed fix:** Add `autocapitalize='words' spellcheck='false' autocorrect='off' inputmode='text' enterkeyhint='next'` (first name) / `enterkeyhint='done'` (last name) to the inputs.

### 51. Stylist shown as bare initial on generic brown gradient

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Stylist avatar (Z monogram)
- **What breaks:** For a salon premised on chair-side identity and relationship, Zainab is reduced to a 'Z' on a hardcoded #6B5C4A/#473b2e gradient. No photo, no warmth, no acknowledgment of the stylist as a person — feels like a generic avatar placeholder.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the initial-letter avatar with a 54px photo of Oumou (or whichever stylist is assigned). Use object-fit:cover and a 2px --cream ring. Fall back to initial only if photo fails to load.

### 52. Bell ding-dong plays at the requester's own chair

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Assistance request > Audible bell chime fires on client's own kiosk
- **What breaks:** The Web Audio chime (two-tone ding-dong) plays from the client's own kiosk speaker when they tap a request, not at the staff station. They already know they tapped it — the acoustic feedback to them is redundant and intrusive in a salon where music is playing.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove chime() from the client kiosk entirely. The chime belongs at the staff station / Manager Front Desk surface (where alerts arrive). On the kiosk, replace audio feedback with a subtle haptic (navigator.vibrate(40)) and a clay pulse on the tapped card.

### 53. Confirmation modal lacks role='dialog' and aria announcement

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Missing dialog semantics
- **What breaks:** The .confirm panel has no role='dialog', aria-labelledby, or focus management. Screen reader users get no announcement that their request was received, and keyboard focus is not trapped — Tab moves to elements behind the scrim.
- **Proposed fix:** Add `role='dialog' aria-modal='true' aria-labelledby='confirmTitle' aria-describedby='confirmMsg'` to .confirm. On open, move focus to the close X (flag 7) and trap focus within the modal until closed. Restore focus to the triggering card on close.

### 54. Break return time resets to now+30min each toggle, no continuity

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Break state > Return time recomputed every toggle
- **What breaks:** Every time toggleBreak() fires, it recalculates returnTime as Date.now()+30 minutes. So if a stylist is on break, returns, then leaves again, the displayed return time leaps forward by another 30 minutes regardless of when they actually said they'd be back. Time has no source of truth.
- **Proposed fix:** toggleBreak should only set returnTimestamp on the first toggle-on. Subsequent toggles read from a persistent break-start value (sourced from the stylist app — operator surface, not the kiosk). If unset, fallback to now+30. Add a property `breakStartedAt` distinct from `returnTime`.
  - *Route target:* Stylist App owns break start time; Kiosk reads it.

### 55. Enter on empty last name fails silently

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Last name field > Enter key
- **What breaks:** Pressing Enter in the last-name field calls enterKiosk(), which guards with 'if(!f||!l)return' and does nothing visible. No error, no shake animation, no focus jump — the client just thinks the kiosk is broken.
- **Proposed fix:** Refactor with the "Tap to begin" pattern (flag 14) so this case disappears. If keeping inputs: on Enter with empty last name, focus the last name field and pulse the field border in --clay with caption "Last name to finish."
  - *New copy:* "Caption: \"Last name to finish\""

### 56. Bell uses a div with onclick, not a button — no keyboard or screen reader access

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > Bell button (clickable div)
- **What breaks:** The bell at `<div class='bell' id='bell' onclick='ringBell()'>` is not a real button. It has no role='button', no tabindex, no keydown handler, no aria-label. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot trigger it.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert .bell div to <button class='bell'> with type='button', aria-label='Call my stylist' (after wiring flag 2). Add keyboard handler via native button semantics.

### 57. autocomplete='off' disables tablet autofill for returning clients

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Name inputs (autocomplete='off')
- **What breaks:** Both first and last name inputs set `autocomplete='off'`, which suppresses iPad/Android keyboard suggestions and contact autofill. Returning clients must retype their full name every visit instead of one-tap autofill.
- **Proposed fix:** Change `autocomplete='off'` to `autocomplete='given-name'` (first) and `autocomplete='family-name'` (last). Enables iPad/Android contact suggestions while keeping the inputs purpose-typed.

### 58. No font fallback strategy — entire UI breaks if Fraunces/Hanken fail to load

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Global > Google Fonts dependency
- **What breaks:** All headings use `'Fraunces',serif` and body uses `'Hanken Grotesk',sans-serif`. On a salon tablet behind a captive-portal Wi-Fi or with blocked Google Fonts, the fallback serif/sans-serif renders without the carefully sized letter-spacing, breaking the layout (greeting wraps, eyebrow caps overflow).
- **Proposed fix:** Update the font stacks: `'Fraunces', 'Iowan Old Style', 'Georgia', serif` and `'Hanken Grotesk', 'Inter', 'SF Pro Text', system-ui, sans-serif`. Add `font-display:swap` (already via Google Fonts URL) and size-adjust descriptors via @font-face for offline fallback.
