### 59. Confirm modal change not announced to screen readers

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > No aria-live region
- **What breaks:** When a request is sent, confirmTitle and confirmMsg textContent updates but neither element has aria-live. Screen-reader users hear nothing change when the modal appears with new content.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-live='polite' to the .confirm element and aria-atomic='true' to confirmTitle + confirmMsg. With the role='dialog' from flag 58, screen readers announce the title + body on appearance.

### 60. Stage interval cleared at 100% but break overlay can still hide completion

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Progress reaches 100
- **What breaks:** When progPct hits 100, progText becomes 'All done, you look beautiful' and the interval clears. But if `tracker.on-break` is still applied (stylist toggled break right at the end), the entire normal-state is hidden and the client never sees the 'All done' state — break overlay sits on top of a finished service.
- **Proposed fix:** When progPct reaches 100, force-clear the break state: remove `.on-break` class from .tracker, clear breakInt, then show the celebration overlay from flag 22. Completion always wins over break.

### 61. Progress always starts at 46% — even immediately after sign-in

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Hardcoded 46% start
- **What breaks:** `let progPct=46` is a module-level constant. The instant a client signs in, they see 'About 2 hr 10 left' and the bar at 46% — regardless of when the appointment actually started. A client arriving early sees fake mid-service progress.
- **Proposed fix:** Initialize progPct from a serviceStartedAt timestamp passed in via the operator. For the prototype, derive progPct from (Date.now() - sessionStart) / serviceTotalMs. New clients start at 0; the 46% start state should only show in a demo-data fixture.

### 62. Confirm modal does not queue or replace cleanly — second request overwrites title/msg mid-animation

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Multiple rapid requests reuse the same scrim
- **What breaks:** If a client taps a second tile while the first confirm is still animating in, the title/msg textContent overwrites but the modal does not restart its open animation. The first request acknowledgement is silently lost without a visible transition cue.
- **Proposed fix:** With the multi-request list view from flag 29 or the in-flight Set from flag 38, the second request appends to an in-flight list rather than overwriting. Modal title reads "On their way" if >1 request.

### 63. Modal does not auto-dismiss when client taps another request card

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > 'On its way' (after sending request) > Subsequent requests
- **What breaks:** Once the modal is open, the underlying assistance grid is covered by the scrim, but if the modal closes (Got it) and the client wants another request, every fresh request shows the same generic icon/check. There's no indication that previous requests are still in-flight - the modal treats each request as if it's the only one ever sent.
- **Proposed fix:** With the multi-request modal (flag 29) the client can keep tapping cards; each one extends the list shown. Modal auto-dismisses 4s after the last tap, with a "Dismiss" button always available.

### 64. Sign-in CTA is in body copy not the button

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > h1 'Settle in and sign in'
- **What breaks:** The italic emphasis 'sign in' is in the headline (clay italic), which the eye reads as the action. But the actual action button below says 'Enter' - a generic verb that does not match the headline language. The two compete for what the action is called.
- **Proposed fix:** Match the button label to the headline italic.
  - *New copy:* "H1 italic: \"sign in\" → Button label: \"Sign in\" (replaces \"Enter\")"

### 65. No way to learn anything about your stylist from the kiosk

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stylist row (Z avatar + Zainab O.)
- **What breaks:** The stylist card shows avatar, name, title. There is no link to her portfolio, no 'meet your stylist' card, no Instagram/social, no bio. For a first-time client whose only context is this chair, the kiosk treats the stylist as an opaque label.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 4/44 — tapping the stylist row opens a bottom-sheet with bio, portfolio, and routes to Client Companion App for full profile / messaging.
  - *Route target:* Client Companion App > Stylist profile

### 66. No way to view or confirm what was actually booked

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Style metadata 'Medium · Waist length · Gold cuffs'
- **What breaks:** Three modifiers shown as a single dot-separated line, no way to expand, no booking summary, no price. If the client wants to confirm 'wait, did I book gold cuffs or silver?' there is no recourse on the kiosk - it's display-only and incomplete.
- **Proposed fix:** Tapping the .meta line under the H2 opens the same booking-detail bottom-sheet (flag 4). Adds a "View full receipt" link routing to Client Companion App's Today tab.
  - *Route target:* Client Companion App > Today > Booking detail

### 67. Bathroom icon is generic rectangle + dot/line, illegible at glance

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Bathroom Break card icon
- **What breaks:** The SVG for Bathroom Break ('<rect x="5" y="3" width="14" height="18" rx="2"/>' plus a dot and line) renders as a phone-screen or notepad shape, not a recognizable restroom symbol. Clients glance-scanning the grid won't identify it without reading the label.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace with a universal restroom door + person icon (Lucide 'DoorOpen' or a stylized person glyph). 24x24 viewBox, 1.6px stroke, clay tone.

### 68. Centered Fraunces serif inputs are decorative-first, function-second

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Name input fields
- **What breaks:** Inputs use Fraunces serif at 26px centered - beautiful for display but adds typing friction on a tablet keyboard. Centered text inputs are well-known UX antipattern (cursor jumps mid-word). For chair-side speed, function should win over typographic elegance.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag 14's "Tap to begin" simplification, the typing problem disappears entirely. If keeping inputs as fallback, switch text-align to left and reduce font-size to 22px Hanken — function over flourish.

### 69. Sub-copy is generic salon platitude not Jolieden voice

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > Sub copy 'You are in good hands'
- **What breaks:** 'You are in good hands. Relax and enjoy your time with us' could appear on any massage chair or hotel chair. The Jolieden voice (warmer, more specific, with named affection) is missing - no 'your stylist Zainab has you' or 'we're glad you're here today' specificity.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the sub-greeting in Diéssou's warm specific voice using the stylist's name and time-of-day awareness.
  - *New copy:* "\"You are in good hands. Relax and enjoy your time with us.\" → \"Oumou's got you today — settle in.\""

### 70. Bell chime tone (880Hz + 660Hz pure sines) is harsh and clinical

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Bell button > Audio file
- **What breaks:** The chime uses bare sine oscillators at 880Hz and 660Hz with no harmonic richness, no reverb, no decay envelope variation. The result sounds like a microwave timer, not a warm boutique-salon ding. The audio brand moment is the opposite of Diéssou's warm cream/clay aesthetic.
- **Proposed fix:** With chime() removed from the kiosk per flag 55, this disappears at the source. For staff-side audio on the Front Desk surface, use a soft marimba sample (mp3) instead of synthesized sines.

### 71. Touch device cards use hover transform that never triggers on real kiosk

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Card hover transform
- **What breaks:** The .areq:hover lift effect requires hover capability, which tablets don't have without a stylus. The :active state does scale to 0.99 briefly but the primary visual feedback (hover lift + clay border + shadow) is dead code on the actual kiosk hardware. Tap feedback should not depend on :hover.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the hover transform rules in `@media (hover:hover){...}`. Add :active state with a clay outline + 0.97 scale so tap feedback is consistent on touch.

### 72. Demo controls don't visually identify themselves as demo-only

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Demo control buttons
- **What breaks:** The demo buttons in bottom-right ('Demo: stylist on break', 'Reset') sit at 50% opacity but otherwise look like real production buttons. No 'DEMO' badge, no dotted border, no 'preview-only' tag - they're production-styled CTAs that just happen to say 'Demo' in their label. Easy to mistake the intent.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap demo controls in a labeled container with dotted clay border, monospace "PROTOTYPE TOOLS" tag at the top-right, and a tinted background. Even when revealed, the framing makes them obviously not production UI.

### 73. Heading copy '<3 'Need something?'' is too tentative for a service moment

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > 'Need something?' heading
- **What breaks:** The heading 'Need something?' phrases hospitality as a question with no implicit yes - it's the kind of thing a busy waiter says. Diéssou's voice would lean warmer: 'Anything for you' or 'How can we take care of you?'. The current copy makes the client feel they need to justify the ask.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the question with a warmer declarative.
  - *New copy:* "\"Need something?\" → \"Anything you need\""

### 74. Confirm modal title h3 not labeled as the dialog heading

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Title element role
- **What breaks:** The 'On its way' h3 in the confirm modal has no aria-labelledby relationship to the modal container, so assistive tech does not announce the title as the dialog's accessible name.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag 58's role='dialog' fix, add `aria-labelledby='confirmTitle'` and ensure id='confirmTitle' is set on the h3.

### 75. End-session button has no visible :focus-visible outline

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > 'Not you? Sign out' button focus state
- **What breaks:** The .greet .end button defines only :hover but no :focus styling, so keyboard users tabbing to it (the only easily-reachable focusable element on the kiosk screen) get no visible indicator.
- **Proposed fix:** Add `.greet .end:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--clay); outline-offset:3px}` so keyboard focus is unmistakable. Apply the same focus token system-wide for any focusable element.

### 76. Request cards have no role='button' on the div element

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > .areq cards (cursor:pointer)
- **What breaks:** Each .areq is a div with onclick but no role, so screen readers announce it as a generic group rather than a button, and Voice Control on iPad cannot target it by name.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 51 — convert .areq to <button> elements with `type='button'`. Native button semantics make Voice Control + screen readers + keyboard all work.

### 77. Sign-out button visually competes with the welcome greeting

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > 'Not you? Sign out' positioning
- **What breaks:** The end-session button sits inline with the 40px Fraunces 'Welcome, Amara' greeting in the same flex row — a major destructive action gets equal visual weight with the greeting, encouraging accidental dismissal.
- **Proposed fix:** Move the end-session button OUT of the .greet flex row. Put it as a small text link at the bottom-right of the tracker card ("End my visit") with a 13px Hanken treatment — visually de-emphasized but still discoverable.
  - *New copy:* "Bottom-right of tracker: \"End my visit\" (text link, not pill)"

### 78. Static 'Amara' fallback ships in production HTML

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting > 'Welcome, Amara' default text node
- **What breaks:** If JavaScript fails to run (CSP, blocked inline script, network error mid-load) the kiosk visibly greets every client as 'Amara' — a hardcoded persona name leaks into the live UI.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 31 — empty default. If JS fails, the greeting reads "Welcome" (no name) which is brand-safe.

### 79. Break-state copy is always 'lunch break' regardless of time

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > 'Lunch break' copy hardcoded
- **What breaks:** If the stylist toggles break demo at 9am or 4pm, the kiosk still says 'on a lunch break' — the break-type label is a string literal, not driven by time-of-day or stylist input.
- **Proposed fix:** Driver the break-type from time-of-day: <11am "a quick break" / 11-2pm "a lunch break" / 2-5pm "a quick break" / >5pm "a dinner break". Or accept a break-type string from the operator side.
  - *New copy:* "Variable: \"Zainab is on {{breakType}}\" with the table above."

### 80. Progress text region not marked aria-live

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Progress text element id='progText'
- **What breaks:** When the progress hits 100 and the text changes to 'All done, you look beautiful', no screen reader announcement fires — a visually-impaired client doesn't know the service is complete.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-live='polite' to #progText. State transitions are announced when they change.

### 81. Enter in first-name field still fires focusLast even when last name is already populated

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > Enter key focusLast() flow
- **What breaks:** If a client tabs back to fix a typo in first name and presses Enter, focus is yanked back to last name — they cannot submit by pressing Enter while the first field is focused.
- **Proposed fix:** In the first-name keydown, check `if(e.key==='Enter'){ if(lastInput.value.trim()) enterKiosk(); else lastInput.focus(); }`. Enter submits when both are filled, advances when not.

### 82. 'In progress' label has no completion-state replacement

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > 'In progress' static label
- **What breaks:** When progPct hits 100, the .pt text changes to 'All done, you look beautiful' but the adjacent .pl label still reads 'In progress' — the label and value contradict each other.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 90 — drive .pl label from state. At 100%: "Complete". The label always matches the progress value.

### 83. SVG stroke=var(--teal) — inline SVG attribute referencing CSS custom property

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > break-ring icon svg uses var(--teal)
- **What breaks:** SVG presentation attributes don't resolve CSS variables in older Safari/Chrome — the coffee-cup icon renders with no stroke (invisible) on those engines.
- **Proposed fix:** Move stroke to a CSS rule: `.break-ring svg{stroke:var(--teal)}`. Remove the inline stroke='var(--teal)' attribute. CSS rules resolve custom properties reliably across engines.

### 84. Disabled Enter button color contrast falls below WCAG AA

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > btn.clay disabled state opacity .4
- **What breaks:** At opacity .4 the white text on clay #A8623C drops to roughly 2.3:1 contrast against the page background — fails normal-text AA (4.5:1).
- **Proposed fix:** With 'Tap to begin' (flag 14) the disabled state disappears. If kept: disabled state uses background var(--espresso-soft) with text var(--cream) at full opacity instead of clay+.4 opacity. Contrast meets 4.5:1.
  - *New copy:* "Disabled button: muted espresso-soft background, cream text"

### 85. Progress text doesn't update if break is toggled mid-progress

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > 'In progress' label .pl + 'About 2hr 10 left' .pt
- **What breaks:** Toggling break while progress is at 60% leaves the .pt text reading 'About 2 hr 10 left' — but this text is initialized literal and only changes at 100% completion, not while paused.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag 11's dynamic progress text, the text already updates each tick. Add break-state copy override: while onBreak, .pt reads "Paused — back around [returnTime]". Resumes normal countdown on toggle-off.

### 86. Break ring fills 20-330deg over 775 seconds (~13 min) regardless of actual break length

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Break ring conic-gradient timing 0.4deg/s
- **What breaks:** breakDeg increments 0.4 per second, reaching max 330 after ~13 minutes — but the displayed return time is 30 minutes out, so the ring fills 2x faster than the actual countdown implies.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 20 — tie the ring fill to the actual returnTimestamp. The 30-min displayed time matches the 30-min ring fill. One clock, one truth.

### 87. Outline pill 'Not you? Sign out' visually outranks the in-content session controls

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > 'Not you? Sign out' (right side)
- **What breaks:** The only visible button at the top of the kiosk session is 'Not you? Sign out' — a pill that hovers clay on hover. Because it is the lone control in the greeting bar, it reads as the screen's primary action even though signing out mid-style is the worst possible thing a real client could do. There is no positive-action button (e.g. a 'Save photo to my journey' or 'Tip Zainab') to balance it.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 123 — move end button to a small text link in the tracker footer. Add a positive primary action in the greeting bar instead: "Save photos to my journey" (clay pill) routing to Client Companion App.
  - *Route target:* Client Companion App > Journey

### 88. Stage labels render at 11.5px — below tablet legibility minimum

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stages row > stage labels font-size
- **What breaks:** The stage labels (Sectioning, Braiding, Finishing, All done) are set to font-size 11.5px in CSS. At chair-side viewing distance (24-30 inches on a tablet stand), 11.5px sans-serif at espresso-soft color falls below the legibility threshold, especially for older clients. Already-flagged item 23 covered assistance card subtitles at 12.5px but missed the tracker's even smaller 11.5px stage labels.
- **Proposed fix:** Bump .stage .sl2 to 14px and .stage.now .sl2 / .stage.done .sl2 to 14px font-weight 600. Maintains visual differentiation at tablet viewing distance.

### 89. All six request icon tiles share identical clay-tinted square — no visual differentiation

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Card icon backgrounds (.ai)
- **What breaks:** Every assistance card has the same 50x50px rounded square in rgba(168,98,60,.13) clay tint behind the icon. The cards become a wall of identical earth-tone squares; visual scanning for a specific request (Water vs Bathroom Break vs Charger) relies entirely on the small glyph and the title text. A subtle color or shape variation per category (refreshments vs comfort vs utility) would let clients spot what they need in their peripheral vision.
- **Proposed fix:** Differentiate by category: hospitality (Water, Refreshment) use --clay tint. Comfort (Need a moment, Something feels tight) use --teal tint. Utility (Phone, Translate) use --ochre tint. Visual scanning by warm/cool now works.

### 90. Stylist last name shown as initial 'O.' while client must enter full last name to sign in

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stylist row > 'Zainab O.' last initial
- **What breaks:** The kiosk demands the client type their full last name to enter, then displays the stylist as 'Zainab O.' — withholding the very information it required from the client. It reads as a one-way power dynamic: the salon knows your full name but you only get an initial of theirs. Inconsistent with Jolieden's warm hospitality voice.
- **Proposed fix:** Show the stylist's full name ("Oumou Dieng" not "Oumou D."). The salon owns the data and warmth comes from completeness.

### 91. Tracker H2 'Knotless Box Braids' (34px) competes with greeting (40px) — no clear primary

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Style name 'Knotless Box Braids' vs greeting font weight
- **What breaks:** On the kiosk's main screen there are two Fraunces 500 weight serif headlines within 100px of each other — the 40px 'Welcome, Amara' and the 34px 'Knotless Box Braids' — both at the upper left. Neither owns the page. The screen has no single content anchor, just two near-peer headings.
- **Proposed fix:** Reduce tracker H2 to 26px. Greeting clearly dominates as the page anchor. Tracker H2 reads as the secondary 'what's happening here'.

### 92. Sign-in column capped at 560px leaves vast empty cream on either side of a tablet kiosk

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > .signin-wrap width 'min(560px,86vw)'
- **What breaks:** On a 1024-1280 wide kiosk tablet, a 560px-wide sign-in column with two centered inputs and a button leaves 230-360px of empty cream on each side. The aesthetic minimalism reads as 'unfinished page' on a wide tablet rather than as a deliberate composition. Either widen the column or add a visual anchor (illustration, brand mark, today's date / appointment summary) in the negative space.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a right-column composition on tablets ≥900px: 60/40 split with left holding the sign-in CTA and right holding today's date, the assigned stylist photo + name, and a small 'Today's reference' card showing the booked style photo. Negative space becomes intentional context.

### 93. Stage dots have no tap interaction or detail

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker stages (Sectioning / Braiding / Finishing / All done)
- **What breaks:** The progress stages look like a stepper that should be tappable to see what each stage involves or to see timestamps. No handlers, no tooltips, no detail view. Decorative-only on a touch surface where every visual element invites a tap.
- **Proposed fix:** Add onclick to each .stage that opens a tiny popover anchored above the dot showing the stage's plain-language description ("Sectioning: Zainab parts your hair into the grid she'll braid from. About 20 min.") and timestamp if reached. Use the same paper card + clay border as existing cards.
  - *New copy:* "Sectioning: \"Parting your grid — about 20 min\" / Braiding: \"The long stretch — sip water, take breaks\" / Finishing: \"Sealing tips, trimming, cuffs\" / All done: \"You look beautiful\""

### 94. No error/validation feedback for edge cases (single character, numbers, emoji)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > 'Enter' button + name inputs
- **What breaks:** checkName() only validates non-empty trimmed input — entering '1' / '1' is accepted and proceeds. There is no minimum length, no character validation, no error state. A client typing just a space then a real character gets through with a malformed name displayed in the greeting.
- **Proposed fix:** Add validation to checkName: require ≥2 letters per field, regex /^[\p{L}\p{M}'\- ]+$/u to permit accented + apostrophe + hyphen names but reject digits/emoji. On invalid input show a 12px clay caption below the field; do not block — only the Enter button stays disabled.
  - *New copy:* "Caption (when invalid): \"Letters only, please — we want to greet you properly.\""

### 95. Modal has no visible close X — only Got it / scrim dismiss

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal ('On its way')
- **What breaks:** The 'On its way' confirmation overlay can be dismissed by tapping the scrim or 'Got it', but there is no visible close X in the modal corner. On a touch kiosk, the scrim dismiss is not discoverable and a client who doesn't see the 'Got it' button (it's below the message at the bottom) has no obvious way out. Minor but a common kiosk-pattern miss.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 36px circular close button (top-right of .confirm card, –12px offset so it overlaps the corner) with an X icon (1.6px stroke matching kiosk icon family), aria-label "Close", calls closeConfirm.
  - *New copy:* "aria-label: \"Close\""

### 96. Jolieden wordmark is not a home/exit link

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Station tag (Jolieden / Station 14)
- **What breaks:** The 'Jolieden' wordmark in the top-left station tag is styled like a brand mark — on the other artifact surfaces, the wordmark typically links somewhere. Here it has no handler, no href, no role. Inconsistent with other surfaces and a missed home/exit affordance.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the .station-tag .mark in a button with aria-label "Open surface picker" that opens the same surface picker sheet from flag 1. Long-press (1.5s) opens demo controls (fixes flags 10/15/110/122/163).
  - *Route target:* Surface picker sheet

### 97. 'Bathroom Break' tile copy is misleading when stylist is on break

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Break state > Assistance tiles still visible
- **What breaks:** When the stylist is on lunch break, the break overlay says 'The buttons on the right still work' — but the 'Bathroom Break' tile still says 'Your stylist will pause and pick right back up'. The stylist is already paused (on break), so the copy is contradictory. Tile still triggers a confirm modal but the message doesn't acknowledge the break context.
- **Proposed fix:** In sendRequest, branch on the onBreak state. When true, the Bathroom Break confirm body should read "Perfect timing — Zainab's stepped away. We'll show you to the restroom." Use a contextual lookup table keyed by [requestType, onBreak].
  - *New copy:* "During break: \"Perfect timing — Zainab's stepped away. We'll show you to the restroom.\""

### 98. Demo controls visible to real clients in production-style mock

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls (bottom-right)
- **What breaks:** The 'Demo: stylist on break' and 'Reset' buttons in the bottom-right are visible (opacity 0.5 → 1 on hover). On a real kiosk a curious client would tap them and either trigger the break overlay or sign themselves out. These should be hidden behind a hidden gesture or a query-param flag for the prototype review only.
- **Proposed fix:** Hide .demo by default (display:none). Reveal only via the long-press gesture on the JOLIEDEN wordmark (flag 8) OR via ?demo=1 query param. When shown, wrap in a labeled chrome bar with a "PROTOTYPE TOOLS" badge so they read as a separate environment.
  - *New copy:* "Badge above demo buttons: \"PROTOTYPE TOOLS — not visible in production\""

### 99. Eyebrow and italic emphasis use the same clay color, flattening hierarchy

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Sign-in > Eyebrow + H1 em color stack
- **What breaks:** The 'Welcome to your chair' eyebrow and the 'sign in' italic emphasis in the H1 are both --clay, with no other contrasting accent between them. Diéssou's system has --ochre and --teal precisely for these layering moments. Same flattening happens on the kiosk greeting (eyebrow class isn't present but the italic 'Amara' is again --clay). Pick one role for clay (primary accent) and lift the eyebrow into ochre or espresso-soft so the eye reads in order.
- **Proposed fix:** Move all eyebrow elements (.eyebrow, .lbl) to --ochre. Reserve --clay for italic emphasis and primary CTAs. This applies to both sign-in eyebrow and tracker eyebrow.
  - *New copy:* "CSS: .signin-wrap .eyebrow{color:var(--ochre)} and .tracker .lbl{color:var(--ochre)}"

### 100. Card titles read as form labels, not hospitality copy

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Tracker > 'Bathroom Break' / 'Too Tight or Discomfort' card titles
- **What breaks:** 'Bathroom Break' and 'Too Tight or Discomfort' are title-cased like form fields and feel clinical against the warm cream surface. 'Need a moment' and 'Something feels tight' would carry the same meaning with Jolieden's voice. The heart icon used for discomfort also conflicts with the common 'favorite' / 'save' pattern.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite all six card titles in Jolieden's warm voice. Swap the heart icon for Discomfort to a hand/palm icon (open hand glyph) to avoid favorite-pattern collision.
  - *New copy:* "Water → \"Water\" (kept) / Bathroom Break → \"Need a moment\" / Phone Charger → \"Phone's dying\" / Translate Please → \"Help in your language\" / Too Tight or Discomfort → \"Something feels tight\" / Refreshment → \"Snack, please\""

### 101. Brand wordmark and station number weighted equally

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Kiosk > Station tag (top-left fixed)
- **What breaks:** 'JOLIEDEN' and 'Station 14' sit at the same scale with a thin divider between them. The brand should anchor; the station number is metadata. Either lift JOLIEDEN (size/weight) or demote the station number to a smaller, more utilitarian treatment so the brand registers first on the chair tablet.
- **Proposed fix:** In .station-tag, increase JOLIEDEN to 17px and tighten letter-spacing to .28em. Demote "Station 14" to 11px uppercase letter-spaced .2em color --espresso-soft so it reads as utility metadata.

### 102. Inputs allow leading/trailing whitespace then strip it silently

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > First name + Last name inputs
- **What breaks:** checkName uses .trim() to enable the Enter button, but a user typing only spaces sees no feedback explaining why Enter stays disabled. Two visually-filled fields produce a disabled button with no hint.
- **Proposed fix:** On blur, strip leading/trailing whitespace from the input value. If the trimmed value is empty, show a 12px clay caption "We need your first name to greet you" / "And your last name" below the field.
  - *New copy:* "Captions: \"We need your first name\" / \"And your last name\""

### 103. Pressing Enter in last name fires enterKiosk even when button is disabled

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > Last name input (Enter key)
- **What breaks:** The onkeydown handler calls enterKiosk() directly without checking the disabled state. If only first name has content, pressing Enter in the empty last name field still attempts to submit (the internal !f||!l check rejects it silently, but the keystroke contract is inconsistent with the visible disabled button).
- **Proposed fix:** In the last-name keydown handler, guard with `if(e.key==='Enter' && !enterBtn.disabled) enterKiosk()`. The Enter contract now matches the button's disabled state.

### 104. Confirm modal not dismissible with Escape key

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal ('On its way') > Got it button
- **What breaks:** The modal only closes via scrim click or Got it tap. There is no keydown listener for Escape, which is the universal modal-dismiss expectation on any device with a keyboard (BT keyboard attached to a tablet, accessibility keyboard).
- **Proposed fix:** Add a global keydown listener: `if(e.key==='Escape' && scrim.classList.contains('show')) closeConfirm()`. Also add to the sign-out confirm from flag 3.

### 105. Default greeting name 'Amara' flashes before client sign-in resolves

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar ('Welcome, Amara')
- **What breaks:** The kiosk markup hardcodes 'Amara' in #greetName. If a CSS load delay causes the signin screen to briefly not be the active one, or if a stylesheet fails, the kiosk shows the wrong name. Should default to empty or to the station number.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the HTML default of #greetName from "Amara" to empty string. The kiosk JS sets it on signin. If JS fails to load, the greeting reads "Welcome." which is brand-safe.

### 106. When progress hits 100, 'All done' replaces time text but stages don't all light

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > All done state
- **What breaks:** updateStages uses marks [15,75,95,100]. The final 'All done' stage only becomes done when progPct >= 100, but the prior stage's 'now' logic uses progPct >= marks[i-1]. At exactly 100, the All done dot flips done but the prior 'now' decoration vanishes with nothing celebratory — the user sees four small dots and a static line.
- **Proposed fix:** Use the celebration overlay from flag 22. Before the overlay shows, animate all four dots to .done state in sequence (cascading 100ms apart) with a gold pulse on the final dot, then fade in the overlay.

### 107. Reset button is an alias for endSession with no visual distinction or confirmation

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls (bottom-right) > Reset button
- **What breaks:** Clicking Reset wipes the input state and returns to sign-in identically to endSession. The label 'Reset' implies a different demo-state action (e.g. clear break state and progress) but it doesn't — confusing for a stakeholder demo.
- **Proposed fix:** Make Reset actually reset demo state: progPct=46, onBreak=false, clear any open modals, clear name fields, return to sign-in. Rename to "Reset prototype" so its scope is explicit.
  - *New copy:* "Button: \"Reset prototype\""

### 108. Disabled Enter button has no aria-disabled or screen-reader cue

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > Disabled Enter button
- **What breaks:** The button uses the HTML disabled attribute (good) but the visual cue is just opacity:.4. Users with low vision or color sensitivity on a glare-prone tablet screen may not realize the button is disabled — they tap, nothing happens, no feedback explains why.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-disabled='true' to the button when disabled. Add a visually-hidden caption tied via aria-describedby explaining what's missing ("Add your first and last name to continue").

### 109. Scrim click dismisses but is not announced as a dismiss affordance

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Scrim
- **What breaks:** The dark backdrop has onclick=closeConfirm but no cursor:pointer, no role=button, no visual cue that tapping it dismisses. Users who don't know the convention have only the 'Got it' button.
- **Proposed fix:** Add cursor:pointer to .scrim, role='button', aria-label='Close confirmation'. The visible close X from flag 7 covers the primary affordance; the scrim becomes a fallback only.

### 110. Sub-copy promises 'ask for anything you need without interrupting your stylist' before any examples shown

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Sub copy paragraph
- **What breaks:** The promise of frictionless service is made on the sign-in screen but the request grid only appears after sign-in. A hesitant first-time client has no preview of what kinds of requests are available, lowering the chance they engage.
- **Proposed fix:** Below the sign-in sub-copy, add a horizontal scrolling preview row of 3-4 example request icons + labels ("Water", "Phone's dying", "Need a moment") at reduced opacity. Anchors the promise with concrete examples.
  - *New copy:* "Below sub-copy: small label \"Here's what you can ask for:\" followed by icon row preview."

### 111. Initial avatar is decorative-only and unlinked

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Stylist initial avatar ('Z')
- **What breaks:** The 54px Z avatar circle next to Zainab O. is the most clickable-looking element in the tracker but has no handler. Users may tap it expecting to see the stylist's profile, bio, or send a thank-you note.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the .sa avatar tappable — opens the stylist bottom-sheet (flag 4) with bio, portfolio, and a 'Send Oumou a thank-you' CTA that routes to the Client Companion App messaging.
