### 112. Sub-greeting copy 'Relax and enjoy your time with us' never changes once shown

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > 'You are in good hands' sub-greeting
- **What breaks:** The static welcome line stays identical from sign-in through break to completion. A more dynamic kiosk would shift to 'You're nearly done' or 'Sip your water' as the session evolves. As-is, the page feels frozen.
- **Proposed fix:** Drive the sub copy from progPct: 0-30 "Welcome in. You're in good hands." / 30-70 "Sip some water — we've got you." / 70-95 "Almost there." / 95-100 "Final touches." / break-state "Zainab will be right back." Add a copy table keyed by progress band.

### 113. Break icon is a coffee mug for a 'lunch break' message

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Break state > Coffee-cup icon labelled 'lunch break'
- **What breaks:** The break-state ring contains a coffee/tea mug glyph, but the headline says 'Zainab is on a lunch break'. Coffee for lunch is an iconography mismatch — should be a fork/sandwich or a more neutral pause symbol.
- **Proposed fix:** Swap the SVG for a simple fork+spoon glyph (Lucide 'Utensils') at the same 1.6px stroke as other kiosk icons. Use a neutral pause icon if break-type is generic.

### 114. Stylist avatar gradient uses raw hex outside design tokens

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Stylist avatar > Hardcoded gradient hex
- **What breaks:** linear-gradient(140deg,#6B5C4A,#473b2e) hardcodes two opaque browns that don't exist in the cream/clay/ochre/teal token system. Escapes the design system and reads as a different palette family.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace `linear-gradient(140deg,#6B5C4A,#473b2e)` with `linear-gradient(140deg, var(--espresso-soft), var(--espresso))`. Aligns with the token system.

### 115. Clay button hover shadow uses opaque hex as shadow color

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > btn.clay hover shadow
- **What breaks:** box-shadow:0 18px 34px -18px var(--clay) uses the opaque #A8623C clay color as a shadow tint. The result is a hard orange-tinted shadow rather than the warm cream-paper drop intended by the design language.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace `box-shadow:0 18px 34px -18px var(--clay)` with `box-shadow:0 18px 34px -18px rgba(168,98,60,.45)` (or define a --shadow-clay token). Softens the tint into a warm halo instead of a hard orange smear.

### 116. Multiple stages can show 'now' state simultaneously

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > Stage logic (updateStages)
- **What breaks:** The updateStages logic adds 'now' to every stage where progPct is past the previous mark but not yet the current mark. When progPct is between two marks, both stages can light up as 'now' since `else if (i===0 || progPct>=marks[i-1])` matches multiple stages in sequence on a single pass.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite updateStages: find the highest mark index where progPct >= marks[i]. Mark all stages ≤ that index as 'done'. Mark index+1 as 'now' if it exists. Single source of truth per pass.

### 117. Hardcoded '2:38' return time visible before break toggled

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Default return time '2:38'
- **What breaks:** The break-state markup hardcodes `<b id='returnTime'>2:38</b>` as a placeholder. If the break overlay is ever shown without toggleBreak() running (e.g. CSS class manipulated externally or future bug), the client sees a fake '2:38' return time unrelated to current time.
- **Proposed fix:** Set `<b id='returnTime'></b>` empty in HTML. Populate on toggleBreak. Add a CSS rule to hide the parent line when returnTime is empty.

### 118. Sign-in inputs not wrapped in a form element

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Name inputs (no form element)
- **What breaks:** Inputs sit loose in a div, not in a `<form>`. No native form submit, no implicit Enter handling via form, no autofill semantics, no input grouping for assistive tech. Per-input keydown listeners are a hand-rolled substitute that misses standard form behavior.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap inputs and Enter button in a <form onsubmit='event.preventDefault(); enterKiosk()'>. Remove the per-input keydown listeners. Native form submit handles Enter on either field correctly.

### 119. Reassurance copy claims progress is on track even when stylist breaks during finishing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Break state > 'Your chair is held and your style is right on track'
- **What breaks:** The 'right on track' tagline shows regardless of progPct. If the stylist breaks at 90% (finishing stage), the copy contradicts the visible state since taking a break late in a service is not 'on track'.
- **Proposed fix:** Drive the reassurance line by progress band. When progPct >= 85 during break, copy reads "Almost done — Zainab will finish up after lunch."
  - *New copy:* "≥85% break: \"Almost done — Zainab will finish up after lunch.\" / Default: \"Your chair is held and your style is right on track.\""

### 120. Reset button visible and clickable on sign-in screen does nothing useful

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Reset on sign-in screen
- **What breaks:** The Reset button calls endSession() which only resets fields and refocuses input. On the sign-in screen (already there), it just blanks any typed text — no acknowledgement, no separation from normal sign-in actions.
- **Proposed fix:** With demo controls hidden on sign-in (flag 10), this disappears. If Reset must work on sign-in, change it to clear any partial input and show a brief toast "Cleared."
  - *New copy:* "Toast: \"Cleared.\""

### 121. Greeting is not a heading element — semantically a generic div

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Greeting 'Welcome, Amara' element
- **What breaks:** The 40px display 'Welcome, [name]' is wrapped in `<div class='hi'>` not `<h1>` or `<h2>`. Screen readers do not announce a primary landmark for the page; no heading hierarchy on the kiosk screen at all.
- **Proposed fix:** Change `<div class='hi'>` to `<h1 class='hi'>`. Update CSS selector accordingly. The sign-in screen's H1 only appears before sign-in, so there's no document-wide conflict.

### 122. Break ring --deg variable not reset when break ends

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Break state > break-ring (--deg variable)
- **What breaks:** When toggleBreak turns break OFF, the code clears the interval but never resets the `--deg` CSS variable on `.break-ring`. The next break starts visually with whatever fill the previous break ended at (until ~1s later when interval rewrites it to 20deg).
- **Proposed fix:** In toggleBreak when turning off, set `breakRing.style.setProperty('--deg', '20deg')` to reset to the starting value before the next break. Also set breakDeg=20.

### 123. Progress bar 1-second linear transition fights with 1-second interval — visible stutter

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Progress bar transition
- **What breaks:** `.ptrack i` has `transition:width 1s linear` and the interval that advances progPct also fires every 1000ms. The CSS transition completes exactly as the next jump starts, so the bar never reaches a steady-state and constantly drags.
- **Proposed fix:** Increase the interval to 1500ms and keep the transition at 1s. The bar visibly settles for 500ms between jumps. Or compute progress from `(Date.now() - serviceStartedAt) / serviceTotalMs` on a requestAnimationFrame loop for smooth fill.

### 124. Page lang='en' never updates when Translate Please is requested

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Global > <html lang='en'>
- **What breaks:** The HTML document declares lang='en'. Tapping 'Translate Please' summons a translator but the page itself remains lang='en' — screen readers using language-aware voice will keep reading in English regardless of the client's preferred language.
- **Proposed fix:** On Translate Please request, the kiosk sets `document.documentElement.lang` to the selected language (after the follow-up picker from flag 57). The visual UI stays English but assistive tech reads in the requested voice for any newly-rendered translated copy.

### 125. Water 'refill anytime' contradicts Refreshment 'one per visit' policy

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > Water confirm 'Refill as often as you like'
- **What breaks:** Water tile/confirm promise unlimited refills while the Refreshment tile says 'One per visit'. The inconsistency surfaces a hospitality policy contradiction — why is sandwich rationed but water unlimited? Confusing for a kiosk that aims for premium feel.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag 17's removal of 'one per visit' from the client UI, the contradiction disappears. Both items are now unlimited from the client's perspective. If portion control matters, surface it on the staff side, never the kiosk.

### 126. Greeting sub copy uses two sentences with mixed sentence-case style

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > Sub copy 'You are in good hands. Relax and enjoy your time with us.'
- **What breaks:** The sub copy is two short sentences with periods, while the rest of the UI (cards, button labels, confirm titles) uses sentence fragments without periods. Inconsistent punctuation tone across the screen.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the sub copy as a single fragment, matching the rest of the UI.
  - *New copy:* "\"You are in good hands. Relax and enjoy your time with us.\" → \"You're in good hands — settle in\""

### 127. Avatar text 'Z' uses Fraunces but has no aria-label or alt

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Stylist avatar (initial 'Z')
- **What breaks:** The avatar div shows 'Z' visually for Zainab but provides no accessible name. Screen reader announces only 'Z' as a meaningless token before reaching 'Zainab O.' text node — confusing for assistive tech users.
- **Proposed fix:** With the photo avatar from flag 52, add alt='Oumou D., your stylist'. If fallback initial renders, wrap in aria-hidden='true' since the stylist name is announced by the adjacent text.

### 128. Reset button uses outline style while 'Demo: stylist on break' uses solid — visual hierarchy implies Reset is the dismiss action

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Reset button styling
- **What breaks:** The `.alt` class on Reset makes it look like a Cancel/secondary, but it's actually the destructive action (ends current session). The break toggle gets the prominent solid espresso styling. Demo controls invite an accidental Reset by anyone who reads 'alt = safe'.
- **Proposed fix:** With demo controls behind a long-press gesture (flag 10), restyle both as utility-tier buttons (small, dotted clay border, monospace label). Neither button should look like a primary action. Reset becomes "Reset state" with a small refresh icon; break toggle becomes "Toggle break".

### 129. Disabled Enter button still receives hover transform via CSS specificity

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > btn.clay disabled hover
- **What breaks:** `.btn.clay:hover` defines transform and box-shadow without checking disabled. `.btn:disabled` is declared after but only sets `transform:none; box-shadow:none` — CSS order works here, but hover on a disabled button still flashes opacity transitions. Minor polish: disabled button shouldn't react to hover at all.
- **Proposed fix:** _(none returned — judgement call required)_

### 130. Bell visually rings on the client's own kiosk for every request, even when they did not tap the bell

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Bell button > ringBell() called on every request
- **What breaks:** sendRequest() unconditionally calls ringBell() which animates and chimes the bell on this client's chair. The bell is supposedly a 'call staff' visual, so it firing automatically conflates 'I asked for water' with 'I rang the bell'. Already partly flagged as audio (#55) but the visual animation firing on the client's own chair is a separate semantic confusion.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the bell swing animation from sendRequest. Animate the tapped CARD itself (clay pulse on its border) as the feedback. The bell stays static unless the client explicitly taps it (per flag 2/21 wiring).

### 131. Headline uses hardcoded <br> that breaks on narrow tablets

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > h1 line break <br>
- **What breaks:** `<h1>Settle in and<br><em>sign in</em></h1>` forces a line break. On portrait tablet widths under 380px (or with large accessibility text), the hardcoded br causes 'Settle in and' to wrap awkwardly while 'sign in' sits alone on a third line.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace `<br>` with a span: `<h1>Settle in and <em class='break'>sign in</em></h1>` and CSS `.signin-wrap h1 .break{display:block}` on screens ≥420px, else inline.

### 132. Inline onclick handlers from template literals — no event delegation

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Areq cards > onclick=sendRequest(${i}) inline
- **What breaks:** Each areq card has `onclick="sendRequest(${i})"` injected from innerHTML template. If the requests array were ever mutated or re-rendered, the indexes could go stale and produce wrong confirm messages. Brittle — should use data-index + event delegation.
- **Proposed fix:** Use event delegation: add one click listener on `.areq-grid` that reads `event.target.closest('.areq').dataset.requestKey`. Each card has `data-request-key='water'` etc. Request lookup uses the key, not an index.

### 133. Static 'In progress' label persists into break state if break starts before progress finishes

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Progress tracker > 'In progress' label
- **What breaks:** When break toggles on, the tracker shows the break overlay, but if the client toggles break off, the same hardcoded 'In progress' label reappears with no acknowledgment that time passed. There's no distinction between 'just resumed' and 'mid-style' for the client.
- **Proposed fix:** Drive .pl label from state: progPct<5 "Just started" / 5-95 "In progress" / 95-100 "Final touches" / break "Paused" / 100 "Complete". The label is no longer hardcoded.

### 134. Refreshment icon path renders as a bag/lunchbox not a sandwich/juice

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance grid > Refreshment card (sandwich icon path)
- **What breaks:** The SVG path 'M4 8h16l-1 12H5z' draws a trapezoid bag shape - it reads as a shopping bag or container, not the 'mini sandwich and juice' the copy promises. Icon and copy don't match.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the path with a Lucide 'Sandwich' icon (or two stacked horizontal rounded rectangles representing bread slices). Match 1.6px stroke + clay fill of the icon family.

### 135. Eyebrow uppercase letterspacing weaker than sign-in eyebrow

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > 'Your style today' eyebrow label
- **What breaks:** Tracker eyebrow uses letter-spacing .18em at 12px; sign-in eyebrow uses .34em at 13px. The brand voice element should be consistent across surfaces - here the same UI role uses two different specs, making the tracker feel slightly less branded than the sign-in.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize on letter-spacing .28em for all eyebrows across the kiosk. Update .tracker .lbl and .signin-wrap .eyebrow to the same spec.

### 136. Confirm button copy 'Got it' inverts the speaker

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > 'Got it' button
- **What breaks:** The salon is the one acknowledging the request ('On its way... A team member will be with you'), but the button says 'Got it' as if the client is the one confirming receipt. Should read like an acceptance/thanks from the client (e.g., 'Thank you') or simply a dismissal ('Close'). Voice is muddled.
- **Proposed fix:** Reframe the button as the client closing the loop.
  - *New copy:* "\"Got it\" → \"Thank you\""

### 137. Reassurance text is teal italic-bold but never animates in

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > 'Your chair is held and your style is right on track'
- **What breaks:** The break state animation fades the whole panel but the reassurance line at the bottom appears with the same prominence as the headline. Design system would have it appear slightly later or with a subtle reveal - here it's just plain text at the bottom, weakening the reassurance moment.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an animation: `.break-state.show .br-msg{animation:fadeRise .6s ease .4s both}` with a 0.4s delay relative to the headline. The reassurance line now arrives a beat after the headline, weighting the warmth moment.

### 138. Sign-in and main kiosk share identical background - no state distinction

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Background gradient
- **What breaks:** Both screens use the same radial/linear gradient on body. There's no visual differentiation between the 'I'm about to start' state and the 'I'm in service' state. The kiosk would benefit from subtly warmer tones during active service to mark the transition.
- **Proposed fix:** Sign-in keeps the cream gradient; the kiosk main screen warms slightly via a body class swap to a softer linear-gradient pulling --bone and --paper deeper. Adds a subtle warm wash signal that service is active.

### 139. Progress bar gradient direction doesn't shift with progress

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Progress bar fill (clay → ochre gradient)
- **What breaks:** The bar uses 'linear-gradient(90deg,var(--clay),var(--ochre))' over its entire length, so at 5% you only see clay and at 100% you mostly see ochre. The color message should be consistent (e.g., always clay→ochre at all widths) - currently the visible color literally changes from one stage to the next, which is visually confusing.
- **Proposed fix:** Apply the gradient to a fixed-width container instead of the i element: outer .ptrack gets the full clay→ochre gradient as background, and the inner i is a paper-colored mask that shrinks as progress advances (reverse-mask). Color stays consistent regardless of width.

### 140. Italic Fraunces serif on 'sign in' clashes with sentence case rest

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Italic emphasis 'sign in'
- **What breaks:** The h1 reads 'Settle in and sign in' with the second 'sign in' italicized in clay. The word 'in' appears twice in close proximity, with one styled differently - this is a copywriting tic that calls attention to the repetition rather than the action. The phrase itself doesn't pay off the italic emphasis.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the headline to remove the duplicate 'in'.
  - *New copy:* "\"Settle in and <em>sign in</em>\" → \"Take a seat — <em>let's get started</em>\""

### 141. Default confirm body is generic and overrides specific copy

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Body copy 'A team member will be with you shortly'
- **What breaks:** The default modal text is the generic 'A team member will be with you shortly' - this is the initial HTML and is replaced when a request fires. But if confirm() ever opens without a request (race condition, future feature), the placeholder leaks through. The default should be brand-true even as fallback.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the default placeholder HTML to a brand-true fallback: title "Hi there." body "Tap a card to send a request to your team." This way if confirm opens accidentally, the default is on-brand.
  - *New copy:* "Title: \"Hi there.\" / Body: \"Tap a card to send a request to your team.\""

### 142. h1 line break makes screen reader read as two separate utterances

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign in screen > 'Settle in and sign in' h1 br tag
- **What breaks:** The hardcoded <br> between 'Settle in and' and 'sign in' causes assistive tech to pause mid-sentence, breaking the natural reading flow of the welcome message.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 86 — replace <br> with a styled span. Screen reader announces the H1 as one utterance.

### 143. Stage state conveyed by color only, no text or icon distinction

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stage 'done' / 'now' indistinguishable when scanned
- **What breaks:** A colorblind client cannot tell which stage is 'done' vs 'now' vs upcoming — all three are differentiated only by background color and a subtle outer glow that may not register.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a small checkmark glyph inside .stage.done .dot and a small filled dot pulse inside .stage.now .dot. State is now indicated by both color and shape, meeting WCAG 1.4.1.

### 144. Time-remaining text wrapped in italic Fraunces clay color matches stylist title color

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker .prog-wrap > 'About 2 hr 10 left' text inside .pt span
- **What breaks:** The progress remaining time uses the same Fraunces clay color as the 'Senior Braiding Influencer' stylist subtitle, making it read like another caption rather than a live countdown.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the .pt color from --clay to --espresso (regular weight) and keep the Fraunces italic for personality. Reserve --clay for actionable accents only.

### 145. Break-ring icon stroke uses var(--teal) which equals the conic-gradient fill

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > break-ring svg coffee cup color
- **What breaks:** The coffee mug icon and the conic-gradient ring use the identical teal value, so the icon visually disappears into the ring once the conic gradient sweeps past 180deg.
- **Proposed fix:** Set the icon stroke to --paper (cream) so it stands out against the teal fill. Or use --espresso for a darker contrast — either resolves the camouflage.

### 146. Focus call fires even if user has already navigated away from sign-in

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Auto-focus call window.addEventListener('load')
- **What breaks:** The load handler calls firstInput.focus() unconditionally — if a future route change keeps the page loaded, focus jumps back to the sign-in field even after the client has already entered the kiosk.
- **Proposed fix:** Guard the focus call: `if(document.getElementById('signin').classList.contains('active')) firstInput.focus()`. Focus only fires when sign-in is the visible screen.

### 147. Modal backdrop blur fails silently on Firefox kiosk tablets

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > Backdrop-filter blur(3px)
- **What breaks:** The scrim relies on backdrop-filter for separation from the kiosk content behind it; browsers without support show only the .45 alpha overlay, leaving the modal feeling flat and the underlying request cards still legible.
- **Proposed fix:** Increase the scrim alpha from .45 to .65 as a fallback. Use `@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(3px))` to reduce alpha back to .45 when blur is supported. Separation is guaranteed either way.

### 148. Stylist row has no aria-label tying avatar and name together

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stylist row (.stylist div)
- **What breaks:** Voice Over reads 'Z, Zainab O., Senior Braiding Influencer' as three separate elements instead of a single 'your stylist is Zainab O.' utterance.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the .stylist row in an element with aria-label='Your stylist today is Oumou D., Senior Braider'. Mark the inner avatar + name + title as aria-hidden='true' since the wrapper label covers it.

### 149. Decorative .wave span is always present in the DOM with role implications

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > Bell .wave element
- **What breaks:** The empty .wave span sits inside the bell container and gets read by some screen readers as an unnamed region — it has no aria-hidden='true' to suppress it.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-hidden='true' to the .wave span. Decorative elements suppressed for assistive tech.

### 150. Tracker eyebrow letterspacing .18em narrower than sign-in eyebrow .34em

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > .lbl 'YOUR STYLE TODAY' eyebrow
- **What breaks:** The tracker uses a tighter letterspaced eyebrow than the sign-in 'Welcome to your chair' — two different eyebrow treatments on consecutive screens of the same surface.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 99 — standardize all eyebrows at .28em letter-spacing across both screens.

### 151. break-ring default --deg fallback value 30deg shows partial fill on initial render

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Break state > break-ring conic gradient css var --deg
- **What breaks:** The conic gradient defaults to 30deg when --deg is unset, so for one frame on first break-state show the ring already appears 8% filled before the interval kicks in.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the CSS default from `var(--deg,30deg)` to `var(--deg,0deg)`. Ring starts empty until the interval ticks it.

### 152. Confirm checkmark uses 2px stroke while bell/request icons use 1.6-1.7px

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Confirm modal > .ci checkmark icon SVG
- **What breaks:** The confirmation checkmark renders thicker than every other icon on the screen, making it feel like a different icon family.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize all kiosk icons at 1.6px stroke. Update the .ci checkmark SVG stroke from 2 to 1.6.

### 153. Demo break button text changes only after toggle completes — no transition feedback

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Demo controls > Demo break button label state lag
- **What breaks:** Tapping 'Demo: stylist on break' instantly flips the label to 'Demo: stylist back' but the underlying screen state takes a frame to repaint — a tester double-taps thinking nothing happened.
- **Proposed fix:** On click, immediately apply a `.is-loading` class to the button (small clay spinner + locked label) until the screen transitions. Disable the button until the visible state matches.

### 154. Bell SVG has no width/height attributes, relying solely on CSS

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > Bell svg view box missing
- **What breaks:** If CSS fails to load the bell SVG renders at the user-agent default (often 300x150), spilling out of its 58px container before styles arrive.
- **Proposed fix:** Add `width='58' height='58' viewBox='0 0 24 24'` to the bell SVG. Even if CSS fails the SVG renders at intended size.

### 155. Break ring conic-gradient has no fallback for older browsers

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Conic-gradient browser support
- **What breaks:** Tablets running older Chromium kiosk software won't render the conic gradient — the timer ring shows as a solid teal circle with no progress indication.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an @supports fallback: where conic-gradient is not supported, render the ring as a solid teal circle with a small clock-arrow SVG overlaid pointing at the current angle. Maintains the time-passing signal without the gradient.

### 156. Sign-in copy column does not adapt to landscape vs portrait kiosk orientation

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > .signin-wrap fixed width min(560px, 86vw)
- **What breaks:** An iPad rotated landscape on a wall mount gets a tall narrow column that wastes horizontal space; portrait gets a clamped 86vw that crowds the inputs.
- **Proposed fix:** Use orientation media queries: portrait keeps min(560px, 86vw). Landscape uses min(720px, 72vw) and arranges the inputs side-by-side. With the 'Tap to begin' simplification (flag 14), this is trivial.

### 157. Greeting flex justify-content:space-between with no wrap rule

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > .greet flex layout collapse
- **What breaks:** On a narrow kiosk in portrait, the long name 'Welcome, Aaliyah-Jacqueline' plus the 'Not you? Sign out' pill overflow the row — content clips against the right edge.
- **Proposed fix:** Add `flex-wrap:wrap; row-gap:14px` to .greet. With the end button moved out of the row entirely (flag 123), the wrap concern is reduced to handling long names — `min-width:0` on .greet .hi prevents overflow.

### 158. Stage threshold 95 vs 100 means 'All done' stage only triggers at exactly 100%

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Stage marks array [15,75,95,100]
- **What breaks:** There is a 5% window (95-100) where 'Finishing' is done but 'All done' has not lit yet — clients see three lit stages and one dim stage even when service is effectively complete.
- **Proposed fix:** With flag 19's new thresholds [25,60,90,100], extend updateStages so the final stage shows 'now' from 90-99% and 'done' at 100%. Final stage no longer dim during the home stretch.

### 159. Sign-out leaves audioCtx alive across sessions

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > endSession does not clear interval-state
- **What breaks:** audioCtx is created on first ringBell() and never closed — subsequent clients sharing the kiosk reuse the previous client's AudioContext, which Chromium may have suspended.
- **Proposed fix:** With chime() removed (flag 55), audioCtx is never created in the first place. This concern disappears.

### 160. Rapid taps add and remove .ring class within 950ms before animation completes

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Bell button > 'ring' class race condition
- **What breaks:** If a client taps three request cards in quick succession, the bell swing animation restarts but the .wave pseudo-element animation can desync, leaving the wave visible after the swing ends.
- **Proposed fix:** Before adding .ring, force a reflow: `bell.classList.remove('ring'); void bell.offsetWidth; bell.classList.add('ring');`. Restarts the animation cleanly. With the bell's role redefined per flag 21, this only fires on explicit bell taps.

### 161. Long stylist title wraps under the stylist name, pushing avatar-row layout

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > 'Senior Braiding Influencer' line wrap
- **What breaks:** The .sr span has no max-width or overflow handling — a longer stylist credential like 'Senior Braiding Influencer & Color Lead' wraps to two lines and breaks the .stylist row vertical rhythm.
- **Proposed fix:** Set .stylist .sr to `white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; max-width:240px`. Long titles truncate with an ellipsis instead of breaking the row.

### 162. Got it button is full-width with no minimum touch separation from screen edge on small tablets

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Confirm modal > 'Got it' button width 100%
- **What breaks:** On 7-inch tablets the .confirm at 84vw shrinks, and the 100%-width Got it sits flush against the 40px padding — touch targets press the panel edge, easy to mis-tap onto the scrim.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 14px horizontal inset to .confirm .actions so the button sits within a comfortable margin from the panel edge. Increase .confirm padding-bottom to 32px so the button doesn't kiss the bottom edge.

### 163. Large serif input swallows trailing characters during fast typing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > Name field input font 26px Fraunces serif
- **What breaks:** Fraunces is loaded async from Google Fonts; while it's loading the input uses fallback metrics, then when Fraunces arrives the text reflows and characters typed during the swap can appear cut off until next keystroke.
- **Proposed fix:** With 'Tap to begin' (flag 14) there are no inputs. If kept: add `font-display:swap` already exists; explicitly size-adjust Fraunces fallback via @font-face descriptor (size-adjust:104%) to match metrics and avoid reflow.

### 164. Break icon mug uses 1.5 stroke vs other icons 1.6-2 stroke

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Break state svg with hardcoded paths for mug
- **What breaks:** The break-state coffee mug icon is drawn at 1.5px stroke while every other icon in the kiosk is 1.6-2px — the mug renders visually lighter than its surrounding text.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize all kiosk icons at 1.6px stroke (per flag 135). Update the break icon SVG stroke-width to 1.6.

### 165. Inline style on .normal-state defeats CSS-based hide via .on-break selector

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > .normal-state inline style display:flex
- **What breaks:** The .tracker.on-break .normal-state{display:none} rule has lower specificity than the inline style display:flex — relying on the cascade order; if a future CSS edit reorders rules the break overlay won't hide the normal state.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the inline `style='display:flex'` from .normal-state. Define `.normal-state{display:flex}` in CSS instead. The `.tracker.on-break .normal-state{display:none}` cascade now wins predictably.

### 166. Subtitle implies one-tap behavior but the modal then requires a second tap to dismiss

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Assistance > .ah-sub copy 'Tap and a team member comes to you'
- **What breaks:** The promise 'tap and a team member comes to you' suggests a one-action flow, but the actual flow is tap-card → confirm modal → tap Got it — two taps before the user returns to baseline.
- **Proposed fix:** With auto-dismiss after 4s (flag 118), the user doesn't need to tap to close. "Tap and a team member comes to you" matches the actual experience.
  - *New copy:* "Keep current sub copy; the auto-dismiss makes the promise true."

### 167. Tracker can vertically overflow without scrolling when tall break content shown

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > .kiosk-grid grid-template-rows auto 1fr
- **What breaks:** The 1fr row holds both tracker (left) and assistance (right) — if the break-state content is taller than the available row height, the tracker content clips because .tracker has overflow:hidden behavior from min-height:0 in flex children.
- **Proposed fix:** Set `.tracker{overflow:auto}` and `.tracker .break-state{max-height:100%}`. If break content overflows, the tracker scrolls within its card rather than clipping content.

### 168. First and last name inputs not grouped as a form-control set

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > .signin-wrap absence of fieldset/legend
- **What breaks:** There is no semantic fieldset wrapping the two name inputs and no shared accessible label — screen readers cannot announce 'sign-in form, two fields' as a group.
- **Proposed fix:** With the <form> wrapper from flag 66, also add `<fieldset class='name-fields'><legend class='visually-hidden'>Your name</legend>...</fieldset>` so assistive tech announces the group.

### 169. Sign-out does not call clearInterval(breakInt)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > endSession breakInt cleanup
- **What breaks:** When endSession runs while break is active, it calls toggleBreak() which clears the interval — but if break ends naturally via toggleBreak then endSession is called separately, breakInt may persist depending on order.
- **Proposed fix:** In endSession: `clearInterval(progInt); progInt=null; clearInterval(breakInt); breakInt=null;`. Cleanup is unconditional.

### 170. Stylist initial 'Z' rendered in serif font that requires italic Fraunces variant load

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > 'Z' avatar font-family Fraunces serif
- **What breaks:** The Fraunces font weights 500/600 loaded includes upright but not italic — the avatar 'Z' should match Jolieden's brand-italic header style but renders upright, breaking the brand voice.
- **Proposed fix:** With the photo avatar from flag 52, the initial is fallback-only. When it falls back, keep it Fraunces upright (already loaded) — the brand italic was never required.

### 171. Style metadata uses interpunct separators while assistance subtitles use commas

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Style metadata 'Medium · Waist length · Gold cuffs'
- **What breaks:** The tracker meta line uses interpunct dot (·) separators ('Medium · Waist length · Gold cuffs'), but the assistance card subtitles right next to it use comma separators ('A chilled bottle to your station, refill anytime', 'Help in your language, English, French, or Spanish'). Two competing list-separator conventions sit four inches apart on the same screen.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize on interpunct (·) separators across the kiosk for metadata/list strings. Update assistance subtitles where appropriate.
  - *New copy:* "\"A chilled bottle to your station, refill anytime\" → \"Chilled bottle · refill anytime\""

### 172. Two clay-colored eyebrow elements compete at top-left

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Greeting 'Welcome, Amara' vs eyebrow 'Your style today'
- **What breaks:** The italic 'Amara' in the greeting and the uppercase 'YOUR STYLE TODAY' eyebrow directly below it both use the same --clay color and both compete to be the eye's first anchor at the top-left of the kiosk. The eye doesn't know whether to read the welcome line or the eyebrow first.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag 24 — move the eyebrow .lbl to --ochre, keep italic 'Amara' (or no italic post-flag 47) at --clay. Two-tone hierarchy restored.

### 173. Generic 'your chair' eyebrow ignores Station 14 personalization opportunity

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > 'Welcome to your chair' eyebrow
- **What breaks:** The station-tag in the corner already declares 'Station 14', but the sign-in eyebrow just says 'WELCOME TO YOUR CHAIR'. Jolieden's voice and the per-chair nature of the device support something more grounded like 'Welcome to Station 14' or 'Welcome to Zainab's chair' — both of which exist as known facts at sign-in time but are not surfaced.
- **Proposed fix:** Read the station + assigned stylist from the booking and personalize.
  - *New copy:* "\"Welcome to your chair\" → \"Welcome to Oumou's chair\" (when stylist known) / \"Welcome to Station 14\" (fallback)"

### 174. Sub-greeting copy crowds the bottom of the greeting block with no breathing room

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Greeting bar > Sub copy line height vs greeting baseline
- **What breaks:** The .greet .sub element has margin-top:7px under a 40px Fraunces serif greeting. Seven pixels between a 40px display serif and a 15px sans subtitle is too tight — the descenders of 'g' in 'Welcome' nearly touch the cap-line of 'You are in good hands.' This is the marquee moment of the kiosk and the typography is cramped.
- **Proposed fix:** Increase .greet .sub margin-top from 7px to 14px. The 40px Fraunces greeting and the 15px Hanken sub-copy now have a comfortable rhythm.

### 175. Confirm modal title (27px) is smaller than the welcome greeting (40px) — hierarchy inverted

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Confirm modal > Title font-size vs greeting font-size
- **What breaks:** The confirm modal that fires when a request goes out has a 27px Fraunces title, but the ambient welcome greeting on the page behind it is 40px Fraunces. A modal that is the only thing the user should be reading at that moment should outweigh, not underweigh, the page header it's overlaying. The scrim helps but the typographic hierarchy fights the focus.
- **Proposed fix:** Bump .confirm h3 to 32px Fraunces 500. The modal title now visually dominates the page header it overlays.

### 176. Break copy 'Zainab is on a lunch break' uses indefinite article 'a' — reads slightly impersonal

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Break state > break-state .bt copy 'Zainab is on a lunch break'
- **What breaks:** The phrasing 'Zainab is on a lunch break' sounds like a workplace status. Jolieden's voice would more naturally say 'Zainab stepped away for lunch' or 'Zainab is taking lunch' — recognizing the stylist as a person, not a worker on a scheduled break.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite to recognize the stylist as a person.
  - *New copy:* "\"Zainab is on a lunch break.\" → \"Oumou stepped away for lunch.\""

### 177. Confirm modal narrower than necessary on a tablet — looks like a phone alert

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Confirm modal > .confirm width 'min(440px,84vw)'
- **What breaks:** The confirm modal caps at 440px wide on a tablet that's likely 1024px+ across. A modal that small floating in the middle of a 1024-wide screen reads as a smartphone notification, not a tablet-native confirmation. Tablet-native modals are typically 60-70% of viewport width to feel intentional.
- **Proposed fix:** Change .confirm width from `min(440px,84vw)` to `min(640px,72vw)`. Modal now feels tablet-native and intentional.

### 178. Cream/clay background gradient identical to other client-facing surfaces — no kiosk identity

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Global > body background gradient
- **What breaks:** The body uses the same cream-to-warm-sand radial gradient pattern shared across Jolieden's client-facing surfaces. The kiosk is a fundamentally different context (stationary tablet, single-purpose, 3-4 hour use), and could earn a slightly distinct background treatment — a touch more saturation, a paper-grain texture stronger than the current 0.045 opacity noise — to signal 'you are at the chair' versus 'you are browsing on your phone.'
- **Proposed fix:** Bump the noise opacity from 0.045 to 0.07 on the kiosk surface only. Adjust the radial gradient warmth toward --sand. Subtle but signals 'chair-side, not phone'.

### 179. Tracker card padding (32px) vs assistance card padding (20px) creates visual weight imbalance

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > '.tracker' card padding (32px) vs assistance card padding (20px)
- **What breaks:** The tracker card on the left has 32px internal padding while each of the six assistance cards on the right uses 20px. The left half breathes; the right half feels packed. The two halves of the kiosk's primary content grid use inconsistent spacing systems, so the screen reads as 'one luxurious panel and a grid of buttons' rather than two balanced halves.
- **Proposed fix:** Reduce .tracker padding to 28px and bump .areq padding to 24px. The two halves of the grid now share a 24-28px breathing system.

### 180. Tracker uses 1px border + shadow; assistance cards use 1.5px border + no shadow

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Border treatment vs assistance card borders
- **What breaks:** The .tracker card has border:1px + box-shadow:var(--shadow-soft). The .areq assistance cards have border:1.5px + no shadow (until hover). Two different elevation strategies in adjacent areas with no system reason for the difference — the kiosk's visual hierarchy language is inconsistent.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize: both surfaces use border:1px var(--line) + box-shadow:var(--shadow-soft). Consistent elevation language across the kiosk.

### 181. Sign-in note re-explains what the sub-copy just said

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Sign-in screen > .signin-note 'No appointment lookup needed...'
- **What breaks:** The sub-copy above the inputs says 'Enter your first and last name to begin. This screen is yours for the visit, so you can ask for anything you need without interrupting your stylist.' Then the note below the button says 'No appointment lookup needed. Your stylist already has your booking, this is just so we can take care of you while you are here.' Both blocks of copy are reassuring the client that name entry is low-stakes — the second block is redundant and pushes the Enter button further from the eye.
- **Proposed fix:** Delete the .signin-note element. With 'Tap to begin' (flag 14), the simplification removes the need for any reassurance copy. The H1 + sub-copy + CTA is sufficient.

### 182. 'All done' shown as a future stage marker is confusing as a checkpoint vs an end state

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Stages row > Stage labels include 'All done'
- **What breaks:** The four stage markers are Sectioning / Braiding / Finishing / All done. 'All done' is not a stage, it's a state. The progress bar already conveys completion; treating 'All done' as a labeled marker is like a flight-tracker showing 'In flight / Landing / Arrived / Already left airport'. A three-stage progression with completion implied by the bar reaching the end would read cleaner.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove 'All done' as a stage marker. Use three stages (Sectioning / Braiding / Finishing) and let completion be implied by the bar reaching 100% + the celebration overlay (flag 22).

### 183. Greeting block and sign-out button align at center, not at the greeting baseline

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Station Kiosk > Main screen > Tracker > Greeting + 'Not you? Sign out' button > Same row baseline
- **What breaks:** The .greet flex container uses align-items:center, so the 40px Fraunces greeting line and the 14px pill button align at their midpoints. Visually the pill floats too high on the line — it should align to the baseline of 'Welcome' or be visually pinned to the bottom-right corner of the greeting block.
- **Proposed fix:** With the end button moved out of the greeting row (flag 123/166), this layout concern disappears. The greeting block stands alone, properly anchored.

## Stylist App  `stylist`

*Mobile braider companion: schedule, prep notes, before/after photo capture, time tracking, earnings/tips, EN/FR toggle.*

**220 findings · 220 fixes**

### 1. Guide sheet scrim calls undefined closeSheet() function

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Client prep > Size and length guide sheet > scrim/dismiss
- **What breaks:** The guide scrim's onclick is closeSheet('guide'), but no closeSheet function exists in the script (only closeStationPicker is defined). Clicking outside the guide sheet throws a JS ReferenceError and the sheet stays open. There is also no X / close button inside the sheet, so the only escape is the broken scrim handler.
- **Proposed fix:** Rename the scrim onclick handler to closeGuide() and define closeGuide() to remove the .open class from #guideSheet and its scrim. Add an X button in the sheet header (top-right, 44px) that calls the same handler. Match the closeStationPicker pattern.

### 2. Capture CTA only shows a toast, no forward navigation

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Capture screen > Begin the style button
- **What breaks:** After snapping all 4 angles the primary CTA 'Begin the style' only fires showToast(). It does not navigate back to Today, to the progress tracker, or to anywhere else. The user is stranded on the capture screen with no natural next step.
- **Proposed fix:** After snap-count===4, beginStyle() should advance the Amara progress card from Sectioning to Braiding (call advanceStage()), navigate go('today'), and scroll to the in-progress card. Toast becomes 'Photos saved, style started.'
  - *New copy:* "Photos saved. Style started for Amara."

### 3. Stylist avatar is non-interactive, no profile/sign-out access

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Today + Portal > avatar circle (Z)
- **What breaks:** The 'Z' avatar in the topline of both Today and Portal screens has no onclick handler. There is no way anywhere in the stylist app to reach profile, settings, language preferences, timesheet, or sign-out. A stylist who needs to log out or change account info has no path.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the avatar 'Z' circle in a button that opens a bottom sheet (#profileSheet) listing: Profile, Timesheet, Language, Notifications, Sign out. Reuse the station-picker sheet pattern. Each row routes to a sub-view or fires a toast for sign-out.

### 4. Greeting language ignores app default state

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Today tab > header > greeting display
- **What breaks:** Initial HTML renders "Bonjour, Zainab" before setLang('en') overwrites it, causing a French flash on every load. More importantly, EN/FR toggle only translates the Today screen — Prep, Capture, Break, and Earnings stay in English. A French-speaking braider sees mostly English UI after toggling, undercutting the entire bilingual promise.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the static HTML greeting to 'Good afternoon,<br><em>Oumou</em>' (EN default). Extend the T translation map to cover Prep, Capture, Break, Earnings strings and call applyLang() on every go() so all screens render in the active language.
  - *New copy:* "Good afternoon, Oumou"

### 5. Today header claims 6 appointments, shows 4

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Today tab > eyebrow "Today · 6 appointments"
- **What breaks:** The day-summary eyebrow advertises 6 appointments but only 4 cards render (1 now, 2 next, 1 done). Stylist can't tell if 2 are missing/hidden or if the count is wrong — erodes trust in the schedule.
- **Proposed fix:** Render the appointment count dynamically from the appointments array length. Change eyebrow to 'Today, 4 appointments' (or seed two more cards if 6 is canon — recommend 4 to match what is shown).
  - *New copy:* "Today, 4 appointments"

### 6. Earnings numbers contradict the day shown

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Earnings tab > Today's commission card
- **What breaks:** Earnings shows "$420 today, 4 services" while Today shows 1 completed appointment (Maya R., 11 AM) and Amara in progress. A stylist comparing the two will distrust both. The numbers should derive from the actual completed appointments on Today.
- **Proposed fix:** Derive Today's commission from the completed appointments array: only Maya R. ($180 boho braids + $25 tip) is done at 1pm. Change hero to '$180 today, 1 service' and update tips/services cards to match. Recompute on every advanceStage to 'All Done'.

### 7. Four-angle capture uses identical icon for every angle

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Capture tab > Front/Back/Left/Right tiles
- **What breaks:** All four angle tiles render the same generic camera icon. The whole point of standardized angle capture is guiding the stylist to the correct framing — front-facing silhouette, back-of-head, side profiles. Currently the tiles are only differentiated by the word "Front/Back/Left/Right", defeating the photo-consistency goal.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the camera icon in each tile with a distinct silhouette outline SVG: front (face circle with center part line), back (head-back oval with nape line), left (profile facing left), right (profile facing right). Keep the dashed border + 'Tap to capture' microcopy below each.

### 8. Portal translate button cycles instead of choosing target

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Portal tab > any card > Translate button
- **What breaks:** Tapping Translate cycles EN→FR→ES→EN regardless of which language the card is currently in. An English-first stylist who taps Translate on a Spanish coaching note gets French next, not English. The button needs to know the user's primary language and translate TO it, not rotate through a fixed order.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace cyclePortalLang with translateToPrimary(cardIdx): translate the tapped card's text to appLang (user's primary). If already in primary, toggle back to original. Show a small caption 'Translated from FR' under the card title.

### 9. Pay deduction styled same as routine announcement

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Portal tab > Late arrival card
- **What breaks:** A $25 wage deduction lives in the same card chrome as a team meeting announcement, separated only by a small red pill. A punitive financial action against a worker's paycheck warrants stronger visual weight, plus context (when this hits the next paycheck, dispute path, who to talk to). Currently it's just informational with no recourse.
- **Proposed fix:** Give pay-red cards a distinct treatment: thicker left border (4px clay-deep), larger amount typography (Fraunces 20px), and an inline 'View details' link routing to a #deductionDetailSheet showing pay-period date, dispute path, and HR contact (Diéssou).

### 10. Unknown manager "Larysa" not introduced

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Portal tab > Larysa-authored cards
- **What breaks:** Three portal cards are "From Larysa" (a deduction, a recognition, a coaching note) but the project canon only includes Diéssou as owner. A stylist would not know who Larysa is, what authority she holds to issue a deduction, or whether to trust the recognition. Either introduce her clearly (role on profile) or attribute to a known cast member.
- **Proposed fix:** Rename Larysa to 'Mame Diarra' (existing operator-fixture floor manager). Or, if a new manager is intended, add a small subtitle under the name 'Floor manager' on first appearance and add her to personas.ts. Recommend Mame Diarra for canon consistency.

### 11. Upcoming appointment cards open the wrong client's prep

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Today tab > 3:30 Halima S. and 5:00 Treasure A. appointment cards
- **What breaks:** Both the 3:30 Halima and 5:00 Treasure cards call go('prep'), but the prep screen is hardcoded with Amara N.'s details (avatar 'A', name, member tag, hair color, notes, inspiration). Tapping a later appointment lands on the current client's prep instead of that client's.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the prep view to read the client slug from a clickedClientId variable set by each appt-card's onclick. Build separate prep data objects for Amara, Halima, Treasure. Render the appropriate client's avatar, name, tags, color, notes, and inspiration.

### 12. Guide sheet has no in-sheet close affordance at all

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Size and length guide sheet > entire sheet
- **What breaks:** Beyond the broken scrim handler already noted, the guide sheet itself has no X button, no Done button, no swipe-to-dismiss, and no Cancel — only the (broken) scrim tap. A stylist who opens it and never sees the scrim is fully trapped with no visible exit.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a sheet header row with a 44px X button (top-right) and a 'Done' pill (bottom-right of the sheet) that both call closeGuide() from fix #1.

### 13. Acknowledged state cannot be reversed even if tapped by mistake

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > formal notice > Acknowledge button
- **What breaks:** ackFormal() sets acked=true and replaces the button with a 'pointer-events:none' confirmation pill. If a stylist taps the acknowledge button by accident, there is no undo, no confirmation modal, and no way to flag the acknowledgement as accidental — and the toast says it has already been escalated to Diessou.
- **Proposed fix:** After ackFormal, show a 5-second 'Undo' link in the success toast and inside the button area that reverts acked=false. After 5s the action becomes irreversible and the Undo link disappears.

### 14. Final progress stage has no path forward

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Today tab > Amara progress card > 'Complete, she looks beautiful' end state
- **What breaks:** When the stylist reaches the 'All Done' stage, the CTA button disappears and the card just sits there with no next action. There is no 'Move to capture after photos' or 'Send to checkout' affordance — the appointment lifecycle dead-ends with no way to advance to the after-capture or completion.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as fix #49: when stage===All Done, render 'Capture after photos' as primary CTA and 'Send to checkout' as secondary, routing to Capture (after mode) and the Station Kiosk checkout screen respectively.

### 15. Capture screen has no before/after mode distinction

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Capture tab > 'Capture before' header / 'before/after' toggle (missing)
- **What breaks:** The screen is hardcoded to 'Capture before' but the copy below says 'the same four are required after.' There is no way to indicate which set is being captured now or switch modes, so the same screen can't serve both phases of the documentation workflow.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a segmented control at the top of Capture with 'Before' and 'After' tabs. State persists per client. Header changes to 'Capture before, Amara' or 'Capture after, Amara'. Each mode has its own 4 angle slots.
  - *New copy:* "Capture before, Amara / Capture after, Amara"

### 16. Hero number lacks payday-relevance context

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Earnings tab > 'Today's commission $420' hero
- **What breaks:** $420 today's commission sits in the dark hero card with no indication of whether tips are included, whether deductions apply, or how it differs from take-home pay. Given that the Portal tab tracks $25 deductions and $120 bonuses, the disconnect between 'commission' and actual pay needs reconciling in the hero or it becomes misleading.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a subtitle under '$420' reading 'Commission only, tips $95, take-home shown on Portal'. On tap, route to the Portal pay-impact card for full reconciliation.
  - *New copy:* "Commission, tips $95 separate. See Portal for take-home."

### 17. Pay-impact cards don't actually drill into detail

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > pay-impact hero > 'Tap any pay item below to see the detail' microcopy
- **What breaks:** The hero says 'Tap any pay item below to see the detail' but tapping a pay card (Late arrival, Goal bonus) only triggers translate/listen/mark-read — there's no detail drawer showing the deduction calculation, related timesheet, or appeal path. The copy promises a behavior the UI doesn't deliver.
- **Proposed fix:** Make pay-green and pay-red cards tappable (and pi-r rows too). Each opens a #payDetailSheet showing the calculation (e.g. '5 min late × $1/min × peak multiplier'), affected timesheet entry, pay date, and 'Dispute this' link.

### 18. Formal acknowledgment lacks a 'disagree / dispute' path

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > Formal notice card > Acknowledge button
- **What breaks:** Formal notices about attendance only offer 'I have read and understood' — there is no way to flag a dispute, request a meeting, or contest the notice. For an employment-record item that escalates to the owner, the unilateral acknowledgment carries legal risk and feels coercive.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a secondary 'Disagree, request a meeting' button under the Acknowledge button. On tap, opens a #disputeSheet with a textarea pre-filled with a polite template and a 'Send to Diéssou' CTA.

### 19. Active appointment shows start time but no elapsed or expected end

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Today tab > Amara card > '1:00 In progress' time
- **What breaks:** Amara's card shows '1:00 In progress' but no indication of how long she's been in the chair, expected completion, or whether the stylist is on track vs. running behind. A braider doing a 5-hour knotless install needs to manage time against the next 3:30 appointment.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace '1:00 In progress' with two lines: '1:00 - 5:30 (4h 30m booked)' and '52 min elapsed, on track' (or 'running 15 min over' in clay if behind). Live-update each minute.

### 20. Break screen offers only one fixed 30-min meal break

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Break tab > 'Start break' screen > break type selection
- **What breaks:** The screen hardcodes 'A 30 minute meal break' with no option to take a shorter rest break, restroom break, or longer one. Real salon shifts include multiple break types with different pay treatment — the rigid single option doesn't fit how a stylist actually paces an 8-hour day.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a segmented control with three break types: 'Rest 10m', 'Restroom 5m', 'Meal 30m'. Each preselects the duration and adjusts the ring accordingly. The meal break is the default.

### 21. Over-break visual escalation is too subtle

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Break tab > Over-time state > '+MM:SS' counter in clay
- **What breaks:** When the break runs over, the timer just turns the same clay color used throughout the app and prepends '+'. There's no animation, no haptic-equivalent visual urgency, no escalating message about pay impact — yet the Portal feed shows $1/minute deductions for being late. The financial consequence is invisible at the moment of decision.
- **Proposed fix:** On overtime, switch the ring to clay-deep with a slow pulse animation, change the counter to '+MM:SS, $X deducted' (live-updating $1/min), and show a clay banner 'You are over. Clock back in to stop the deduction.'
  - *New copy:* "You are over. Clock back in to stop the deduction."

- **What breaks:** Header is hardcoded to 'Capture before' and the subcopy says 'the same four are required after the style is complete' implying a second pass, but there is no UI path or state to ever flip the screen into 'Capture after' mode. The stylist would have no way to complete the required after-photos described in the copy.

Only the earn-hero and pay-impact use dark warm — those exceptions suggest the rest of the stylist surface is off-brief.

### 35. Audio bar control button has no handler

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 1

- **What breaks:** The .ab-play button in the audio bar shows two rects (pause icon) but has no onclick. The audio auto-dismisses after 4.2 seconds with no way for the stylist to pause, restart, or stop early. Tapping the visible play/pause control does nothing.
- **Proposed fix:** Wire .ab-play to a toggleAudio() function that pauses/resumes the playback (clearTimeout on the 4.2s dismiss), swaps pause/play icons, and adds a small X dismiss button to the right of .ab-play that calls hideAudioBar().

### 36. Clock-in and break-status cards look tappable but are not

- **What breaks:** The two .cs cards at the top of Today ('Clocked in / Since 8:02 AM' and 'Next break / Available') have no onclick handlers. They visually read as interactive status cards, but tapping the clocked-in card does not clock out and tapping Next break does nothing — break is only reachable from the bottom nav.

### 37. Photo and swatch tiles are decorative-only

A stylist cannot zoom, lightbox, or view source images for the reference photos. Critical for matching the brief, but only available at thumbnail size.

### 38. Language toggles are separate state, not unified

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Today vs Portal > language toggle
- **What breaks:** Today exposes EN/FR only; Portal exposes EN/FR/ES. Selecting ES on Portal does not propagate to Today, and selecting FR on Today does not propagate to Portal. setLang and setPortalLang maintain independent state with no shared store, so the stylist sees a mixed-language UI.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace setLang and setPortalLang with a single setAppLang(lang) writing to a shared appLang variable used by every renderer. Both top-line toggles read/write this one state. Add ES to the Today toggle so all surfaces offer EN/FR/ES.

### 40. Step-back has no confirmation despite affecting client screen

Tapping the right small chip on a phone is fiddly, and the choice has no memory between days.

### 45. Inspiration block reads as placeholder

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

### 46. Audio bar collides with bottom nav and content

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **What breaks:** The audio bar appears at bottom:100px, sitting just above the bottom nav and obscuring the last appointment card or portal item. No close affordance — it auto-dismisses after 4.2s. A stylist mid-read loses content under the bar with no way to dismiss it manually.

### 47. Speaker and edit pills below recommended touch size

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Today tab > speaker icons; Earnings > Edit button
- **What breaks:** Speaker `.spk` is 34px; goal Edit pill is roughly 28px tall. Apple HIG minimum is 44pt and Material is 48dp. On a working stylist's busy phone — possibly with gloves or wet hands between clients — these are easy to mis-tap.

### 48. Cannot retake or undo a snapped photo

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Capture tab > Front / Back / Left / Right angle tiles
- **What breaks:** snap() bails immediately if the angle already has the 'done' class (`if(el.classList.contains('done'))return;`). Once an angle is tapped accidentally, there is no way to retake it, remove it, or view what was captured.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the early return when classList.contains('done'). On second tap of a done tile, open a small popover with 'Retake' and 'View' actions. Retake clears the .done state and decrements snapped count.

### 49. Clocked-in card does not reflect break state

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Break tab > Today tab clock strip
- **What breaks:** startBreak() never updates the 'Clocked in / Since 8:02 AM' card on Today. While on break the Today screen still says the stylist is clocked in. After endBreak() the 'Next break: Available' card is also never marked as used, so a stylist could appear to be eligible for a break they already took.
- **Proposed fix:** When startBreak() fires, update the Clocked-in card to show 'On break' with a clay accent and the break-pill from fix #14. On endBreak(), set Next break card to 'Taken at {time}' and disable it for the rest of the shift.

### 50. Translate quietly marks unread cards as read

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > any card > Translate button
- **What breaks:** cyclePortalLang() calls markRead(i) on every press. Tapping Translate (often the first thing a non-English stylist would do) silently clears the red unread dot and decrements the bottom-nav badge, even though the stylist has not actually read or acknowledged the item.
- **Proposed fix:** Decouple translate from markRead. Translate only changes the displayed language; markRead is called only when the user taps the card body or an explicit 'Mark read' action.

### 51. Listen has no pause / stop control once playback starts

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > any card > Listen button
- **What breaks:** portalAudio() starts speechSynthesis playback and toggles a .playing class on the button. Pressing the same button again does nothing useful — it cancels then re-speaks from the top. There is no pause, stop, or scrub control, and the only way to silence playback is to navigate away or wait it out.
- **Proposed fix:** Make portalAudio() a play/pause toggle: first tap speaks, second tap calls speechSynthesis.pause() and swaps to a play icon, third tap resumes. Add a small X next to the button (visible only during playback) that stops fully.

### 52. Listen silently no-ops with no fallback when TTS unavailable

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Portal tab > any card > Listen button on iOS / muted devices
- **What breaks:** speechSynthesis.speak() does not throw synchronously when no voices are loaded or the device is muted, so the try/catch fallback never fires. The button toggles 'playing' state, no audio plays, and the stylist gets no error or visual indicator that playback failed.
- **Proposed fix:** Check speechSynthesis.getVoices().length and the device muted state before calling speak. If empty/muted, show a toast 'Audio unavailable, check device volume' and add an aria-live polite announcement. Don't add .playing class on failure.

### 53. No way to mark the client style as cancelled or no-show mid-stage

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **What breaks:** The progress card only advances forward (Sectioning → Braiding → Finishing → All Done) or steps back one stage. There is no way to abort the appointment, mark a no-show, or cancel — leaving any cancelled real-life session permanently stuck on a partial stage in the client's view.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a small 'More' button (3-dot icon) to the top-right of the progress card opening a sheet with: 'Mark no-show', 'Cancel appointment', 'Move to another stylist'. Each shows a confirm sheet and updates the appointment status.

- **Proposed fix:** Same as fix #10: add onclick to each totrow opening a per-row #totalsDetailSheet (this week breakdown, this month breakdown, payout schedule with past payouts).

### 110. Pay impact net number doesn't account for unviewed/pending items

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > pay impact hero > headline number
- **What breaks:** updatePayImpact() simply sums all pay-green and pay-red kinds in portalItems regardless of unread/acknowledged state. A formal notice that hasn't been acknowledged still counts toward the net. There's no pending/finalized distinction.
- **Proposed fix:** Compute pay-impact net only from acknowledged/finalized items. Add a 'Pending, $X' subtitle showing the unacknowledged total. Net updates when each item is acked or auto-finalized at period end.

### 111. Formal notice Acknowledged button has pointer-events:none after click

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > formal notice > acked state irreversibility
- **What breaks:** Once a formal notice is acknowledged, the .pc-ack.done CSS rule sets pointer-events:none. The stylist cannot tap to dispute, add a comment, or undo. The only state is acknowledged-and-sealed.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as fix #51: add a 5-second Undo window. After that, the button stays disabled but a 'Dispute' link below opens the dispute sheet (fix #58).

### 112. App has no connectivity state indicator anywhere

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** All the 'live on her screen', portal sync, station picker confirms, and TTS calls assume always-on network. The app has no offline indicator, no retry affordance, and no queue-when-offline pattern visible.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a global offline banner that appears at top:0 (above the topline) when navigator.onLine is false: 'Offline, changes will sync when reconnected.' Banner is clay-deep with white text.
  - *New copy:* "Offline, changes will sync when reconnected."

- **What breaks:** Portal shows pay impact +$95 net (bonus $120 - deduction $25). Earnings shows Today's commission $420 + Tips $95. These are independent number sets with no reconciliation copy explaining how the pay impact relates to the daily commission/tips totals.

- **What breaks:** If user opens station picker, selects station 5, taps scrim to dismiss without confirming, then reopens, station 5 still shows .sel state and the Confirm button is still enabled with pickedStation=5. State doesn't reset on scrim dismiss.

### 116. Completed appointment strip uses muted brown not green

- **What breaks:** The strip on the completed Maya R. card uses --espresso-soft (a muted brown), identical visually to the eyebrow text color. Status-completed should read as 'done' (typically green/teal in the brand) but here the only signal is gray-on-cream, making the kanban color-coding fail.

### 117. Progress stage dots use 'pd on' on stages already passed AND current

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

### 118. Previous styles tiles smaller than Inspiration tiles with no caption

Stylist cannot tell which install was when, and the visual hierarchy implies these are less important than 'inspiration' which is backwards (real history should outrank reference).

### 119. Bonus/Deduction labels use 13px on dark espresso background

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** The .pi-r text on the dark pay-impact card runs at 13px with .85 opacity over a #2C241D background. The reduced opacity drops contrast for the supporting label words and may fail AA for users on a phone in bright daylight.

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

### 121. Birthday banner uses generic gift/cake icon, no Jolieden mark

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** The pink celebration block uses a generic SVG cake/gift outline, the same kind any salon app would ship. No Jolieden champagne accent, no Fraunces flourish, no brand wordmark moment - the celebration screen is the strongest brand opportunity and it reads as boilerplate.

### 122. Three-button row on Formal notice wraps awkwardly to two lines on mobile width

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** With the long 'I have read and understood' label plus Translate and Listen, the .pc-actions flex-wrap row breaks to a second line where Ack sits alone, far from the natural reading order. The hierarchy of which is primary becomes ambiguous when wrapped.

### 124. Mixed timestamp formats across portal cards

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** Announcement (teal), Recognition (sage), Coaching (ochre), Formal (red), Pay-green (sage), Pay-red (red) - six chip colors stacked vertically on one feed create visual noise rather than helping scanning. No grouping or sticky-section separates them.

Apple HIG recommends 44pt min touch target with comfortable padding; the nav buttons hit minimum but their labels (Earnings, Portal) compete for visual weight. Considering Portal also carries a badge, the right edge feels heavier.

### 135. Teal token used for both 'live sync' status and 'break' primary action

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Proposed fix:** Split into two tokens: --teal-action for buttons (Start break, Mark complete) and --teal-status for indicators (Live on her screen). Different lightness keeps them visually distinct.

### 139. Step-back link hidden on first stage breaks the recovery affordance

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

Step back' link is hidden when stageIdx===0, so if the stylist accidentally taps 'Start braiding' once they can step back, but they can never step back from the initial Sectioning state if they later want to restart. Also, once the style hits 'All Done' the advance button disappears but the step-back is still shown — there's no way to un-complete cleanly except chained step-backs.

No persistent break indicator on Today.
- **Proposed fix:** When breakActive is true, add a persistent .break-pill banner above the bottom nav on Today/Earnings/Portal/Capture showing remaining time with a Resume link that returns to the Break tab. Reuse the audio-bar overlay pattern.

- **What breaks:** Stylist must trust the green pulsing dot that says "Live on her screen" without seeing what the client actually sees. A small preview thumbnail or "View what she sees" link would close the loop and let the stylist verify before advancing stages.

### 145. Weekly day-of-week bars lack amounts

### 146. Prep screen has no highlighted bottom-nav tab

### 147. Goal edit uses native browser prompt() dialog

### 149. Staff note has no link to full client history or other notes

### 150. Audio bar has no manual dismiss

### 151. Greeting uses French even before EN/FR toggle

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Today tab > greeting > 'Bonjour, Zainab' hardcoded initial
- **What breaks:** The page initial HTML says 'Bonjour, Zainab' even though setLang('en') runs on load and EN is the default toggle. There's a flash of French content before JS hydrates — discordant with EN being the labeled default. Should match the default language in static HTML.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as fix #15: change static HTML to 'Good afternoon, Oumou' to match EN default. Also matches the persona rename to Oumou per fix #205.

### 152. Break ring rotates clockwise but reads as filling, not depleting

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Break tab > Break ring conic-gradient progress
- **What breaks:** The conic-gradient fills the ring as time elapses (0deg at start to 360deg at end), so it visually grows. But conceptually a break depletes — most users expect a countdown ring to empty out, not fill up. Direction conflict between visual metaphor and timer semantics.
- **Proposed fix:** Invert the conic-gradient so the ring starts full (360deg of teal) at break start and depletes counterclockwise to 0deg as time elapses. Overtime fills back up in clay-deep.

### 153. Sunday-off styling assumes a fixed schedule

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Earnings tab > Weekly goal day strip > Sunday with .off opacity
- **What breaks:** The day strip hardcodes Sunday as .off (greyed out), but stylists may work Sundays in real schedules. The 'off day' is a personal config, not a salon-wide truth — yet the prototype treats it as fixed CSS state with no way to indicate which days the stylist actually works.
- **Proposed fix:** Read off-days from a workDays config (default Mon-Sat). Render .off styling only on configured off-days. Add a 'Set my schedule' link in the goal block that opens a sheet to toggle which days are working days.

### 154. Goal messaging assumes installs of consistent value

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Earnings tab > Goal message > 'two more installs does it'
- **What breaks:** The dynamic message says 'two more installs does it' but installs vary wildly — a knotless box at waist length is $400+, a quick cornrow refresh might be $80. The same '2 more installs' framing is meaningless without average ticket size context.
- **Proposed fix:** Change message to use dollar gap, not install count: '$660 to go this week, you average $330 per install.' Compute from goalTarget - currentTotal and avg ticket size.
  - *New copy:* "$660 to go this week, you average $330 per install"

### 155. 30 stations is implausibly large, no salon context
