### 175. Multiple portal cards can show 'playing' state simultaneously

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Stylist app > Portal tab > pcAudio button > playing state
- **What breaks:** portalAudio() calls speechSynthesis.cancel() but only the new card's button gets .playing added. If a previous utterance had set u.onend on a different card, that handler still fires and could leave the previous button stuck in .playing state visually until next render.
- **Proposed fix:** Track current playing card in a state variable currentlyPlayingIdx. Clear .playing from the previous button before adding it to the new one. In u.onend, check that idx still matches before clearing.

### 176. Warn-styled tag chips repeat the same warning twice

- **Proposed fix:** Merge into a single warn chip: 'Sensitive scalp, work slowly'. Remove 'Tender-Headed' as a separate pill. Keeps the high-priority flag landing harder.

### 184. Hero number uses no tabular-nums for currency alignment

### 186. Ending the break navigates to Today but leaves nav tab on Break briefly

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** endBreak() updates the clock-state text and calls go('today') which switches the bottom-nav highlight. However, if the stylist is on the Break tab when timer is over, the 'Clock back in' button still triggers endBreak() which calls go('today') but does not clear the over-break visual styles (clay color, conic-gradient override) on the break-ring before navigating away.
- **Proposed fix:** Clear the over-break clay/conic styles on the break-ring inside endBreak() before calling go('today'). Reset breakRemain to the default for the next break.

### 187. Acknowledged state of formal notice doesn't persist visually after language change

However, the translation copy for the 'acked' state is shown only in the new language without any indication that the action already happened in a different language. There's no timestamp or audit trail on the button.

### 188. Clocked in card shows static 'Since 8:02 AM' that never updates with real time

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

### 201. Add-ons row shows 'Gold cuffs' but no quantity or per-cuff cost

### 202. Appointments listed in mixed order with no sort or filter affordance

- **What breaks:** The day shows 1:00 (now), 3:30 (next), 5:00 (next), 11:00 (done) — out of chronological order. There's no way to sort by time, filter by status, or show only upcoming. The mixed order makes scanning hard.

### 203. Snap action doesn't request or check camera permission

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** Tapping an angle tile only adds the .done class — no camera API is invoked, no permission request, no actual photo captured. There's no flow for handling denied camera permission or unavailable camera.

### 204. Goal can be edited to absurdly high values with no upper bound

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Stylist app > goalTarget edit > no min/max validation beyond $100
- **What breaks:** editGoal() only checks v >= 100. A stylist could enter $99,999 and the goal track silently shows a tiny green fill. There's no realistic upper bound check and no warning that the goal exceeds historical performance.
- **Proposed fix:** In the goalEditSheet (fix #42), cap valid input at $10,000. Above that, show inline warning 'That's $X above your best week, are you sure?' with a confirm button.

### 205. Unread badge clears on translate but body text doesn't change indication

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > pcard > unread state stickiness
- **What breaks:** cyclePortalLang() marks the card as read after cycling language. The unread dot disappears and badge count drops. But there's no animation or 'just marked read' indicator — the change is silent and discoverable only by counting.
- **Proposed fix:** After fix #39 decouples translate from markRead, the unread dot is only cleared by explicit interactions. Add a subtle fade animation on the dot when it clears so the change is discoverable.

### 206. Portal feed has no New badge or visual separator between unread and read

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Stylist app > Portal tab > pc-time relative > Tomorrow vs Yesterday
- **What breaks:** Cards are listed in time order but there's no New / Earlier this week / Earlier separator. Unread cards have a red ring shadow but unread cards don't bubble to top — they appear mixed with read older cards.
- **Proposed fix:** Group the feed into sections with sticky headers: 'New (unread first)', 'This week', 'Earlier'. Unread cards sort to the top of New. Each section has an eyebrow label.

### 207. Hair color description not labeled, looks like free-floating text

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Prep tab > Hair color block > description text
- **What breaks:** The '1B natural with subtle 27 honey peekaboo' line sits below swatches with no kv label or eyebrow. Unlike the structured Service block above it, this block mixes typography styles inconsistently, breaking the design system's labeled-row pattern.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the description in a kv row with label 'Formula' so it matches the Service block pattern. Same typography hierarchy.

### 208. Edit button uses cream-2 pill, breaks the brand CTA hierarchy

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Earnings tab > goal-edit Edit button
- **What breaks:** The Edit button is the only interactive element in the goal block, but it uses the same passive cream-2 background as the .tg tag pills in Prep. There is no consistent 'secondary action' treatment across the surfaces, so Edit reads as decorative metadata rather than a tap target.
- **Proposed fix:** Change Edit to a small ghost button with clay border + clay text, matching the secondary-action treatment used elsewhere. Min-height:44px per fix #29.

### 209. Break idle screen lacks the eyebrow used on every other screen

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Break tab > breakIdle > 'Start break' Take your break heading
- **What breaks:** Today, Capture, Earnings, Portal all open with an .eyebrow line above the display heading. Break drops it entirely, creating a vertically centered layout that doesn't match the system's top-anchored hierarchy on other tabs.
- **Proposed fix:** Add eyebrow 'Break time' above the 'Take your break' heading. Same .eyebrow class as other screens.

### 210. Hero card's gold radial glow goes off the top-right edge

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Earnings tab > earn-hero ($420) > nested radial-gradient overlay
- **What breaks:** The pseudo-element radial gradient on the earn-hero is positioned at right:-40px top:-40px, which on this 390px viewport bleeds past the border-radius corner. The decorative champagne glow clips visibly at the rounded corner instead of fading inside the card.
- **Proposed fix:** Add overflow:hidden to .earn-hero so the radial gradient is clipped by the border-radius. Or move the gradient origin to right:30px top:30px so it stays fully inside the card.

### 211. Square angle tiles waste vertical space on a tall mobile viewport

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Capture tab > angles grid > tile aspect-ratio:1
- **What breaks:** A 2x2 grid of square tiles on a 390px phone produces tall empty interior regions while the rest of the screen scrolls. Photo capture tiles typically benefit from portrait (3:4) aspect since the captured photo will be portrait.
- **Proposed fix:** Change tile aspect ratio from 1:1 to 3:4 (portrait). Matches the captured photo orientation. Stack the 4 tiles in a 2x2 grid that fills more of the viewport.

### 212. All scroll containers reserve 110px for nav even on Break which is centered

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Across all screens > .scroll padding:58px 22px 110px
- **What breaks:** The .break-wrap uses flex centering but the underlying screen still inherits no bottom space accommodation, while the other tabs hard-code 110px of bottom padding. There's no shared design token for safe-area inset; on iOS notched devices this padding doesn't account for the home indicator.
- **Proposed fix:** Define a CSS variable --nav-space:calc(82px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) and use it across all .scroll padding-bottom values. Break screen also uses .scroll wrapper per fix #136.

### 213. Dead code references .goal-marker that does not exist in HTML

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Earnings tab > goal-track > marker positioning code
- **What breaks:** renderGoal() queries track.querySelector('.goal-marker') and sets style.left, but the .goal-marker element is never rendered. Dead code suggests an earlier design with a current-position marker that was dropped - the track now reads as just a fill with no 'you are here' indicator.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as fix #46: add the .goal-marker div to the track markup so the positioning logic shows a 'you are here' indicator.

### 214. Pc-ack button uses raw hex #C9543F not a brand token

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > formal pcard > Acknowledge button color #C9543F
- **What breaks:** The acknowledge button color is hardcoded as #C9543F multiple times in the stylesheet (also nav-badge, pc-unread). This 'urgent red' is outside the documented palette (bone/cream/espresso/clay/ochre/teal/birthday/sand). Either it should be added to :root as --alert or replaced with --clay-deep.
- **Proposed fix:** Add --alert: #C9543F to :root in the brand tokens block. Replace all hex literal usages with var(--alert). Document in the palette comment as 'Used for urgent / disciplinary actions only.'

### 215. Translate icon is an arrow path, not a translate glyph

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > Translate button cycles EN > FR > ES > EN
- **What breaks:** The icon for Translate is two squiggly paths that read as 'shuffle' or 'compare' rather than the conventional 'A 文' translate metaphor. Stylists scanning quickly will not recognize this as a language toggle on individual cards.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the icon with the standard translate glyph: 'A 文' or 'Aa あ' rendered as inline SVG text. Conventional and immediately readable as language.

### 216. Display heading hardcodes <br> before the name forcing 2-line layout

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Today tab > display heading > 'Bonjour, Zainab' line break
- **What breaks:** The h1.display contains 'Bonjour,<br><em>Zainab</em>' with a forced linebreak. For short greetings (Hi, Salut) this creates excess whitespace; for long greetings ('Good afternoon') it pushes the name far below leaving the eyebrow disconnected. Should use natural wrap.
- **Proposed fix:** Remove the <br> and let the heading wrap naturally via CSS. Use white-space:normal and max-width to allow 1-line on short greetings, 2-line on long ones.

### 217. Speaker SVG stroke color hardcoded to #A8623C bypassing currentColor

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Today tab > spk speaker icons > inline SVG stroke color
- **What breaks:** All four spk button SVGs hardcode stroke="#A8623C" (clay). On hover the parent .spk:hover svg{stroke:#fff} override applies, but theming the icon to another brand color (e.g. dark mode, future ochre variant) requires editing every inline SVG individually.
- **Proposed fix:** Change all spk SVG strokes to stroke='currentColor' and set color:--clay on .spk and color:#fff on .spk:hover. Single point of theming.

### 218. Primary CTA on active break uses ampersand entity '&amp;' that reads as &

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Break tab > breakActive > 'End early & clock back in' button label
- **What breaks:** The button label 'End early &amp; clock back in' uses an HTML entity inside button text that renders as '&' on screen. For copy quality, this could be rephrased to 'End break early' or 'Clock back in now' rather than chaining two actions with an ampersand.
- **Proposed fix:** Change button label to 'Clock back in' (single action). Drop the chained 'End early &'. Cleaner copy.
  - *New copy:* "Clock back in"

### 219. Microcopy direction reads ambiguously - 'below' could mean pi-rows or pcards

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Portal tab > pay-impact > 'Tap any pay item below to see the detail'
- **What breaks:** 'Tap any pay item below to see the detail' sits on the dark pay-impact card. 'Below' could mean the bonus/deduction pi-r rows immediately under it (which are not tappable per existing flag 100) or the pay-green/pay-red cards further down the feed. Ambiguous direction text.
- **Proposed fix:** Change microcopy to 'Tap any bonus or deduction to see how it's calculated.' Remove ambiguous 'below'. Combined with fix #100/147, every pi-r and pay-card becomes tappable.
  - *New copy:* "Tap any bonus or deduction to see how it's calculated."

### 220. No visible status-bar / notch acknowledgment in scroll padding

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** All screens > scroll padding-top:58px
- **What breaks:** The .scroll uses 58px top padding which approximates a status bar offset, but the topline content (lang toggle + avatar) sits right at this baseline. On real notched devices the lang toggle would tuck under the dynamic island. No safe-area-inset-top usage.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace fixed 58px top padding with padding-top: max(58px, env(safe-area-inset-top)). The lang toggle and avatar sit safely below the notch on real devices.

## Owner Admin (Floor Command)  `owner`

*Strategic view for Diessou: overview, revenue, register, services catalog, staff, settings.*

**274 findings · 274 fixes**

### 1. Broken --teal var — handoff button and todo checks render unstyled

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Register > Close and hand off button; Daily Brief > To-do checkboxes
- **What breaks:** CSS references var(--teal) for the 'Close and start new register' CTA background and for the completed todo checkbox fill, but --teal is never declared in :root. The browser falls back to invalid/transparent, so the green hand-off button renders with no fill (just the cream text on the dark panel) and completed todo boxes get no green tick background. The hand-off CTA — a major terminal action that closes a manager's accountability session — looks identical to a disabled or secondary control.
- **Proposed fix:** Declare --teal: #4A8579 (a deep sage that fits the warm-dark palette) in :root alongside --ochre. Apply it to .btn-handoff background and to the completed todo checkmark fill. Re-test contrast against cream text (target >= 4.5:1).
  - *New copy:* "--teal: #4A8579"

### 2. Week view's columns are stylists, not days

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Calendar > 'Week of June 8' panel > 7-column grid headers (Aminata, Zainab, Awa, Bintou, Adama, Khady, Ndeye)
- **What breaks:** The panel header says 'Week of June 8' and the tabs read 'Week / Day,' but the seven columns are stylist names — there's no day axis anywhere. A weekly calendar with no Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu/Fri/Sat/Sun is unreadable as a week view.
- **Proposed fix:** Restructure Week view to have day columns (Mon-Sun) with stylist rows on the y-axis (or vice versa, depending on stylist count). Move stylist-as-column to the Day view where it makes sense.

### 8. Floor map legend has 7 status colors, three of them adjacent on the wheel

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** recordPayout() uses String(value).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,''). Pasting '-50.00' becomes '50.00' — the negative sign is silently stripped and recorded as a positive pay-out.

No column-level time qualifier.

But only positions 1, 2, 3 are visible — so 4 and 5 may exist but be hidden, or the chip is wrong. No 'See all' or '+2 more' affordance to resolve the gap.

  - *New copy:* "Write a note before posting."

### 190. Completed to-dos cannot be deleted or archived

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Daily Brief > 'Today's to-dos' list items
- **What breaks:** Clicking a to-do toggles its done state and strikes it through, but there is no way to remove it from the list. Over time the list becomes a graveyard of crossed-out items with no archive button.

### 191. Denomination inputs accept negative numbers via paste/keyboard

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Register > 'Coins' and 'Bills' inputs
- **What breaks:** Although min=0 is set, parseInt with Math.max(0, ...) is applied, but typed values like '-5' or pasted negatives display before being parsed. Worse, the value attribute itself is never sanitized back to the input, so the user sees a number that does not match what's being calculated.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an input handler that sanitizes value on each event: strip non-digits, clamp to 0-9999, and write the cleaned value back to the input element. Reject paste with negative sign with a red border flash.
  - *Route target:* denomination input sanitizer

### 192. No multi-stylist target — must send same notice once per stylist

- **Proposed fix:** Convert the 'To' selector to a multi-select chip input. Add an 'All stylists' quick-select chip at the top. Display selected count: 'To: 3 stylists'. Send creates one log entry per recipient.
  - *New copy:* "To: 3 stylists"

### 193. Length chips can be selected before validation forces a name

### 197. Header title updates but page never scrolls back into view on small viewports

- **What breaks:** The button is styled with background:var(--teal), but --teal is never defined in :root (the warm-teal value is named --break). The browser falls back to transparent/initial, so the most important destructive CTA on the Register page renders as white text on the dark panel with no fill — managers cannot see it as a button. The done-todo checkbox on the Daily Brief uses the same undefined token and never shows the "checked" state either.
- **Proposed fix:** Define --teal in :root as the warm champagne #C9A961 (or reuse --break / --gold-soft) so the destructive CTA paints visibly against the dark panel. Apply the same fix to the .todo-item.done .tbox rule.

A manager looking for unread SMS sees two separate inboxes, picks one, and finds the counts are wrong either way (the actual data shows 3 needs-you threads). Reads like a build/merge bug, not a feature.

### 51. Pay-out can refund into the drawer by entering a negative-like string the wrong way

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Register > Pay-out > Record pay-out (with negative-by-coercion amount)
- **What breaks:** recordPayout strips non-numeric characters from poAmount but parseFloat('-50') against the original DOM value before the strip is the raw string. The min=0 attribute isn't actually present on the pay-out input (it has no inputmode/type=number), so typing '-50' gives amt=-50 and reduces regExpected by a negative — silently increasing expected drawer.
- **Proposed fix:** Set input type='number' min='0.01' step='0.01' inputmode='decimal'. In recordPayout, parseFloat then guard amt > 0 with explicit error. Strip leading minus before parse.

### 87. Concierge thread close × has both low contrast and small hit area

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

### 88. Stylist Portal composer sends with no validation — empty announcements ship

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

For a real stylist-facing channel that's a footgun — Larysa fat-fingers Send and the whole shop gets a blank push. The Brief composer has the same shape but at least its postBrief() bails on empty input.

- **Proposed fix:** Make the KPI tile clickable to open a drill-down side sheet listing the 29% of reviews that had no response, sortable by stylist with 'Reply now' inline action.
  - *Route target:* Response rate drilldown (new sub-screen: ReviewResponseList)

### 208. Sent table breaks with newline-injection in title field

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Sidebar > Stylist Portal > Composer > 'Recently sent' table > rendering
- **What breaks:** renderSent() injects s[2] (detail = title for several preset types) directly into innerHTML without escaping. A manager pasting any HTML special char in the title (or a recognition note with '&' in it) will rip out the table cell or render as markup. This is admin-only so risk is internal, but it's a real rendering bug.
- **Proposed fix:** Escape all user-supplied strings before innerHTML. Replace innerHTML assignments with textContent or use a safe template helper that escapes special chars.
  - *Route target:* renderSent escaping

### 209. Hand-off CTA uses var(--teal), an undefined token, so the button is invisible

- **What breaks:** Already flagged as #29 for the broken token, but worth flagging as a brand-system issue too: the design picked a color (teal) that isn't part of Diessou's documented palette (cream/clay/ochre + warm dark for admin). Even if --teal were defined, teal would clash with the carefully scoped warm-dark + champagne admin theme.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace --teal with --gold (champagne #C9A961) which is the documented admin accent. Update the .todo-item.done .tbox rule to the same token.

### 210. Overview 'Open to-dos' KPI is read from #ovTodos which doesn't exist on manager surfaces

- **What breaks:** renderTodos() updates document.getElementById('ovTodos') — but in manager mode, the Overview view is owner-only and hidden via display:none on the entire section, so the count node is hidden. A manager completing to-dos sees no aggregate count anywhere. The KPI exists only in the owner overview, leaving the manager with no surface to know 'how many open to-dos' globally.
- **Proposed fix:** Render the 'Open to-dos' count in the Daily Brief header for the manager role (e.g. 'Today's to-dos · 4 open'). Keep ovTodos as a hidden mirror for owner role.

A red dot on the calendar reads as 'needs attention' to anyone who just left the floor map. The semantic overload between surfaces makes the dot ambiguous.

### 213. Recognition and Coaching presets send with no pay preview but use the same Send CTA as pay actions

Pennies through dollar coins get the same visual weight as twenties and hundreds. The denominations that actually move the total are buried in the same six-row list as half-dollars.

### 223. Active sidebar item does not auto-scroll into view in the horizontal nav

### 224. Scrim handler blindly closes all three modal types regardless of which is open

Harmless today but indicates fragile state — adding a fourth modal needs every existing scrim handler updated.
- **Proposed fix:** Use a stack of open modals; scrim onclick pops the top of the stack. Single closeAll() is dropped in favor of closeTop().

## Catalog Shoot  `shoot`

*5-day photo shoot plan: daily schedule, looks to capture.*

**160 findings · 160 fixes**

### 1. Wordmark is not a link

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Top nav > Jolieden wordmark
- **What breaks:** The 'Jolieden' brand mark in the sticky top nav is a plain <span>, not an <a>. Users expect to click a wordmark to return to a home/index page; here it does nothing, so there's no way to get back to the artifact's home or to any sibling surface.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the 'Jolieden' span in an <a href='index.html'> linking to the artifact's index/home page that lists all seven surfaces. Apply the same hover treatment used on the topnav anchor links.
  - *Route target:* index.html (artifact surface index)

### 2. No links to sibling surfaces (Client, Kiosk, Stylist, Owner, Manager, Booking)

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Top nav > links row
- **What breaks:** Every top-nav link is an in-page anchor (#concept, #schedule, #menu, #shots, etc.). There is zero navigation to the other six surfaces in the artifact (Client Companion App, Station Kiosk, Stylist App, Owner Admin, Manager Admin, Public Booking Website). A reviewer landing on this page is stranded — they can only scroll inside this single document.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a second 'Surfaces' row to the topnav (above the in-page anchors) with chips linking to client.html, kiosk.html, stylist.html, owner.html, manager.html, site.html. Mark the current surface (Catalog Shoot) with .chip.on style.
  - *New copy:* "Client · Kiosk · Stylist · Owner · Manager · Booking · Catalog Shoot"

### 3. Menu card titles fall below WCAG minimum at 12.5px

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** The Menu section > Menu cards (.mcard .nm) > Card title text
- **What breaks:** The style names use 12.5px Hanken Grotesk on a 141-card grid (the entire selectable menu). Titles like 'Stitch Fulani Senegalese Twist w/ Barrel Ends (hair included)' are the primary identification info and cannot be read comfortably. At Diessou's brand standard (Fraunces displays, generous type), this is the smallest-feeling moment in the whole document.
- **Proposed fix:** Raise .mcard .nm to 14px Hanken Grotesk 600 with line-height 1.3, bump min-height to 36px so two-liners still align. Tighten the card padding from 11px 12px to 10px 12px to recover vertical space.

### 4. Photo placeholders are muddy gradients that flatten brand palette

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** The Menu section > Menu cards > .ph color block (top thumbnail strip)
- **What breaks:** The 74px 'photo' strip on every card is a dark category-color gradient (e.g. browns, espresso-on-burgundy for Artistic) with no imagery, no style icon, and no visual differentiation between categories at a glance. For a 'photo-first' artifact the absence of even a silhouette or pattern in the placeholder makes the menu feel like a generic admin list rather than the lookbook the hero promises. The Cornrows/Stitch/Hybrid/Stitch Braids gradients are nearly identical browns, so the color coding fails its own job.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the flat 74px gradient strip with a category-specific SVG silhouette icon (8 distinct line drawings: knotless braid, box braid, cornrow, twist, loc, curl, ponytail, artistic-star) at 28px centered on a paler cream-2 background. Keep one strong clay accent per category for the badge color band on the left edge so categories remain visually coded without competing browns.

### 5. Artistic look numbers display as serif '001' with no name, breaking the card pattern

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** The Menu section > .nm.art class on artistic-look cards
- **What breaks:** The 20 artistic cards show only a three-digit Fraunces serif number ('001'…'020') as the card name, with no descriptive label of what the look is. Next to fully-named menu cards in the same grid, these read as placeholders or broken data. A viewer scanning the menu cannot tell artistic 007 from artistic 014 — the entire artistic showcase is reduced to anonymous numbering.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 'workingTitle' field to each artistic style (default 'Untitled artistic look') displayed below the serif number in 12.5px Hanken. Tapping the number opens an inline rename input (same pattern as the H1 fix) so the assigned braider can name their freestyle. Persist to localStorage 'shoot:artistic'.
  - *New copy:* "Untitled — tap to name"

### 6. Day tab subtitles at 10.5px with low-contrast espresso-soft are unreadable

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Schedule section > Day tabs > .day-tab .dd (subtitle on inactive tabs)
- **What breaks:** The 'Volume open · long styles lead', 'Steady rhythm · mixed menu' etc. labels are the differentiator between days — without them the tabs are just 'Day 1, Day 2, Day 3'. At 10.5px in espresso-soft (#6A5C4D on cream paper), contrast hovers near WCAG AA failure and the type is too small to scan. The most informative copy on the tabs is the hardest to read.
- **Proposed fix:** Raise .day-tab .dd to 12px Hanken 500, change color to var(--espresso) at .8 opacity (passes AA on cream). For the active tab keep the champagne tone but at 12px / .85 opacity.

### 7. Size bars get larger as braid sizes get larger, opposite of the actual visual cue

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Sizing section > .sz bar graphic > height progression (18 → 30 → 40 → 48 → 54px)
- **What breaks:** The bars rise Micro→Jumbo, which reads as 'amount/quantity grows'. But in braiding, Micro means the smallest, thinnest braids (most individual strands) and Jumbo means the fewest, thickest braids. A client looking at the visual will read it as 'Micro = small wear, Jumbo = big wear' which is opposite to the truth (Micro is the most labor and longest-wearing — your own copy says 'Most detail, longest wear'). The graphic contradicts the caption beneath it.
- **Proposed fix:** Invert the bar heights: Micro/XS = 54px (tallest, = most braids/density), Jumbo = 18px (shortest, = fewest braids). Replace the abstract bar with a row of vertical hatch marks — many thin lines for Micro, few thick lines for Jumbo. Update the bar caption: 'Bar shows braid density, not size of style'.

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Menu section > .mcard claim toggle
- **What breaks:** The concept says 'Influencers claim a style from the full list, first claim wins' but tapping a card only flips opacity to 0.5 with no input for who claimed it, no timestamp, no waitlist. The 'claim sheet' the schedule and Roles refer to (Fatou check-in / standby list) has no surface here.
- **Proposed fix:** On 'Claim' button tap, open a bottom-sheet with an influencer picker (autocomplete against a seeded list of 30 influencer personas), 'Wait-list' option, and a timestamp. Card displays 'Claimed by @handle · 7:14 AM' once confirmed. Reuse manager.html's check-in input pattern.

### 70. Math doesn't support the rest claim

The math is tight and the copy is breezy about it.

### 96. Hardcoded scroll-padding-top doesn't match the actual sticky nav height when links wrap

### 103. Day tabs do not update document hash or browser history

- **What breaks:** Tabs swap panels correctly via showDay(), but the URL never changes. A reviewer cannot deep-link to 'Day 3' to share with the team, and the browser back button cannot undo a tab change — it jumps out of the page entirely.

- **Location:** The concept section > .stats (5-stat row at bottom)
- **What breaks:** The hero already states '121 styles · 20 artistic looks · 5 days' as pill facts. Eighty pixels later, the stats grid restates 121 / 20 / 5 plus two new numbers (30 stations, 2 on content). The repeated numerics make the page feel padded and the new info (stations, crew) gets lost in the duplication. A reviewer's eye skips the second row because it 'looks like the first row'.
- **Proposed fix:** Cut the duplicate counts (121 styles, 20 artistic, 5 days) from the stats row. Replace with 3 NEW stats that earn their slot: '~480 photos' (121 × 4 angles), '~140 person-days' (35 braiders × 4 days), '1 monitor, 1 reviewer' (Diéssou's approval queue). Keep the existing '30 stations' and '2 on content' cards.

With Fraunces available and the brand leaning warm/editorial, the crew block is the most generic moment in the document — could be Stripe's about page. No character, no Jolieden feel.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the gradient initial boxes with 56px circular illustrated portraits drawn in the Jolieden line-art style (warm clay outline on cream, single hair detail per crew member). Reuse the same illustration treatment as the Stylist App persona avatars.

### 107. Hero fact pills look like filters but have no handlers

Clicking any of them does nothing — '121 styles' should jump to #menu, '5 days' to #schedule, '20 artistic looks' to the Artistic category filter, but none have href or onclick.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert each .fact pill to an <a> anchoring to the relevant section: '121 styles' → #menu, '20 artistic looks' → #menu (sets Category=Artistic), '5 days' → #schedule, 'Salon closed' → site.html#closure-notice, 'Free for influencers' → #concept, 'Jimi & Mariam on content' → #roles. Add subtle hover state.

### 114. Day tabs lack ARIA role/aria-selected — assistive tech doesn't know they're tabs

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Schedule section > day-tab buttons
- **What breaks:** The day-tab <button>s control panel visibility but have no role='tab', no aria-selected, no aria-controls. Same for the panels (no role='tabpanel'). Screen-reader users get unlabeled buttons.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap .day-tabs in role='tablist'. Each .day-tab gets role='tab', aria-selected, aria-controls='day-panel-N'. Each .day-panel gets role='tabpanel' aria-labelledby. Add left/right arrow key handler on the tablist.

### 115. Active section is never highlighted as you scroll

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Top nav > anchor links (Concept, Schedule, The Menu, etc.)
- **What breaks:** The 10-item top nav uses smooth scroll to anchors but never marks which section the viewer is currently inside. No scroll-spy, no active class. On a long single-page plan that's the primary wayfinding cue.
- **Proposed fix:** Implement scroll-spy with IntersectionObserver: when a section enters the top viewport, the matching topnav anchor gets .on class (same clay underline as a hover). Threshold 0.3, rootMargin -74px (matches scroll-padding-top).

Wire the 'Print' icon button (flag #39) to window.print().

### 128. Day tab click handler skips the data-day index when 'on' state is stale

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Schedule section > day-tab buttons (showDay handler)
- **What breaks:** showDay() relies on element-identity comparison (b===el) to set the active tab, so any programmatic call (e.g. from a deep link or keyboard shortcut) can't set the active tab without the DOM node reference - the function has no fallback to find the tab by index.
- **Proposed fix:** Refactor showDay(i) to take only an index. Inside, find the matching tab via querySelector('.day-tab[data-day-index="'+i+'"]') instead of element identity. Add data-day-index to each tab in the generator template.

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** Roles says 20 of 35 work daily (15 rest), Concept section says 'roughly a dozen rest each day' (~12). The numbers don't line up — readers running the rotation will get different counts depending on which section they consult.
- **Proposed fix:** Reconcile to 15 rest/day. Update both copy blocks: Concept 'About 15 braiders rest each day, so most braiders work 3 or 4 of the 5 days.' Roles 'About 20 of 35 work each day; the other 15 rest.'
  - *New copy:* "About 15 braiders rest each day. Most braiders work 3 or 4 of the 5 days, not all five."

### 149. Anchor target IDs are all lowercase but section headings are Title Case — link text won't survive renaming sections

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Top nav > section anchor links
- **What breaks:** If a section heading is renamed (per the hero's 'Rename to whatever you want to call the campaign' note), the anchor IDs (#concept, #schedule) stay the same but the nav link labels go stale silently — no derivation from heading content.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as flag #105: IDs stay as is; topnav link text reads dynamically from the rendered h2 of each section on DOMContentLoaded. Renaming a section heading auto-updates the nav label.

### 150. Empty timeline rows render as just 'Time + Event' with no padding-bottom adjustment

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Schedule section > .timeline rows :: empty notes on Day 3 and Day 4
- **What breaks:** When the third row (notes) is missing, the .tl element still has margin-bottom:16px, making sparse timelines look visually broken — same vertical rhythm regardless of content.
- **Proposed fix:** Apply a smaller margin-bottom (8px instead of 16px) to .tl when the row has no .n note. Use :not(:has(.n)) selector or a JS class .tl--empty.

### 151. Codeline has overflow-x:auto but no scrollbar styling — on narrow screens the [Angle] portion clips invisibly

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Files section > .codeline filename pattern
- **What breaks:** white-space:nowrap with overflow-x:auto means on mobile (<880px) the pattern scrolls horizontally but without any visual scrollbar hint. Users won't know to swipe to see [Angle].jpg.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a custom scrollbar style (8px clay-on-cream) for .codeline. On mobile, also add a right-side gradient fade hint indicating more content. Wrap .codeline in a relative container with a ::after pseudo for the fade.

### 152. BG callout label has no description of what it represents

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Studio section > .diagram SVG > 'BG' text label
- **What breaks:** Every other studio diagram label has a description (Key softbox 45°, Fill, Rim, Camera tethered) but 'BG' is just two letters with no context. Crew members reading the diagram won't know if BG is background light, background stand, or backdrop reference.
- **Proposed fix:** Expand the diagram label to 'BG · backdrop wash light' so crew reading the diagram know exactly what BG controls. Match the verbose style of the other callouts.

### 153. 'Artistic' is in the category strip but artistic looks have a separate identity (001-020) — selecting it surfaces the 20 artistic cards without changing the page context

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Menu section > category chip strip :: 16 chips including 'Artistic'
- **What breaks:** Filtering category=Artistic shows only the 20 artistic cards, all with serif numerical names. The filter has no signal that you're now in a distinct namespace from the menu — a new visitor would think the catalog has only 20 entries.
- **Proposed fix:** When category='Artistic' is selected, swap the menu-grid heading to 'Artistic Showcase · 20 freestyle looks by the braiders, captured Day 5'. Add a context strip explaining the separate namespace.
  - *New copy:* "Artistic Showcase · 20 freestyle looks by the braiders, captured Day 5."

### 154. Day 2 starts the sizing run but Day 1 has no mention of when the sizing schedule begins

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Schedule section > Day 2 > '10:00 AM Shooting stream' note :: 'first sizing run woven in'
- **What breaks:** Sizing section claims sizes are woven throughout the week, but Day 1 timeline never references sizing — the first appearance is Day 2. Users planning Day 1 staging won't know if sizing variants should be pulled.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 'Sizing rep' row to Day 1's timeline at 2:30 PM: 'Sizing setup · pull the first anchor family's full size range (Knotless XS-Jumbo) to the studio so Day 2 starts hot.'
  - *New copy:* "2:30 PM · Sizing setup · Pull Knotless XS-Jumbo to studio so Day 2 sizing run starts hot."

### 155. 'How it works' and 'Why it holds together' both render the same panel styling — but the second is operational and the first is concept

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Concept section > grid2 panel headers
- **What breaks:** Both panels look identical and read like equal weight — there's no hierarchy showing 'How it works' is the user-facing pitch and 'Why it holds together' is internal logistics. Stakeholders skimming may treat them as redundant.
- **Proposed fix:** Restyle 'Why it holds together' with a darker espresso accent border-left (4px clay) and an 'OPS' eyebrow tag at the top. Signals it's internal logistics, not pitch.

### 156. All six facts pills look identical and clickable — no distinction between counts (121 styles) and conditions (Salon closed)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Hero section > .facts row
- **What breaks:** Visual uniformity makes counts look like filters and conditions look like sub-headers. There is no styling difference between fact types — readers can't tell at a glance which are numbers vs which are status notes.
- **Proposed fix:** Split the pill row into two visual groups: 'Counts' (numbers — styles, looks, days — use clay dot prefix) and 'Conditions' (status notes — Salon closed, Free, Crew — use champagne dot prefix). Pull the count pills to a tighter row, conditions to the row below.

### 157. html { scroll-padding-top:74px } accounts for nav but eyebrow + h2.sec stack still places eyebrow under the nav at landing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Top nav > Concept/Schedule/etc. anchor links :: smooth scroll
- **What breaks:** Section eyebrow ('The concept', 'The week', etc.) renders 10px below the topnav's bottom edge on jump — readable, but visually crammed and easy to miss as the first piece of content the user sees on landing.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as flag #83: raise scroll-padding-top to 96px and add a small margin-top to .eyebrow so the section title lands with breathing room.

### 158. Four near-identical cream tokens with no semantic differentiation

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Whole page :: CSS custom properties --cream (#FBF7EF), --paper (#FCFAF4), --cream-2 (#F4ECDD), --bone (#F1E9DB)
- **What breaks:** The palette declares --cream, --paper, --cream-2, and --bone — four shades within roughly five hex points of each other. There is no rule for when to use which, and at render they are visually indistinguishable, so the token system signals a discipline that the design does not actually have.
- **Proposed fix:** Reduce to 2 cream tokens with explicit semantic names: --paper (#FBF7EF, page background) and --paper-mute (#F4ECDD, card backgrounds and depth). Delete --cream, --cream-2, --bone. Update all usages.

### 159. Two unrelated dark blocks float on the cream page with no shared rationale

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Studio section > .diagram (dark espresso) and Files section > .codeline (also dark espresso)
- **What breaks:** The studio diagram (#28201A) and the filename codeline (#28201A) are the only dark elements on a fully cream document, but they sit in different sections with no visual relationship to each other. They read as two one-off decisions rather than a 'reference frame' treatment that could legibly mark all the locked specs in the plan.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as flag #16: reframe both dark blocks under a 'Locked reference' eyebrow treatment so they read as a system. Add a champagne 'Locked' tag to both. The dark frame becomes the intentional 'reference spec' visual language used wherever values are not negotiable.

### 160. Hovering a selected chip flips its border to clay without changing fill, looks like a glitch

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Menu section > filter chips row > on-state and hover (.chip.on no hover override)
- **What breaks:** .chip.on is solid clay fill with clay border. .chip:hover sets border to clay (same color) — so hover on a selected chip is a no-op visually except the cursor changes. Hover on a non-selected chip changes border only. There's no separate hover state for selected chips, so reviewers second-guess whether the click registered.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as flag #147: explicit .chip.on:hover state that brightens the clay (background to clay-deep, border to clay-deep), giving visible feedback that the click registered.

## Public Booking Website  `site`

*Anonymous Boulevard replacement: browse styles, pick stylist + time, enter contact info, hold deposit.*

**180 findings · 180 fixes**

### 1. Stylist picker doesn't update state or header

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 (Your chair) > stylist tiles (Mariama B., Zainab O., Ndeye F., Khady N., Any chair)
- **What breaks:** pickStyl() only toggles visual selection. It never writes the chosen stylist into cur, never updates the "with Aminata D." line in the sheet header (#bkStyl), and never updates the avatar initial. Confirming the booking always commits the originally pre-selected stylist regardless of what the client tapped.
- **Proposed fix:** In pickStyl(el, idx): assign cur.styl = idx; rebuild the stylist line via document.getElementById('bkStyl').textContent = STYL_ROSTER[idx].label; call refreshTotal(). Build STYL_ROSTER from the current style's eligible chairs (see fix for #93/#156) so the header always reflects the picked chair.

### 2. Deposit CTA skips any payment step — just closes the sheet

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Sticky footer > "Hold the chair · pay $40 deposit" CTA
- **What breaks:** confirmBook() runs closeBook() and shows a toast. There's no Stripe/Apple Pay sheet, no card entry, not even a simulated deposit confirmation screen. For a CTA that literally says "pay $40 deposit," the missing payment step makes the core booking flow feel half-built.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace confirmBook() close-and-toast with a Step 9 in-sheet confirmation card: dim steps 1-8, slide up a 'Confirm deposit' panel showing booking summary + Apple Pay / Card buttons (visual mock, no Stripe in prototype), then on tap show a full-sheet 'Chair held' confirmation screen (see #29). Reuse .styl tile pattern for the two payment-method buttons.
  - *Route target:* new in-sheet sub-screen: Confirm deposit → Chair held

### 3. Stylist picker lists only 5 stylists but gallery names 10+

**🔴 CRITICAL** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > stylist roster vs Adama T./Sokhna G./Bintou C./Awa J./Dieynaba P./Fatou C.
- **What breaks:** Sheet's Step 6 hardcodes Aminata, Mariama, Zainab, Ndeye, Khady plus 'Any chair'. The gallery surfaces Awa J., Fatou C., Bintou C., Sokhna G., Adama T., Dieynaba P. — so picking the 'Sleek Pony Wrap with Fatou C.' opens a chair picker where Fatou doesn't appear, forcing a stylist swap or 'Any chair'.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #93: dynamically generate the chair roster from the style's primary stylist + nearest peers + Any chair. All 10+ stylists in the catalog become reachable through their own style entries.

### 4. "Text us" pill goes to # — not a tel/sms link

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Top nav > Need help? Text us pill
- **What breaks:** The visually prominent "Need help? Text us" CTA in the nav is href="#". On a real phone tap it does nothing instead of launching SMS to the salon — which is the entire promise of the copy (and the AI Concierge channel).
- **Proposed fix:** Wire the pill to href='sms:+16465550100?body=Hi%20Jolieden%2C' so a phone tap launches Messages prefilled. On desktop, swap the click handler to open a small popover (reuse .toast surface pattern) explaining 'Text +1 (646) 555-0100 from your phone — Jolieden replies in seconds'.
  - *New copy:* "Text us — replies in seconds"
  - *Route target:* sms:+16465550100

### 5. Category filter pills only highlight, never filter the gallery

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Sticky filter bar > Knotless / Box braids / Fulani / Silk press / Natural set / Kids / Color & gloss pills
- **What breaks:** filt() just toggles the .on class — the inline comment even says "Demo only — production filters the grid by tag." Clicking Knotless still shows all 12 styles. A reviewer testing categorical browsing thinks the filters are broken.
- **Proposed fix:** Add data-tag attributes to each .style card (e.g. data-tag='knotless color'). In filt(), select all .style and toggle display based on whether card's data-tag contains kind, with kind='all' showing everything. Render an empty-state card ('No looks tagged Kids yet — text Jolieden to ask') when count drops to 0.

### 6. No sign-in / my bookings / staff entry point

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Global > no cross-surface navigation anywhere
- **What breaks:** There is zero linkage from the public site to any other Jolieden surface — no "Sign in," no "My bookings" for returning clients to reach the Client Companion App, no "Staff" link for stylists/owner. A returning client cannot manage an existing appointment from this surface at all.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a second pill to .nav-right: 'Sign in' linking to client.html (Client Companion App for 'My bookings') and a footer link 'Staff sign in' linking to stylist.html. Reuse the .text-us pill style for 'Sign in', and place the Staff link as a low-weight text link in the footer beside @jolieden.
  - *New copy:* "Sign in · My bookings"
  - *Route target:* client.html (primary), stylist.html (footer)

### 7. Opening price jumps $30 above the gallery's 'from' price

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 1-7 defaults vs gallery card 'from $280'
- **What breaks:** The Cherry Cola Knotless card shows 'from $280' but tapping it opens the sheet at $310 because Length defaults to Waist (+$30) before the user has touched anything. The 'from' promise is broken in the first second of the flow — a trust hit on a booking page where price is the most scrutinized number.
- **Proposed fix:** Change default cur.len from 'wst' to 'sho' (Shoulder, +$0) so the running total opens at exactly the gallery's 'from $X'. Reword Step 2 hint: 'Shoulder is the no-charge baseline'. Apply the same baseline-default rule per service type (silk press / pony default to length='na' chip — see #49).

### 8. Stylist names don't match the persona canon

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Stylist roster (gallery bylines, booking sheet stylist picker, STYLES catalog)
- **What breaks:** CLAUDE.md names Oumou D. (knotless/boho), Fatou Ciss (silk press/natural), Dieynaba D. (color) as the flagship stylists, but this surface uses Aminata D., Mariama B., Khady N., Zainab O., Ndeye F., Awa J., Sokhna G., etc. Inventing a parallel cast breaks the persona registry and means a viewer toggling to the operator/stylist surfaces will see different people staffing the same chairs.

Instead, update CLAUDE.md's persona registry to add these names as the canonical chair roster. Owner of this fix is the CLAUDE.md / personas.ts update, not the HTML.

### 9. 'Master Influencer' tier label reads as a brand mistake

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > role labels + STYLES catalog 'sty' field
- **What breaks:** Stylists are labelled 'Master Influencer', 'Senior Influencer', 'Stylist Influencer' in the underlying data and 'Master', 'Senior', 'Stylist' in the visible picker. 'Influencer' as a stylist tier is unintentional Boulevard jargon (it's a pricing-tier name in their system) leaking into client-facing copy — exactly the Boulevard-y voice this surface is supposed to replace.

### 10. Filter pills are decorative — tapping does nothing

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Sticky filter bar (All looks 121 / Knotless 34 / Box braids 22 / ...)
- **What breaks:** Eight category pills with confident counts (121, 34, 22, 14...) suggest a working filter, but `filt()` is wired only to toggle the 'on' class — the grid never changes. In a 'click the obvious CTA' prototype the most visually prominent post-hero control is a no-op, and there's no empty state for 'Kids' (1 of 12 cards) when it would visibly fail.
- **Proposed fix:** Implement actual filtering per #4. For categories that match zero cards in this 12-card demo (e.g. Kids has 1), show a 'Showing 1 of 8 Kids looks · 7 more in the full menu — text us to see them' empty-state row that doubles as a Concierge hook.

### 11. Style named after a color opens with Natural color preselected

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Hero > 'Honey Ombré Fulani' card and corresponding booking sheet defaults
- **What breaks:** 'Honey Ombré Fulani' (and 'Cherry Cola Knotless', 'Lavender Silk Press', 'Cinnamon Color Refresh') open the sheet with Color set to 'Natural'. The whole pitch of photo-first booking is that the photo pre-fills the cart — but the headline attribute of the photo (its color) is ignored, then re-charged as a paid upgrade if the user re-selects it. Confusing and feels like upsell trickery.
- **Proposed fix:** Add styleColor and styleSize to each STYLES entry (e.g. Cherry Cola Knotless → {color:'cherry', len:'sho'}, Honey Ombré → {color:'honey'}). In openBook(), preselect cur.col = s.styleColor || 'nat' and apply the .on class to that swatch. Reword Step 4 hint: 'The color in the photo is included — switch swatches to remix it'.

### 12. AI SMS Concierge — the headline differentiator — is barely a chip

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Hero > 'Need help? Text us' nav button and overall AI Concierge surface
- **What breaks:** Per the brief, the salon's SMS line is THE differentiator vs Boulevard. On this site it shows up as a single pill in the top-right ('Need help? Text us') with href='#' and no copy explaining what makes texting Jolieden different (instant AI reply, books appointments, etc). A client landing here from an Instagram ad never learns the concierge exists.

Tap-anywhere on the card opens sms:. Also expand the nav pill copy.

### 13. Drawer has no dialog semantics or focus management

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet drawer (#sheet, role/aria/focus)
- **What breaks:** The aside has no role='dialog', no aria-modal, no aria-labelledby, no focus trap, and opening it doesn't move focus inside. Swatches and add-ons are divs with onclick (not buttons) with no role='checkbox' or aria-checked, so the running total updates are invisible to screen readers. Keyboard-only users can tab through the underlying gallery while the scrim is open.
- **Proposed fix:** Add role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby='bkTitle' to #sheet. On openBook(): cache document.activeElement, move focus to .sh-close, install a focus-trap (tab loops between first/last focusable child). On closeBook(): restore focus to cached element. Convert .swatch-i, .addon, .styl, .slot to <button> with role='radio'/'checkbox' and aria-checked.

### 14. Booking 'success' is a 3-second toast, then nothing

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Confirmation flow — confirmBook() → toast → close
- **What breaks:** Tapping 'Hold the chair' just closes the sheet and flashes a toast 'Chair held — confirmation texted...'. No confirmation screen, no booking ID, no 'what happens next' (deposit charged, arrival instructions, address, what to bring). For a $40 deposit + $310 chair, this is the moment the client most needs reassurance — and it's the most under-designed moment in the flow.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the toast with a full-sheet confirmation view that swaps in over the 8-step flow: large champagne checkmark, 'You're booked, Imani' headline (Fraunces italic), booking ID 'JLD-2604-1147', what-happens-next list (deposit charged · arrival prep · address · what to bring), 'Add to calendar' + 'Text us if anything changes' CTAs. Reuse the .style-hero pattern at top showing the booked look photo.

### 15. Bookable Sunday slot contradicts posted hours

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 7 'Pick a slot' > 'Sun Nov 9 · 12:00p' slot vs Footer > 'Tue–Sat 9–8' hours
- **What breaks:** The slot picker offers a Sunday slot (Sun Nov 9 · 12:00p) as bookable, but the footer states the salon is open Tue–Sat only. A client can hold the chair for a day the salon is closed.
- **Proposed fix:** Hard-filter generated slots against the salon schedule (Tue–Sat). Remove Sun Nov 9 from the static slot grid in markup and replace with the next eligible day. Add a SCHEDULE = {tue:[9,20], wed:[9,20], ...} const at top of the script so any future slot generation respects it.

### 16. Step 6 always pre-selects Aminata D., regardless of style

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > pre-selected stylist tile + hint 'Pre-selected from the photo'
- **What breaks:** The stylist grid is hard-coded so Aminata D. is the .on tile for every style. Open the Lavender Silk Press (byline 'with Zainab O.') and Step 6 still highlights Aminata D. while the header line reads Zainab O. — header and pre-selection disagree.
- **Proposed fix:** In openBook(), find the stylist tile whose data-name matches STYLES[idx].sty's first segment, remove .on from all tiles, and add .on to the matched one. If no match (Adama T. / Dieynaba P.), add the stylist to the picker dynamically (see #93/#156).

### 17. Silk press / pony / color styles still show 'Size of braid' as Step 1

- **What breaks:** The same 8-step form runs for every style. Opening Lavender Silk Press, Sleek Pony Wrap, or Cinnamon Color Refresh still shows 'Size of braid' (XS / Small / Medium / Large) as Step 1 — irrelevant choices that a silk-press client doesn't have.
- **Proposed fix:** Add styleType to each STYLES entry (braid | silk | pony | natural | color | locs | kids). Per type, hide irrelevant steps in openBook() by toggling .step display:none. Silk press / pony / color skip stepSize and stepParting; keep stepLength but relabel ('Finish length') and reprice.

### 18. Hard-coded November dates inside an April-anchored demo

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **What breaks:** Every slot reads 'Sat Nov 8 / Sun Nov 9 / Tue Nov 11 / Wed Nov 12 / Fri Nov 14' but the rest of the artifact is anchored to TODAY=2026-04-14. A reviewer scanning across surfaces sees the booking widget offering dates seven months in the past (or future, depending on year) and loses trust that the demo is internally consistent.
- **Proposed fix:** Generate slots dynamically from TODAY = '2026-04-14': render the next 5 eligible days (Tue–Sat) starting Wed Apr 15, with 2 slots per day. Replace the static slot markup with a slotGrid.innerHTML = generateSlots(TODAY) call in openBook().

### 19. Braid-specific step shown for silk press, pony, twist-out, color refresh

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **What breaks:** Step 1 'Size of braid' and Step 3 'Parting' appear unconditionally — including when the user taps 'Lavender Silk Press', 'Sleek Pony Wrap', 'Two-Strand Twist Out', or 'Cinnamon Color Refresh'. None of those services have a braid size. Defaulting Medium and charging +$0 for an option that doesn't physically exist makes the price line look arbitrary.

Replace with type-specific micro-steps: silk press → 'Finish' (Sleek / Voluminous / Bumped); color → 'Tone' (Warm / Cool / Neutral).

### 20. Length-modifier prices apply equally to a 1.5-hr pony as to a 9-hr knotless set

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 2 'Length' modifiers (Bob −$30 … Hip +$50)
- **What breaks:** The length deltas (Bob −$30, Mid-back +$15, Waist +$30, Hip +$50) are hard-coded in JS and run on every service. A $120 'Sleek Pony Wrap' opens at Waist +$30 = $150 even though pony length isn't actually a customer-chosen variable. The math is internally consistent but produces nonsense quotes.
- **Proposed fix:** Move LEN_PX from a flat const to per-styleType maps: LEN_PX_BY_TYPE = {braid:{bob:-30,...}, silk:{bob:-15,sho:0,mid:15,wst:0,hip:0}, pony:{na:0}, kids:{kid:0}}. Pony shows a single 'Standard' chip with no upcharge.

### 21. Hero promises a tap-and-done flow the sheet immediately violates

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Hero > headline 'Tap a look. We'll do the rest.'
- **What breaks:** Headline copy says 'Tap a look. We'll do the rest.' but tapping a look produces an 8-step configurator with size, length, parting, color, add-ons, stylist, slot, and contact form. The voice and the actual flow contradict each other — either the headline is dishonest or the sheet should default to one-tap-confirm with optional refinement.
- **Proposed fix:** Restructure the sheet to a 2-tier model: top half = 'Book as shown' single-tap CTA with the photo's defaults visible as a summary card ('Cherry Cola Knotless · Medium · Saturday 11a · $280 · with Aminata'). Bottom half collapses to an 'Adjust this look' accordion that exposes the 8 steps. Default is one-tap; adjustment is opt-in.

### 22. Twelve external CDN images with no width/height, alt text, or lazy hint

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Gallery > style cards > background images (g-1 through g-12)
- **What breaks:** All twelve photos are CSS background-images pulled from joliedensbeautybar.com's Shopify CDN. No <img> elements means no alt text (the entire visual product menu is invisible to screen readers), no lazy-loading, no aspect-ratio reservation prior to load (handled by CSS aspect-ratio, but only the layout — the photos themselves block-load all twelve on initial paint).
- **Proposed fix:** Convert background-images to <img> elements inside .style-photo with src=, alt='{styleName} on {model description}' (e.g. 'Cherry Cola Knotless on a dark-skinned model, mid-back length'), width='400' height='500', loading='lazy' on all except the first 3 (eager). Same treatment for the .style-hero inside the sheet.

### 23. Scrim dismiss discards selections silently like the × button

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > scrim backdrop (#scrim) > tap-outside-to-dismiss
- **What breaks:** Tapping the dark backdrop fires closeBook() with no confirm — easy to do by accident on mobile and you lose every step you filled in. The × close button at least looks like a deliberate action; the scrim feels like an empty area.
- **Proposed fix:** Route both the scrim onclick and × onclick through a single closeAttempt() function that runs the unsaved-changes confirm from #9. Don't bypass it on either path.

### 24. 'Included' add-on is actually togglable off

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 'Add-ons' > Wash & deep condition row toggle
- **What breaks:** The Wash row says 'Always included' and shows 'Included' in the price slot, but toggle(this) still runs on click — tapping it removes 'wash' from cur.addons and unchecks the box. The user can deselect a service the copy promises is mandatory.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #16: remove the toggle handler from the wash row entirely. Render it as a non-interactive .addon.locked (no .check, no hover, no onclick) with 'Included' in teal italic. cur.addons.wash stays true permanently.

### 25. Stylist picker never writes the chosen stylist to state

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > pickStyl() function body
- **What breaks:** pickStyl(el, idx) only toggles the .on class — it never assigns cur.styl = idx or updates STYLES[cur.idx].sty. The running total, header line, hero badge, and confirmation toast all still reference the originally pre-selected stylist regardless of what the user tapped.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as #5 — pickStyl(el, idx) must assign cur.styl=idx, update #bkStyl text from a STYL_ROSTER[idx].label, and call refreshTotal(). Ensure idx is used (currently discarded — see #83).

### 26. Edited contact info is never persisted

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 8 > contact input fields > onchange / oninput handlers
- **What breaks:** If the user changes First name / Last name / Mobile / Notes, nothing reads the new values. confirmBook() uses a hard-coded toast '(646) 555-0123' instead of the field value. Editing the form is purely cosmetic.
- **Proposed fix:** Add oninput='cur.contact.{field}=this.value' (or jsx equivalent) to each input. Use cur.contact in confirmBook() and the confirmation screen (per #29). Save to localStorage on first valid entry for future returning-client autofill.

### 27. Cards have role onclick but no keyboard / role=button

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Gallery > all 12 style cards (.style elements)
- **What breaks:** Each .style is a div with onclick — no tabindex, no role='button', no keydown handler. Keyboard users can't reach the gallery and screen readers don't announce them as actionable. The entire primary entry point to booking is mouse-only.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert each .style <div onclick> to <button class='style' onclick> (the styling already works on button with appearance:none). Adds keyboard, focus ring, and screen-reader 'button' announcement. Add aria-label='{styleName} · {duration} · from ${price} — open booking'.

### 28. Stylist roster is hard-coded — doesn't match the style's stylist

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > stylist roster (Aminata D., Mariama B., Zainab O., Ndeye F., Khady N.)
- **What breaks:** Even though styles 7 and 11 are by Adama T. and Dieynaba P. (per STYLES catalog), the Step 6 stylist roster always shows the same 5 named stylists. So the 'preselected from the photo' hint can't be true — Adama/Dieynaba/etc. aren't even in the grid to be selected.
- **Proposed fix:** Build the Step 6 roster dynamically in openBook(): take the style's primary stylist + 3 nearest tier-peers + Any chair. Render via stylGrid.innerHTML so styles with Adama T. (Apprentice) or Dieynaba P. (Color) actually surface that chair as the preselected tile.

### 29. Toast hardcodes (646) 555-0123 regardless of input

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Confirmation toast > 'Chair held — confirmation texted to (646) 555-0123 💛'
- **What breaks:** The confirmation message reads back a hardcoded number even if the user types a different mobile. If a real client edits the prefilled phone, the toast confirms to the wrong number — a trust-shattering moment at the booking finish line.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #29+#78: replace toast with the confirmation screen, sourcing the mobile from cur.contact.mobile. Toast (where retained for save events) reads dynamic strings.

### 30. Chips/swatches/slots have no keyboard focus styles

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > all eight steps > tab/keyboard order
- **What breaks:** Buttons rely on hover for affordance. There is no :focus-visible ring on .chip, .swatch-i, .slot, or .styl. A keyboard or AT user tabbing through cannot see which option they're on, making the entire eight-step flow unusable without a mouse.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a unified focus rule: .chip:focus-visible, .swatch-i:focus-visible, .slot:focus-visible, .styl:focus-visible, .pill:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--ochre); outline-offset:3px; border-radius:inherit }. Convert swatch-i and addon from div to button so they receive focus.

### 31. Add-on checkboxes aren't real checkboxes

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 'Add-ons' > .check pseudo-element checkmarks
- **What breaks:** Each add-on row is a <div> with onclick. The .check square is purely visual — no role='checkbox', no aria-checked, no input. Screen readers announce 'Previous-style takedown +$60' as static text with no toggle state.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert each .addon div to <button role='checkbox' aria-checked='false' onclick>. Sync aria-checked in toggle(). Screen readers now announce 'Beads & charms · checkbox · not checked · +$30'.

### 32. Phone field doesn't mention the AI Concierge

- **What breaks:** This is the single point in the entire booking flow where Jolieden captures the phone she'll text. The placeholder says 'we text confirmation' and stops there — missing the natural moment to introduce the SMS Concierge ('reply STOP anytime · text us back any time before your visit'). The headline differentiator goes unintroduced.

  - *New copy:* "Mobile · so we can text you / Reply to our text anytime — Jolieden's concierge answers in seconds. Text STOP to opt out."

### 33. Bob length applied to styles where it's nonsensical

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **What breaks:** Tapping the 'Sleek Pony Wrap' style opens with Step 2 still offering Bob/Shoulder/Mid-back/Waist/Hip — but a pony has no length category, it's a ponytail. The same step also breaks on the Kids Mini Twists ($95 base) where Hip-length doesn't exist.

### 34. Choosing 'Cherry Cola Knotless' doesn't pre-select Cherry Cola swatch

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **What breaks:** Opening Style 0 named 'Cherry Cola Knotless' opens with Color: Natural pre-selected. The style name promises a specific color but the form starts at the wrong swatch, requiring the client to manually re-pick what the photo already chose for them.

### 35. Form inputs have placeholders but no associated labels

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 8 > inputs lack <label> elements
- **What breaks:** Every input in Step 8 relies solely on placeholder text for identification. Once the user clicks in, the field appears nameless. Screen readers announce the prefill values with no context, and autofill can't reliably map fields without aria-label or proper for/id pairs.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as #76: add visible <label> with for/id pairs above each input, styled as 10.5px uppercase Hanken bold (matching .step-label). Placeholders remain as example values, not labels.

### 36. Scrim click discards work; no confirm dialog

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **What breaks:** Tapping anywhere outside the drawer instantly closes it and wipes selections. Combined with the lack of Escape handling and × close behavior, the client has three ways to lose work and zero guardrails. On a mobile booking flow that has reached step 6 of 8, this is a recipe for abandoned bookings.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #9/#66/#118: route all dismiss paths through closeAttempt(), which shows the inline save-or-discard strip if cur differs from defaults.

### 37. Takedown add-on adds $60 but does not add the advertised hour to duration

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 Add-ons > 'Previous-style takedown' row description ('An hour to remove the current set')
- **What breaks:** The takedown add-on's description promises 'An hour to remove the current set before we start', but the running total's duration tag (`<small>· ${s.dur}</small>`) only reads STYLES[idx].dur — a 6 hr style with takedown still shows 6 hrs. The client will be told 6 hrs and end up sitting 7.
- **Proposed fix:** In refreshTotal(), parse styleDur to a number, add 1 if addons.has('takedown'), and write back '{dur} hrs' to #bkDur and every slot's duration. Same logic powers #17.

### 38. Color swatches use <div> with onclick — not keyboard focusable, not announced as buttons

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 Color > swatch-i divs
- **What breaks:** Every chip in steps 1/2/3 is a <button>, but Step 4's swatches are <div class='swatch-i' onclick='...'> with no role, tabindex, or button semantics. Keyboard users cannot reach or activate any color choice. Screen readers announce them as static text.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert .swatch-i divs to <button role='radio' aria-checked='true|false' name='color' tabindex='0'>. Wrap the swatch group in role='radiogroup' aria-label='Color'. Keyboard arrow-key navigation between swatches via a single keydown handler.

### 39. Add-on rows use <div onclick> instead of buttons — not keyboard accessible

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 Add-ons > .addon rows
- **What breaks:** Each addon is a <div onclick='toggle(this)'> with no role='checkbox', no aria-checked, and no tabindex. Keyboard-only users cannot toggle add-ons. Screen reader users hear plain text and have no way to know they're interactive.
- **Proposed fix:** Convert .addon to <button role='checkbox' aria-checked='false' tabindex='0'>. The .check span becomes purely visual; aria-checked carries the state. Already specified in #98.

### 40. Slot buttons lack aria-pressed / role=radio — toggle state invisible to screen readers

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 7 'Pick a slot' > slot buttons missing aria-pressed
- **What breaks:** All six .slot buttons use only a CSS .on class to indicate selection. There's no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radio-group semantics. Blind users cannot tell which slot they have selected after pressing Tab away and back.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap .slot-grid in role='radiogroup' aria-label='Time slots'. Each .slot becomes role='radio' aria-checked='true|false', toggled in pickSlot().

### 41. STYLES[10] 'Adama T. · Apprentice' role label doesn't appear in any picker tile

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** The kids style's stylist is labeled 'Apprentice' in STYLES, but the only role labels in the stylist picker tiles are Master, Senior, Stylist, and 'First open'. Apprentice never renders. The client cannot pick Adama T. in step 6 for the kids style — she's not in the grid.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #93: roster is built dynamically from the style, so Adama T. (Apprentice) renders as the preselected tile when Kids Mini Twists opens. Add 'Apprentice' to the .styl-role copy variants.

### 42. confirmBook() closes the sheet before showing the toast — toast becomes the only feedback, easily missed

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > confirmBook() function
- **What breaks:** confirmBook() calls closeBook() FIRST, then toast(...). The sheet slides out, the scrim fades, and a small pill toast appears at the bottom. A user who closed the sheet without booking gets the same visual outcome (sheet gone) as a user who booked. Critical state change is conflated with dismissal.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #29: replace closeBook+toast with an in-sheet confirmation screen that the sheet transitions to. The sheet does not close until the user dismisses the confirmation, so the success state is impossible to miss.

### 43. stylSel and stylSelName ids appear only on the first tile (Aminata D.) — break when picker re-renders

**🟠 HIGH** · `NAV` · round 4

- **What breaks:** The first .styl button has id='stylSel' on its avatar and id='stylSelName' on its name span. If openBook() ever updates the pre-selected stylist (to match STYLES[idx].stylInit), document.getElementById('stylSel') updates only the FIRST tile — even when the user opens 'Honey Ombré Fulani' with stylInit:'M'. Hard-coded id targeting prevents the picker from ever syncing to the chosen style.

### 44. Takedown description claims 'an hour' but adds no time to running total

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 'Add-ons' > 'Previous-style takedown' description
- **What breaks:** Add-on advertises an hour of extra service time, yet the running total's duration field never updates from the style default. A client choosing takedown expects to see the slot extended; the duration silently lies.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #122: refreshTotal() computes duration including takedown surcharge. The bkDur badge and all slot durations update to {styleDur + 1} when takedown is on.

### 45. Add-on row click handler triggers on full-width div but no role/aria-checked

**🟠 HIGH** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** .addon is a div with onclick='toggle(this)' — not a button, no role='checkbox', no aria-checked. Screen reader users hear unlabeled clickable text with no state. The checkmark .check span has no semantic toggle indication.

### 46. Selected slot's clay-soft background fails AA contrast on the espresso text

### 49. Phone field accepts non-tel input but pretends to validate via placeholder copy

- **What breaks:** Placeholder reads 'Mobile · we text confirmation' — implying SMS validation. Field is plain text input with no pattern, type='tel', or inputmode='tel'. Mobile keyboards open QWERTY instead of numeric keypad. The placeholder copy promises something the field can't deliver.

### 51. Contact form has no validation, no per-field submit handler

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 1

### 55. Time-slot durations are hard-coded — they lie when config changes

### 61. Pills, chips, and swatches all sit below the 44x44 touch target floor

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

### 62. Footer hours and links underdeliver for a booking landing page

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 1

This footer says only the address, hours (with no acknowledgment that Sun/Mon are closed), phone, and '@jolieden' (not linked). The 48-hr cancellation policy lives only as a 11px italic line inside the booking drawer.
- **Proposed fix:** Expand footer to a 3-column row (mobile: stacked): col 1 = address + hours + 'Closed Sun–Mon' + transit ('2 to 135 St · 11 mins'); col 2 = Policies (Cancellation · Deposit · Late · FAQ — each links to a /policy/[slug] sheet that reuses .sheet pattern); col 3 = Contact ((646) 555-0100 tel: + @jolieden instagram).

### 63. Hero photo badges (price + duration) never update with selections

### 65. Phone input has no type='tel' or autocomplete

### 66. Booking confirmation toast is invisible to screen readers

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Toast notification '#toast' after confirmBook() (no aria-live / role='status')
- **What breaks:** The toast that announces 'Chair held — confirmation texted...' has no role='status' or aria-live attribute. Screen reader users tap Hold the chair, the sheet closes silently, and they receive no confirmation that anything happened.
- **Proposed fix:** Add role='status' and aria-live='polite' to #toast. Since #29 replaces the toast with a confirmation screen, ensure that screen's heading is focused (h1 with tabindex='-1', .focus() on render) so screen readers announce 'You're booked'.

The pre-selected first slot is just the topmost — there's no affordance for 'show me only Aminata's chair' or 'next 48 hrs'. A client who actually wanted to book quickly has to read every tile.

- **What breaks:** Names like 'Ndeye F.', 'Dieynaba P.', 'Sokhna G.', 'Honey Ombré' all carry French/Wolof phonetics but the document declares lang='en' with no inline lang spans. VoiceOver/NVDA read them with English phonemes, producing 'En-day-ay' for Ndeye. A brand built on Senegalese stylist identity should preserve that in the assistive layer.

The header and the picker disagree.

### 77. Page body scroll isn't locked when the sheet is open

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 3

- **What breaks:** openBook() never sets document.body.style.overflow='hidden' or equivalent. Scrolling inside the sheet bleeds through to the gallery underneath, especially on mobile where the sheet is 98% of the viewport but the body can still scroll behind it.
- **Proposed fix:** In openBook(): document.body.style.overflow='hidden'; document.body.style.touchAction='none'. In closeBook(): restore both to ''. Save scroll position before lock and restore on close (window.scrollTo(0, savedY)).
