### 101. Hero stats are static strings — never recompute, can lie on a Monday morning

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Hero > .hero-strip > '8 chairs free this weekend' (data source)
- **What breaks:** The strip says 'Harlem · open today', '121 looks on the menu', '8 chairs free this weekend' as plain HTML text. If the file is served on a closed Sunday or after capacity sells out, the copy still claims 8 chairs free and 'open today'. No data binding.
- **Proposed fix:** Generate hero-strip values at render time from a SCHEDULE const + TODAY=2026-04-14: 'open today · {hoursForToday}' if open, 'closed today · open {nextOpenDay}' if closed. Photos copy reads 'updated weekly'. Drop the dynamic chair-count entirely (per #20).

### 102. Closing the sheet doesn't restore focus or scroll-into-view to the originating gallery card

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Page > body > scroll position when sheet closes
- **What breaks:** After closeBook(), keyboard users have no focus anchor — focus is lost to <body>. The clicked gallery card is no longer in the viewport if the user scrolled inside the sheet. Tab order restarts from the top of the page.
- **Proposed fix:** Save the trigger element in openBook(): cur.trigger = document.activeElement (or the clicked card if onclick provides 'this'). In closeBook(): cur.trigger?.focus({preventScroll:false}); cur.trigger?.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}).

### 103. Two adjacent buttons with identical .d label ('Sat Nov 8') and only time differing — easy to mis-tap

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 7 slot buttons > duplicate dates 'Sat Nov 8' (11:00a) and 'Sat Nov 8' (2:00p)
- **What breaks:** The slot grid renders 'Sat Nov 8 11:00a' and 'Sat Nov 8 2:00p' as visually-identical-looking tiles (date is the bold .d field, time is small grey .t). At a glance the two cards read 'Sat Nov 8 / Sat Nov 8' — clients tapping quickly will land on the wrong one.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as #91: invert visual hierarchy — time becomes the dominant Fraunces row, day becomes the supporting line. Or group same-day slots under one .slot-day header with time chips beneath.

### 104. Kids style resets addons to only 'wash' — including grown-up addons like 'Color gloss after braids'

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > resetSelections > addon-on logic for STYLES[10] 'Kids Mini Twists'
- **What breaks:** When openBook(10) fires (Kids Mini Twists with Bows), resetSelections() leaves all five addons present in the DOM — Color gloss, Beads, Edges, Takedown all visible. Kids shouldn't be upsold a color gloss. The fix is to filter rendered addons per style; the current code doesn't.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #51: ADDONS_BY_TYPE.kids omits color gloss, takedown, edge styling. Only Beads, Bows, Wash (locked). Rebuild stepAddons.innerHTML on each openBook from the per-type list.

### 105. Form input values are hardcoded in HTML — re-opening the sheet does not reset them, but openBook never re-initializes them either

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 8 contact inputs > value attributes
- **What breaks:** The four input fields have value='Amara' / 'Niang' / phone / notes hardcoded in the HTML. openBook() never clears or sets these values. If a hypothetical user edited the name to 'Jane' in one booking attempt, opened a different style, the form would still show 'Jane' — yet the confirmation toast hardcodes (646) 555-0123. State is fully orphaned from the form.
- **Proposed fix:** Move prefill values out of HTML into a CONTACT_DEFAULTS const. openBook() writes defaults to each input from CONTACT_DEFAULTS unless cur.contact has been edited by the user this session. cur.contact persists across openings within one session.

### 106. Gallery card click target is the entire card, including the corner tag — tag click also opens the sheet

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Gallery > each .style card > onclick handler
- **What breaks:** The 'New' / 'Most loved' / 'Color' / 'Kids' tag pills sit inside the .style-photo, which sits inside the .style with onclick. Tapping the tag (a span) bubbles to the card and opens the booking sheet, even though the tag visually looks like a filter chip. Combined with issue 36's note that tags don't filter — tapping a tag does the opposite of what it suggests.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #36: tags become inner <button> elements with event.stopPropagation() that route to the matching filter pill. The card opens booking only when the user taps the photo or meta region.

### 107. confirmBook fires closeBook before toast — toast can be missed

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > confirmBook() / closeBook() sequence
- **What breaks:** confirmBook() calls closeBook() then toast(). Because the sheet slides out (.35s transition) while the toast appears, the user's eye follows the sheet motion; the small bottom toast is easy to miss in peripheral vision, especially on mobile where the sheet slides down past the toast.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #29+#137: replace toast with confirmation screen. The sheet transitions to the confirmation screen in place, no slide-out, no toast race condition.

### 108. Sticky footer gradient mask hides bottom of contact form

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky footer .sh-foot > linear-gradient mask
- **What breaks:** The .sh-foot uses linear-gradient(rgba 0 -> cream 30%). Scrolled content above (Step 8 contact inputs) fades into the cream gradient before being covered by the footer — making the 'Anything we should know' input look semi-transparent or cut off while the user is typing.
- **Proposed fix:** Add padding-bottom:120px to .sh-body so the last input's bottom edge sits above the gradient's start. Alternatively replace the gradient mask with a solid border-top + drop-shadow so it doesn't fade content.

### 109. Sticky sheet header doesn't include step counter or back affordance

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky header .sh-head h2 + stylist-line
- **What breaks:** On a tall sheet with 8 steps, after scrolling to Step 8 the user has no way to know they're 'almost done' or how to jump back. The sticky header only shows style name + stylist — no progress or navigation.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #22+#111: add a 4-dot progress indicator + 'Step n of 4' caption in the sticky header. Add a back-step button (left of the × close) that scrolls the sheet to the previous section when not on the first one.

### 110. Stylist tier in tile (Master/Senior/Stylist) doesn't match catalog 'Master Influencer'

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 stylist 'role' label vs STYLES catalog 'sty' field
- **What breaks:** Tiles show short tier ('Master', 'Senior', 'Stylist') while #bkStyl header shows full 'Master Influencer'. Two formats for same data create reader friction — and worse, when a stylist is swapped the header text isn't even updated to match the new tile.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #14+#116: short tiers everywhere ('Master Stylist', 'Senior Stylist', 'Stylist', 'Apprentice', 'Color Specialist'). Update STYLES.sty and styl-role copy to one canonical form.

### 111. Duration small text reads as multiplier next to dollar amount

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky footer total > #bkTotal innerHTML small element
- **What breaks:** Total renders '$310 · 6 hrs' where '· 6 hrs' uses 13px italic small. At a glance the dot reads like a math operator — '$310 x 6 hrs' or '$310 per 6 hrs' confusing the per-hour vs total semantics. No clear 'Total · est. duration' label split.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an explicit '·' separator and break the total into two labelled rows: 'Total $310' (large Fraunces) above, 'Est. 6 hrs at the chair' (12px Hanken muted) below. Removes any 'per-hour' ambiguity.

### 112. Smaller braid size is the most expensive but priced like an add-on

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 1 chip 'XS +$40' price hierarchy
- **What breaks:** XS shows '+$40' as a small subscript ('.px') with .7 opacity. The chip looks like 'XS' with a faint price modifier — readers parse the size choice without absorbing the cost until total updates. Largest upcharge on the screen is the least visually emphasized.
- **Proposed fix:** Bump .chip .px font-size to 12.5px (same as chip body) and remove opacity:.7. Smaller sizes' price chips become visually prominent rather than hidden. Pair with the explanatory line from #56.

### 113. style-hero background-color fallback (#3a261a) flashes before image loads

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > .style-hero background image inheritance
- **What breaks:** .style-photo, .style-hero{background-color:#3a261a} acts as a fallback. Opening the sheet on a slow connection shows a dark brown rectangle for several seconds before the CDN photo paints — clashes with the cream sheet and reads as a loading error, not a brand background.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the background-color fallback to var(--panel) (cream-adjacent) so the loading state blends with the sheet. Add a shimmer skeleton (CSS linear-gradient animation) over .style-hero while the photo loads, then transition out on image onload.

### 114. Swatch labels wrap by hand with <br> — overflow on long names

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 'Color' > swatch labels with <br>+price
- **What breaks:** 'Honey ombré<br>+$20' is hardcoded. On viewports where '.swatch-i' min-width:62px is enforced, 'Cherry Cola<br>+$35' renders 'Cherry' / 'Cola' / '+$35' as three lines because 62px isn't wide enough for 'Cherry Cola'. The <br> only handles the price split — name still wraps unpredictably.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #25+#80+#99: switch to two-span structure, set .swatch-i min-width:84px (wide enough for 'Cherry Cola' on one line), use font-size:11px tabular for prices.

### 115. 'Any chair' button is keyboard-focusable but reads identically as a stylist

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > 'Any chair' tile button structure
- **What breaks:** All tiles use <button class='styl'>. To a screen reader, 'Any chair · First open' announces as 'Any chair, First open, button' — indistinguishable from a person's name. No semantic separation between 'pick a person' and 'pick first available'.
- **Proposed fix:** Set aria-label='Any chair · first available open · expands slot options' on the Any-chair tile. Add a leading icon (chair SVG) so screen readers and sighted users get the same 'not a person' signal.

### 116. 'Open today' has no day-of-week or hours — meaningless on Sundays

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Hero > 'Tap a look. We'll do the rest.' + hero-strip 'open today'
- **What breaks:** Footer claims 'Tue–Sat 9–8'. Hero says 'open today' with green dot. If 'today' is Sunday or Monday, the dot lies — there's no day-aware logic. As a static page the indicator is always green regardless of actual hours.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #133: render hero-strip from a SCHEDULE const + TODAY. 'Open today · 9 to 8' when open, 'Closed today · open Tuesday 9' when closed. Status dot color flips from teal (open) to ochre (closed).

### 117. Horizontal scroll filters have no scroll indicator or fade

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Sticky filter bar > scroll behavior on mobile
- **What breaks:** .filters uses overflow-x:auto with scrollbar-width:none. On mobile with 8 pills, only 3-4 fit before the right edge cuts off. No fade gradient, no scroll affordance, no arrow — users may not realize 'Color & gloss' exists past 'Kids'.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 24px right-edge gradient fade (.fbar::after with linear-gradient to var(--cream)) when content overflows. Add a small chevron-right indicator that fades out as the user scrolls right. Also add scroll-snap-type: x mandatory so pills snap into view.

### 118. Close × uses font-weight:300 thin character — looks like decoration not control

**🟡 MEDIUM** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **What breaks:** .sh-close uses font-size:24px with font-weight:300 — the × glyph at thin weight reads as a typographic ornament rather than a tap target. Combined with no border, no hover background, and color:--espresso-soft, users may overlook it.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace × with an inline SVG close icon (1.5px stroke, 18px). Add visible 36x36 hit area with a hover background (.panel). Tighter affordance, AA-compliant target.

### 119. Brand wordmark links to # (dead-end)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **What breaks:** The JOLIEDEN logo in the top nav is an <a href="#"> that does nothing. Users expecting it to scroll-to-top or return home get no response — and there's no other nav to land back on the home view.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the .brand <a href='#'> to href='/' (scrolls to top, returns home view). Add onclick that calls window.scrollTo({top:0,behavior:'smooth'}) for in-page consistency.

### 120. Instagram handle link goes nowhere

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

### 121. Escape key does not close the sheet

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > global
- **What breaks:** There's no keydown handler for Escape. Keyboard users have to mouse over to the × or click outside the sheet. The scrim click works, but Esc — the expected modal-dismiss key — does nothing.
- **Proposed fix:** Add document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if(e.key==='Escape' && document.getElementById('sheet').classList.contains('show')) closeBook(); }). Pair with the unsaved-changes confirm from #9.

### 122. Swatch labels stack inconsistently and 'Natural' has no price line

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 swatches and color labels
- **What breaks:** Five of six swatches show 'Name<br>+$X', but 'Natural' just shows 'Natural' (no '+$0' line), so the rows have different heights and the price ladder doesn't read as a price ladder. The 38x38 swatch + 10.5px label is also below the recommended 44x44 touch target.
- **Proposed fix:** Restructure swatch labels to two <span> children with fixed heights: .lab-name (always shown) and .lab-px (always shown, even if empty — render 'Included' for Natural in teal italic instead of blank). Bump .sw to 44x44, .swatch-i min-width to 72px to satisfy 44x44 touch target.

### 123. Byline format is inconsistent — sometimes leads with a size, sometimes not

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 1

- **What breaks:** Some cards say 'Medium · with X' or 'Hip-length · with Y', others just say 'with Z'. The size word is the default config not a distinguishing fact — Cherry Cola at Medium is the same as Boho Knotless at Waist in terms of meaning. This makes the grid scan inconsistent and the bylines feel arbitrary.
- **Proposed fix:** Standardize all bylines to 'with {Stylist}' only — drop the size token from the byline (it's already in the booking sheet). Move duration to where size used to be to keep the line informative: 'with Aminata D. · 6 hrs'.

### 124. Card status tags are decorative — no filter or detail jump

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **What breaks:** The tag chips on gallery cards (New, Most loved, Color, Kids) sit on top of the card and look tappable, but the entire card just calls openBook(idx). There is no way to view all 'New' looks or all 'Most loved' — even though the filter pills could plausibly host this.
- **Proposed fix:** Make tag chips real <button> elements with stopPropagation that route to the matching filter pill (e.g. tap 'Color' tag → click the Color & gloss pill). For 'New' and 'Most loved', add corresponding curated-shelf pills to the .fbar (so all tags map 1:1 to a filter).

### 125. Two different phone numbers shown side-by-side

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Footer > (646) 555-0100 tel link vs Booking sheet > Step 8 mobile field prefill '(646) 555-0123'
- **What breaks:** The footer dials (646) 555-0100 (the salon) while the Step 8 contact form pre-fills (646) 555-0123 (the persona). They look like the same number at a glance; a client glancing at the form might assume that's the salon's line and dial it.
- **Proposed fix:** Change the contact-form prefill to a clearly non-salon format: '(646) 555-0144' (the persona's, per #26 update). In Step 8, add a 5px champagne 'your number' chip overlay on the input to disambiguate from the footer salon number.

### 126. Deposit amount hard-coded three times — no kids/lower-tier deposit

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky footer > deposit line '$40 deposit holds the chair' + CTA + total row
- **What breaks:** The $40 deposit is written into deposit-line copy, the CTA template, and the running total subtitle as a fixed string. For the Kids Mini Twists style (base $95), a $40 deposit is >40% of the bill — there's no way for the salon to scale the deposit per service tier.
- **Proposed fix:** Make deposit a derived value: const dep = Math.max(20, Math.round(total * 0.15)); use it in the deposit-line, CTA, and total subtitle. Pin minimums per tier (kids: $20, color refresh: $25, knotless: $40) via a DEPOSIT_FLOOR map keyed by styleType.

### 127. 'Open today' status pill is not a link to hours or directions

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Hero strip > 'Harlem · open today' indicator with green dot
- **What breaks:** The 'Harlem · open today' indicator visually reads like an interactive status chip (dot + text), but it has no link to today's hours, a map, or directions. A first-time visitor checking 'are they really open?' has nowhere to tap.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the 'Harlem · open today' chip a <button> that opens a small popover showing today's hours + a Maps link ('2510 Lenox Ave · Open in Maps'). Anchor the popover to the chip; reuse the .scrim+.sheet half-sheet pattern at smaller scale.

### 128. No way to bookmark a look without committing to booking

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Gallery cards > no save/heart/wishlist control
- **What breaks:** Tapping any gallery card opens the full 8-step booking sheet. There is no heart, save, or share affordance — a client browsing on lunch break has no way to mark a few looks to come back to later, short of screenshotting.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a heart icon in the .style-meta header row (top-right of the meta panel). Tap toggles a 'saved' state stored in localStorage.saved=[idx,...]. Show a new filter pill 'Saved (n)' at the start of the filter bar when count > 0.

### 129. Mobile drag handle is decorative — drawer can't be swipe-dismissed

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sheet handle (mobile only, top of drawer)
- **What breaks:** On mobile the .sheet-handle pill renders at the top of the drawer, mimicking iOS bottom sheets — but no touchstart/touchmove handler is wired. Users instinctively try to drag it down to dismiss; nothing happens.
- **Proposed fix:** Wire touchstart/touchmove/touchend on .sheet-handle: track deltaY; if drag > 80px down or velocity > .5 on release, call closeBook(); otherwise spring back. Use the same unsaved-changes guard from #9.

### 130. 'Any chair' tile gives no slot adjustment cue

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 2

- **What breaks:** Picking 'Any chair · First open' should logically open up additional time slots (more chairs available), but Step 7 'Pick a slot' shows the exact same six fixed slots. The 'First open' promise is empty.

  - *New copy:* "Slots widen with Any chair"

### 131. Running total displays a service's base $310 with a stale duration

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky bottom > running total ($310 · 6 hrs)
- **What breaks:** On initial render before openBook() runs (or for the brief moment between renders), the total is hard-coded to '$310 · 6 hrs' in the markup — which matches Honey Ombré, not Cherry Cola (the first gallery card, which opens with idx=0 = $280). A screen reader user or someone with slow JS sees the wrong number for a fraction of a second.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the hard-coded '$310 · 6 hrs' in markup with empty placeholders: <span class='total' id='bkTotal'>—</span>. Render only after openBook fires. Add a CSS rule .sheet:not(.show) .sh-foot{display:none} so the footer never shows pre-init.

### 132. Gallery tags use four different visual styles for similar metadata

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 2

Three of the four communicate the same kind of thing (a category callout) but use unrelated colors, so the visual system reads as decorative rather than meaningful. A user can't tell what makes 'Color' tag-worthy when most color styles in the grid have no tag.

Replace .tag.new/.tag.fave with .tag.tag--new / .tag.tag--loved that share the visual treatment and only differ by dot color (ochre / birthday). Drop the 'Color' and 'Kids' inline category tags from cards — those are filter pills, not card tags.

### 133. Large braid size is cheaper than Medium — undisclosed why

- **What breaks:** Going larger drops $15 from the price, but there's no microcopy explaining (e.g. 'fewer braids = less time'). A client reading 'Large −$15' without context wonders if Large is a lower tier or a promo, eroding trust in the pricing logic.

### 134. Color upcharge prices appear inside the label text — no consistent price slot

### 135. Hero strip lacks the visual hierarchy of trust-builders

'Open today' is a key trust signal (vs Boulevard, which hides hours) but blends into the row as a tiny dot. The information is there but reads as decorative chrome.

Each micro-card is tappable: location → map, photos → gallery, text → sms link.

### 136. Free-form notes field has no character guide or examples

### 137. 'Any chair' tile sits alongside named stylists with no visual differentiation

It should either be visually separated (e.g. a small divider, or a different background) or moved out of the grid entirely as a fallback.

### 138. Sheet renders em-dash placeholders before openBook fires

### 139. Total + duration in markup is stale before openBook runs

### 140. CTA #bkCta has a :disabled style but is never disabled

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **What breaks:** CSS defines .cta:disabled{opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed}, signaling there should be a disabled state — but the JS never adds the disabled attribute even when contact inputs are blank or no slot is picked. The styled state is dead code.

Call this check at the end of refreshTotal() and oninput on form fields. Add a 12px ochre helper line under the disabled CTA: 'Pick a slot and add your number to hold the chair'.

### 141. Toast can't be dismissed and blocks repeat-booking feedback

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > toast '#toast' lifecycle
- **What breaks:** Toast has pointer-events:none, no click-to-dismiss, no swipe. Auto-hides after 3000 ms via setTimeout. If the user taps Confirm twice (or another booking flow shows a different toast), the message just gets overwritten with no visual hand-off.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #29, the toast is replaced by the confirmation screen. Keep a separate toast pattern only for low-stakes events (e.g. 'Saved · added to your looks'). For that, add pointer-events:auto, onclick=t.classList.remove('show'), and a 12px '×' on the right edge. Stack toasts with a queue rather than overwriting.

### 142. Card hover lift is mouse-only — no tap feedback on touch

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Gallery > style card hover state (transform: translateY)
- **What breaks:** Style cards rely on :hover for the lift + shadow. On touch devices there is no :active state defined, so tapping a card gives zero visual feedback until the sheet starts to slide in (which is ~350 ms later). Easy to double-tap.
- **Proposed fix:** Add .style:active{transform:scale(.985);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px var(--clay-soft)} so touch users see a tap-down. Also add CSS @media (hover:none){.style:hover{transform:none}} to skip the hover lift on touch devices.

### 143. Swatch label uses <br> tag — breaks screen-reader parsing

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 Color > swatch labels using <br> for prices ('Honey ombré<br>+$20')
- **What breaks:** Each swatch label crams the color name + upcharge into one .lab div separated by <br>. Screen readers may read 'Honey ombré plus twenty dollars' as a single run or split it awkwardly; no aria-label distinguishing the name from the price.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #25/#57/#99: drop <br>, render two <span> children with aria-label='{Name}, {price or no charge}' on the parent button. Screen readers announce one clean string.

### 144. Brand link wraps mixed text in an italic <em> for styling, not semantics

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Top nav > '.brand' wordmark with <em>
- **What breaks:** <em> is used purely as a typography hook for the 'Beauty Bar' subtitle — screen readers add emphasis where none was intended. Should be a <span class='subtitle'> instead.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace <em> with <span class='brand-sub'>. Move the italic styling to .brand-sub CSS rule. Visual is identical; screen readers no longer add emphasis to 'Beauty Bar'.

### 145. pickStyl receives idx parameter but discards it

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > pickStyl signature
- **What breaks:** pickStyl(el, idx) declares idx but the function body never reads it. Dead parameter — and the bug it causes (selection not stored, see flag above) means the API itself is broken, not just unused. Reviewer/code-handover will be confused.
- **Proposed fix:** Same as #5/#69: use idx to write cur.styl=idx and update header. The parameter becomes load-bearing once the bug is fixed.

### 146. Filter bar overlaps content under iOS notch / dynamic toolbar

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Sticky filter bar (.fbar) > top:54px stacking
- **What breaks:** Filter bar is hard-pinned to top:54px under a sticky nav that's also sticky. On iOS Safari with the dynamic toolbar appearing, this stacks awkwardly; no env(safe-area-inset-top) handling.
- **Proposed fix:** Change .fbar top:54px to top:env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px) + 54px via calc(). Add padding-top:env(safe-area-inset-top) to .nav. Test against iOS Safari with the dynamic toolbar visible.

### 147. Sheet uses <aside> but contains the entire primary booking flow

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > #sheet aside element
- **What breaks:** <aside> is for tangential content. The booking sheet is the entire conversion flow — should be a <dialog> or at least a <section>. Screen readers treating the sheet as supplementary will deprioritize navigation to it.
- **Proposed fix:** Change <aside id='sheet'> to <dialog id='sheet'> (or <section role='dialog'>). Use the native <dialog> element if browser support is acceptable — gets focus management and Escape handling free.

### 148. Two Sat Nov 8 slots collapse to identical-looking tiles

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 7 slots > Sat Nov 8 (default) duplicate dates
- **What breaks:** The Sat Nov 8 11:00a and Sat Nov 8 2:00p tiles share the same .d 'Sat Nov 8' header and differ only in the small subtitle. The visual hierarchy reverses what matters (the day is loud, the time is whisper) — easy to mis-tap when scanning.
- **Proposed fix:** Swap the visual weight: make .slot .t the bold Fraunces line ('11:00 am') and .slot .d the supporting small line ('Sat · 6 hrs'). For multiple-slot-per-day, group under a single date heading with each time as a child chip (visual grouping > duplication).

### 149. Active filter pill highlight doesn't persist via aria-pressed

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 3

- **Location:** Filter pills > .fbar > pill 'All looks' active state
- **What breaks:** Active pill uses .pill.on but no aria-pressed='true' / 'false' state. Screen readers announce each as a plain button — no indication which filter is currently 'on' or that they're a toggle group.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-pressed='true|false' to each pill, sync in filt(). Wrap the filter row in role='toolbar' aria-label='Filter looks by category'.

### 150. Every slot redundantly repeats the duration

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 7 'Pick a slot' grid > all six slots show '· 6 hrs'
- **What breaks:** Every single slot card shows the same '6 hrs' badge already visible in the hero badge and running total. The repetition wastes scarce drawer width and adds noise where the most useful detail (stylist availability, soonest open) is missing.
- **Proposed fix:** Drop '· 6 hrs' from every slot tile. Duration is already in the hero badge and running total. Replace with chair availability marker ('Aminata' or 'Any open chair') — the missing signal from #47.
  - *New copy:* "{time} · {chair-availability}"

### 151. Filter pill counts don't sum to 121

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Sticky filter bar > category counts (34, 22, 14, 11, 9, 8, 23) vs 'All looks 121'
- **What breaks:** 34+22+14+11+9+8+23 = 121 by coincidence with overlap implicit, but with no styles assignable to multiple categories the math reads as either dishonest accounting or an arbitrary number. Either way, the precision invites scrutiny that doesn't pay off.
- **Proposed fix:** Drop the precise counts from secondary pills. Keep 'All looks · 121' (the only truthful number), strip counts from category pills. If a count is shown, it must match the filter's actual result.
  - *New copy:* "All looks · 121 / Knotless / Box braids / Fulani / Silk press / Natural set / Kids / Color & gloss"

### 152. Primary CTA uses clay, but hero/gallery emphasize ochre — split brand voice

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > 'Hold the chair · pay $40 deposit ›' CTA color (--clay #A8623C)
- **What breaks:** The hero h1 italic emphasis, brand wordmark accent, and step hints all use --ochre (#C2912F). The single primary CTA pivots to --clay (#A8623C). Without a clear hierarchy rule for when each is used, the booking sheet feels like a different brand than the gallery that led into it.
- **Proposed fix:** Establish a rule: clay = commit / commercial actions (Hold the chair, pay deposit). Ochre = brand flourishes (h1 emphasis, brand-sub, step-hints). Document this in CLAUDE.md brand-tokens section. Keep the CTA clay (correct usage per the rule).

### 153. Only included add-on uses teal accent — color leaks from nowhere

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 'Add-ons' > 'Wash & deep condition' priced 'Included' in teal
- **What breaks:** --teal (#4E7E76) appears exactly twice on the entire page: the 'open today' status dot and the 'Included' label. The two uses share no semantic meaning yet share a unique color. The teal feels arbitrary and creates a phantom relationship between the strip and the addon row.
- **Proposed fix:** Either: (a) extend teal to a semantic 'included / safe / free' family (use it consistently across the artifact for 'no charge' moments — Natural swatch's 'Included' tag, Wash row, etc.), or (b) drop teal from the addon and use --espresso-soft italic 'Included' instead. Recommendation: (a) — semantic teal for no-charge wins.

### 154. Natural color swatch is near-black — hard to see on cream background

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 3

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 'Color' > swatches > 'Natural' first swatch sw circle
- **What breaks:** The Natural gradient (#2c1810 → #0a0604) becomes a near-black dot with only a 2px clay ring to mark selection. The contrast against the cream (.swatch-i.on) background is heavy, and against unselected state it visually dominates as the only 'option' worth noticing.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace the near-black gradient with a softer espresso-to-warm-brown (#3a261a → #5C4B3E) so it reads as 'natural hair tone' rather than ink. Add a subtle 1px line-soft ring on every swatch (not just .on) so unselected swatches have edges on cream.

### 155. cur.size/len/part/col reset before DOM toggle — state vs UI drift on rapid reopens

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > openBook() function > resetSelections() vs cur state
- **What breaks:** openBook() assigns cur.size='m', cur.len='wst', etc., but if a previous open's state still has a different stylist or addon set, the addons Set is reset to ['wash'] only inside resetSelections — meanwhile cur.idx is set before resetSelections runs. If openBook is called twice in a row without the user touching anything, the second call wipes prior selections without warning, contradicting issue 86's scope (this is about state, not scroll).
- **Proposed fix:** Reorder openBook() so resetSelections() runs FIRST (resets DOM + cur), then cur.idx = idx, then style-specific overrides (style's preferred color/length/styl). Race conditions disappear because state and DOM are reset atomically before style-specific writes.

### 156. Slot picker writes cur.slot but does not call refreshTotal

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > pickSlot() function body
- **What breaks:** pick(), pickSw(), and toggle() all call refreshTotal(), but pickSlot() does not. If the running total ever included a time-of-day surcharge (e.g. weekend premium), changing the slot would silently fail to update the total. The function is structurally inconsistent with its peers.
- **Proposed fix:** Add refreshTotal() at the end of pickSlot(). Even if no surcharge today, the function structurally matches its peers and will pick up future surcharges (weekend premium, popular-time pricing).

### 157. Decorative chat-bubble SVG has no aria-hidden or role

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Top nav > Need help? Text us pill > SVG icon
- **What breaks:** The inline SVG inside the Text us pill has no aria-hidden='true' and no <title>. Screen readers may announce 'image' or attempt to read the path data, polluting the 'Need help? Text us' label.
- **Proposed fix:** Add aria-hidden='true' focusable='false' to the inline SVG inside .text-us. The pill's accessible name comes from the visible text 'Need help? Text us'.

### 158. Title italicizes only the LAST word, not the matching segment from gallery cards

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > openBook(idx) > italicization of style title
- **What breaks:** Gallery cards italicize a specific phrase like 'with curls', 'Twist Out', or 'Box Braids' — multi-word italics. openBook() splits on space and italicizes everything after the first word, so 'Cherry Cola Knotless' renders as 'Cherry [Cola Knotless]', whereas the gallery card shows it as 'Cherry Cola [Knotless]'. Style title formatting drifts between gallery and sheet.
- **Proposed fix:** Store the italicized segment on each STYLES entry: e.g. {n:'Cherry Cola Knotless', italic:'Knotless'}. openBook() builds the title as s.n.replace(s.italic, `<em>${s.italic}</em>`). Now gallery card and sheet header italicize the same phrase.

### 159. Sticky footer order (total, deposit copy, CTA) buries the deposit policy between price and action

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky footer > deposit line + CTA + total row > visual order
- **What breaks:** The 11px italic deposit-line sits sandwiched between the running total and the primary CTA. Users scanning vertically (price → big button) physically skip past 'cancel free up to 48 hr before' — the only refund policy on the page.
- **Proposed fix:** Reorder: (1) total row, (2) primary CTA, (3) deposit + policy line below CTA at slightly larger 12.5px. Bringing policy below the CTA matches commerce patterns and puts it in the conversion's natural reading flow.

### 160. Running total uses <small> for duration — inverts semantic meaning

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > total bkTotal > <small> element used for duration
- **What breaks:** '$310<small>· 6 hrs</small>' uses <small> to mean visually-smaller, but <small> is semantically 'side comment' / fine print. Duration is not a legal disclaimer. Screen readers may de-emphasize it. Should be a sibling span with a CSS class.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace <small> with <span class='dur-meta'>. CSS keeps the visual treatment. <small> is reserved for legal disclaimers.

### 161. Footer's tel: link has no visible label as a phone call action

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Footer > <a href='tel:+16465550100'> phone number link
- **What breaks:** The '(646) 555-0100' text is wrapped in a tel: link but renders identically to the '@jolieden' link beside it (same color, no underline) — users cannot tell which one is callable. The link also has no aria-label distinguishing 'Call salon' from 'Open Instagram'.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a small phone icon before the tel: link and an Instagram glyph before the @jolieden link. Add aria-label='Call salon · (646) 555-0100' and aria-label='Open Jolieden on Instagram'. Underline tel: links on hover.
  - *New copy:* "📞 (646) 555-0100 · IG @jolieden"

### 162. Smaller braid sizes cost more — but the inverse jump from Medium to Small (+$20) is half of Small to XS (+$20 → +$40)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 1 'Size of braid' chip 'XS' priced +$40 vs Step 1 'Large' priced -$15
- **What breaks:** Pricing jumps: L (-$15), M (0), S (+$20), XS (+$40). The XS-to-Small delta is $20, but Small-to-Medium is also $20, and Medium-to-Large drops $15 — non-linear with no copy explaining it. Clients can't anticipate the upcharge.
- **Proposed fix:** Same fix as #56: one italic helper line under size chips explaining the rationale. Optionally smooth to linear deltas: L -$15, M $0, S +$15, XS +$30.

### 163. Platinum lab gradient is pale cream — illegible on the cream sheet background

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 Color swatch > 'Platinum' +$45 swatch (.lab 'Platinum<br>+$45')
- **What breaks:** Platinum's swatch gradient runs #e5dac4 → #9a8a6c. The sheet background is --cream #FBF7EF. The lightest stop is nearly indistinguishable from the page bg, making the Platinum choice hard to spot. Mirrors issue 117's 'Natural is near-black' on cream — both extremes fail visually.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a 1.5px line-soft ring to every swatch (not just .on) so pale tones stay visible on cream. For platinum, deepen the second gradient stop to #6a5a44 so contrast holds.

### 164. Nav uses backdrop-filter — degrades to a transparent strip on browsers that don't support it

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Top nav > .nav background rgba(251,247,239,.95) + backdrop-filter:blur(10px)
- **What breaks:** On Firefox versions without backdrop-filter support (or with it disabled for privacy), the nav has a 95% opaque cream background that lets the body content show through. The sticky filter bar below uses the same pattern — text underneath bleeds through when scrolling.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap backdrop-filter rules in @supports (backdrop-filter:blur(10px)){...}. Default fallback: solid var(--bg) background, no blur. Same fix for .fbar.

### 165. Sheet handle is a div, not a draggable surface — touch users may try to grab it

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > #sheet > sheet-handle div on mobile
- **What breaks:** The 42x4px drag handle indicator appears only on mobile, signaling 'I can be dragged', but it's purely cosmetic. Touch users following the visual affordance try to grab and drag — nothing happens. Either implement the gesture or hide the handle.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #44: wire touch handlers for swipe-down dismiss. Pair with cursor:grab/grabbing styling on hover.

### 166. Sheet's h2 is not connected to the aside via aria-labelledby

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky header > h2#bkTitle and #bkStyl wrapped in <div> with no aria-labelledby
- **What breaks:** The <aside id='sheet'> contains an h2 but has no aria-labelledby='bkTitle' or role='dialog'. Screen readers cannot announce the sheet's purpose when it opens — see issue 24, but specifically the labelledby pointer is missing too.
- **Proposed fix:** Set aria-labelledby='bkTitle' on the <dialog>/role='dialog' element (per #89). Add aria-describedby='bkStyl' so the stylist line is announced as the dialog's description.

### 167. Add-on row uses onclick='toggle(this)' on outer container — child .a-desc text isn't a separate target

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 5 add-ons rows > onclick on outer div, no event delegation
- **What breaks:** Clicking the description text 'Always included — keeps the scalp happy' inside the wash row toggles the wash add-on (because the click bubbles to the wrapping <div>). This actually demonstrates issue 67 but specifically: text selection / triple-click highlighting also triggers the toggle.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #98+#124: when row becomes a <button>, browsers handle text selection inside button as part of the button (no separate target). For triple-click drag, add user-select:none to .a-desc inside buttons.

### 168. Default Medium chip has no price chip — implies Medium is the 'free' baseline, but XS / S / L all charge from it

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 1 chip 'Medium' label
- **What breaks:** The chip reads just 'Medium' with no .px price. XS / S / L all show a delta. This implies Medium is the standard. But the running total starts at $310 with Medium pre-selected, so users who downgrade to Large then back to Medium see a price bump from $295 → $310 with no chip indicator saying '+$15 vs Large'. Reference-point pricing is opaque.
- **Proposed fix:** Add an explicit '$0' chip indicator on Medium (or replace with a small 'Baseline' Fraunces italic eyebrow). The visual rule is: every chip declares its price relationship to baseline, baseline declares itself as such.
  - *New copy:* "Medium · Baseline"

### 169. Replacing className wipes any future state classes (e.g. loading, error)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > #bkPhoto > className update in openBook (`photo.className = 'style-hero ' + s.photo`)
- **What breaks:** openBook() does `photo.className = 'style-hero ' + s.photo;` — clobbering all prior classes. If a future addition adds `.loading` while a CDN image streams in, every openBook call would wipe it. The pattern should use classList.remove(prev-g) + classList.add(new-g). Brittle for future maintenance.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace `photo.className = 'style-hero ' + s.photo` with photo.classList.remove(...Array.from(photo.classList).filter(c=>c.startsWith('g-'))); photo.classList.add(s.photo). Preserves any non-photo classes for future loading / error states.

### 170. No lang='fr' on French/Wolof names — extends issue 63 to the booking sheet specifically (stylist roster, persona name in Step 8)

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Page > <html lang='en'> + booking sheet content includes French personas (Diéssou, Aminata D., Ndeye F.)
- **What breaks:** Step 8's pre-filled 'Amara Niang' and Step 6's 'Aminata D., Mariama B., Zainab O., Ndeye F., Khady N.' all sit inside an English root. Issue 63 noted this for gallery only — here it propagates into form-filled values and the sticky stylist line.
- **Proposed fix:** Apply the lang='fr' wrap inside openBook()'s render of #bkStyl and the dynamic stylist tiles. Update the form prefill 'Imani Webb' (per #26) — Imani is Swahili/Arabic, lang='en' is fine; but flag any French/Wolof prefill (Amara Niang would need lang='wo' or 'fr').

### 171. Single-chevron '›' inside CTA reads as plain text to screen readers ('right single angle quotation mark')

**⚪ LOW** · `NAV` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > sticky footer > .cta button > '›' character at end
- **What breaks:** The 'Hold the chair · pay $40 deposit ›' button ends with a literal › character. Screen readers announce 'right single angle quotation mark' or similar after the action verb. Should be an aria-hidden span or a real SVG arrow.
- **Proposed fix:** Wrap the › in <span aria-hidden='true'>. Or replace with a small inline SVG arrow with aria-hidden='true' focusable='false' for higher visual quality.

### 172. Stylist tile contents misaligned by mixed flex direction

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 6 'Your chair' > stylist tile inner layout
- **What breaks:** The .styl button is flex-direction:column with align-items:center, but the second child is a div wrapping name + role. The single avatar plus stacked name/role read as three rows but the role line ends up cramped under the name with no breathing space — visually unbalanced compared to the avatar.
- **Proposed fix:** Restructure .styl as a 2-row layout: avatar row (centered) + name+role stacked with 2px gap between. Add explicit margin between .styl-name and .styl-role (margin-top:2px) so the role doesn't crowd the name.

### 173. 'First swatch is no charge' contradicts visible '+$0' absence on Natural

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 'Color' > step-hint 'First swatch is no charge'
- **What breaks:** Natural swatch has no price chip while every other swatch shows '+$X' via <br>. New users have to deduce that no price means free; the hint sits 60px away in a different color scheme.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #18+#52+#155: the hint becomes style-specific ('Honey ombré is included with this look'). Natural shows 'Included' label explicitly (per #25), so the +$0 absence becomes an explicit 'Included' instead.
  - *New copy:* "{photo's color} is included — switch swatches to remix"

### 174. Color swatches are ordered by price, hiding popular options behind cost

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 4 'Color' > swatch order vs frequency
- **What breaks:** Swatches go strictly Natural -> Honey -> Cinnamon -> Cherry -> Lavender -> Platinum (cheapest to priciest). 'Cherry Cola' is the first gallery card but appears 4th in the picker. There is no 'popular' or 'trending' grouping that matches the gallery's editorial voice.
- **Proposed fix:** Reorder swatches by editorial relevance: 1. Natural (default), 2. The photo's color (preselected and free), 3. Honey, 4. Cinnamon, 5. Cherry, 6. Lavender, 7. Platinum. Move popular over precious. Replace the strict cheapest-first sort.

### 175. H1 italic spans 'do the rest' across two visual lines awkwardly

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Hero > 'Tap a look. We'll do the rest.' h1
- **What breaks:** The italic <em>do the rest.</em> wraps across lines depending on viewport width (max-width:14ch). At certain widths it splits as 'do the' / 'rest.' — italic orphan word at start of line two reads as a typo.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace <em>do the rest.</em> with <em>do the rest.</em> wrapped in <span style='white-space:nowrap'> at break-points. Or shorten copy: 'Tap a look. <em>We'll take it from there.</em>' which wraps more cleanly.
  - *New copy:* "Tap a look. We'll take it from there."

### 176. Footer collapses to misaligned single column on mid-width screens

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Footer > foot-row layout
- **What breaks:** .foot-row uses flex-wrap with no responsive breakpoint. Between ~600-800px the two children wrap but inherit different widths, creating jagged left edges. Address and phone end up left-aligned together but with the address truncated mid-word on narrow tablets.
- **Proposed fix:** Add explicit breakpoint at 768px: .foot-row{flex-direction:column; align-items:flex-start; gap:12px} below 768px. Above, keep flex-row but add justify-content:space-between with min-width:0 on children to prevent jagged truncation.

### 177. Hero strip dot separators conflict with hero-strip 'dot' indicator

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Hero strip > '·' separator usage
- **What breaks:** Hero strip uses both a green status dot (Harlem · open today) AND interpunct separators within phrases. Visual rhythm is ambiguous — is the dot a bullet, a status, or a divider? Three 'd' items with one having an extra visual element creates inconsistency.
- **Proposed fix:** Per #58: replace the flat row with 3 micro-cards (icon + label + detail). The status dot becomes a colored dot inside the location card only — no other dots elsewhere, so the green dot's meaning is unambiguous.

### 178. Pre-filled name is editable but no clear 'this is a demo' affordance

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 8 input value='Amara' / 'Niang'
- **What breaks:** Inputs are fully editable with realistic Amara Niang values. A reviewer trying the flow may not realize the field is pre-filled vs auto-detected from their session, especially since the placeholder text is replaced by the value. There's no muted styling or 'demo' hint.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a small persona chip above Step 8: 'Demo as · Imani Webb (cold-start)' with a chip to switch personas (Imani / Aaliyah / Naomi — matching CLAUDE.md cast). Persona chip changes prefill values across the form, surfacing the demo's persona-aware narrative.

### 179. 'Free-form' as default parting + 'no charge' isn't communicated

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > Step 3 'Parting' chip 'Free-form'
- **What breaks:** Step 3 shows Free-form (preselected), Middle, Side, Zig-zag +$10. Three of four options have no price chip, but only Zig-zag charges. No visual cue that 'no chip = no charge' — first-time users may think Middle is implicitly priced.
- **Proposed fix:** Add explicit '+$0' or 'Included' chip to Free-form, Middle, Side. Keep '+$10' on Zig-zag. Now every chip explicitly declares its price relationship — no implicit knowledge required.
  - *New copy:* "Free-form · Included / Middle · Included / Side · Included / Zig-zag · +$10"

### 180. Stylist-name + stylist-role merge visually due to identical width column

**⚪ LOW** · `DESIGN` · round 4

- **Location:** Booking sheet > #stepStylist > stylist-name vs stylist-role typographic gap
- **What breaks:** styl-name (11.5px, 600 weight) and styl-role (9.5px, regular) sit in same column with no margin between. The 2px line-height inheritance from .styl flex column gap (6px applies between av and div, not within div) makes name and role almost touch — looks like one wrapped string.
- **Proposed fix:** Add margin-top:3px to .styl-role and gap:1px to the inner div containing both. Bump .styl-role to 10.5px (from 9.5px) so the size difference between name and role reads as intentional, not crowded.
